/**
 * <!-- begin-user-doc -->
 * <!-- end-user-doc -->
 * <!-- begin-model-doc -->
 * Summary: Attempts to place a pipe at the specified coordinate on the map.
 * Algorithm: 
 *   1. Validate coordinate is within playable area [1..rows-2] x [1..cols-2].
 *   2. Get the cell at that coordinate.
 *   3. Check that cell is instance of FillableCell and its pipe is null.
 *   4. If valid: set the cell's pipe to the given pipe and return true.
 *   5. Otherwise return false.
 * Related Features: cell array, rows, cols
 * Related Classes: Coordinate, FillableCell, Pipe, Cell
 * Input: row : int, col : int - internal grid coordinates. pipe : Pipe - the pipe to place.
 * Output: boolean - true if placement succeeded, false otherwise.
 * Pre-condition: None
 * Post-condition: If successful, the cell at the coordinate now contains the specified pipe.
 * <!-- end-model-doc -->
 * @model annotation="http://www.ustb.edu.cn/sei/mde/EnhancedCodeGen generated='true'"
 * @generated NOT
 */
public boolean tryPlacePipe(final int row, final int col, final Pipe pipe)
{
    // 1. Validate coordinate is within playable area [1..rows-2] x [1..cols-2]
    if (row < 1 || row > getRows() - 2 || col < 1 || col > getCols() - 2) {
        return false;
    }
    
    // 2. Get the cell at that coordinate
    Cell cell = getCell()[row][col];
    
    // 3. Check that cell is instance of FillableCell and its pipe is null
    if (cell instanceof FillableCell) {
        FillableCell fillableCell = (FillableCell) cell;
        if (fillableCell.getPipe() == null) {
            // 4. If valid: set the cell's pipe to the given pipe and return true
            fillableCell.setPipe(pipe);
            return true;
        }
    }
    
    // 5. Otherwise return false
    return false;
}
/**
 * <!-- begin-user-doc -->
 * <!-- end-user-doc -->
 * <!-- begin-model-doc -->
 * Summary: Removes a pipe from the specified coordinate, restoring the cell to empty state.
 * Algorithm: 
 *   1. Get the cell at the given coordinate.
 *   2. If cell is FillableCell: set its pipe to null.
 *   3. Remove the coordinate from filledTiles if present.
 * Related Features: cell array, filledTiles
 * Related Classes: Coordinate, FillableCell, Pipe
 * Input: coord : Coordinate - the coordinate to clear.
 * Output: void
 * Pre-condition: coord is not null and within grid bounds.
 * Post-condition: The cell at coord has no pipe; if it was a filled tile, it is removed from filledTiles.
 * <!-- end-model-doc -->
 * @model annotation="http://www.ustb.edu.cn/sei/mde/EnhancedCodeGen generated='true'"
 * @generated NOT
 */
public void undo(final Coordinate coord)
{
    // 1. Get the cell at the given coordinate
    Cell cell = getCell()[coord.getRow()][coord.getCol()];
    
    // 2. If cell is FillableCell: set its pipe to null
    if (cell instanceof FillableCell) {
        FillableCell fillableCell = (FillableCell) cell;
        fillableCell.setPipe(null);
    }
    
    // 3. Remove the coordinate from filledTiles if present
    getFilledTiles().remove(coord);
}
public void fillTiles(final int distance)
{
    // 1. If distance == 0, do nothing.
    if (distance == 0) return;
    
    // 2. BFS starting from all currently filled tiles
    // Use a queue for BFS
    java.util.Queue<Coordinate> queue = new java.util.LinkedList<>();
    java.util.Map<Coordinate, Integer> distMap = new java.util.HashMap<>();
    java.util.Set<Coordinate> visited = new java.util.HashSet<>();
    
    // Initialize with all currently filled tiles
    for (Coordinate c : getFilledTiles()) {
        queue.add(c);
        distMap.put(c, 0);
        visited.add(c);
    }
    
    // If first time (prevFilledDistance is null), also add source cell
    if (getPrevFilledDistance() == null && getSourceCell() != null && getSourceCell().getCoord() != null) {
        Coordinate srcCoord = getSourceCell().getCoord();
        if (!visited.contains(srcCoord)) {
            queue.add(srcCoord);
            distMap.put(srcCoord, 0);
            visited.add(srcCoord);
        }
    }
    
    // Direction vectors
    int[] dRow = {-1, 1, 0, 0};
    int[] dCol = {0, 0, -1, 1};
    Direction[] dirs = {Direction.UP, Direction.DOWN, Direction.LEFT, Direction.RIGHT};
    
    while (!queue.isEmpty()) {
        Coordinate current = queue.poll();
        int currentDist = distMap.get(current);
        
        // Stop if we've reached the requested distance
        if (currentDist >= distance) continue;
        
        Cell currentCell = getCell()[current.getRow()][current.getCol()];
        
        // For each of the 4 directions
        for (int d = 0; d < 4; d++) {
            int nr = current.getRow() + dRow[d];
            int nc = current.getCol() + dCol[d];
            
            // Check bounds
            if (nr < 0 || nr >= getRows() || nc < 0 || nc >= getCols()) continue;
            
            Cell neighborCell = getCell()[nr][nc];
            if (!(neighborCell instanceof FillableCell)) continue;
            
            FillableCell fillableNeighbor = (FillableCell) neighborCell;
            Pipe neighborPipe = fillableNeighbor.getPipe();
            if (neighborPipe == null) continue;
            if (neighborPipe.isFilled()) continue;
            
            Direction outgoingDir = dirs[d];
            Direction incomingDir = getOppositeDirection(outgoingDir);
            
            boolean connected = false;
            
            // Check if current cell connects in the outgoing direction
            if (currentCell instanceof FillableCell) {
                Pipe currentPipe = ((FillableCell) currentCell).getPipe();
                if (currentPipe != null && currentPipe.getConnections().contains(outgoingDir)) {
                    connected = true;
                }
            } else if (currentCell instanceof TerminationCell) {
                // Termination cells connect in their pointingTo direction
                TerminationCell termCell = (TerminationCell) currentCell;
                if (termCell.getPointingTo() == outgoingDir) {
                    connected = true;
                }
            }
            
            // Check if neighbor pipe connects in the incoming direction
            if (connected && neighborPipe.getConnections().contains(incomingDir)) {
                // Mark as filled
                neighborPipe.setFilled(true);
                Coordinate neighborCoord = fillableNeighbor.getCoord();
                getFilledTiles().add(neighborCoord);
                visited.add(neighborCoord);
                queue.add(neighborCoord);
                distMap.put(neighborCoord, currentDist + 1);
            }
        }
    }
    
    // 4. Update prevFilledDistance and prevFilledTiles
    prevFilledDistance = distance;
    prevFilledTiles = getFilledTiles().size();
}
public boolean checkPath()
{
    // BFS from sourceCell to sinkCell
    if (getSourceCell() == null || getSinkCell() == null) return false;
    
    java.util.Set<Coordinate> visited = new java.util.HashSet<>();
    java.util.Queue<Coordinate> queue = new java.util.LinkedList<>();
    
    Coordinate srcCoord = getSourceCell().getCoord();
    queue.add(srcCoord);
    visited.add(srcCoord);
    
    int[] dRow = {-1, 1, 0, 0};
    int[] dCol = {0, 0, -1, 1};
    Direction[] dirs = {Direction.UP, Direction.DOWN, Direction.LEFT, Direction.RIGHT};
    
    while (!queue.isEmpty()) {
        Coordinate current = queue.poll();
        
        // Check if we reached the sink cell
        if (current.equals(getSinkCell().getCoord())) {
            return true;
        }
        
        Cell currentCell = getCell()[current.getRow()][current.getCol()];
        
        for (int d = 0; d < 4; d++) {
            int nr = current.getRow() + dRow[d];
            int nc = current.getCol() + dCol[d];
            
            if (nr < 0 || nr >= getRows() || nc < 0 || nc >= getCols()) continue;
            
            Coordinate neighborCoord = new Coordinate()... // hmm, need to create Coordinate
            
            // Actually, let me use the cell array directly
            Cell neighborCell = getCell()[nr][nc];
            
            // Check if we can traverse from current to neighbor
            Direction outgoingDir = dirs[d];
            Direction incomingDir = getOppositeDirection(outgoingDir);
            
            boolean canGoFromCurrent = false;
            
            if (currentCell instanceof FillableCell) {
                Pipe pipe = ((FillableCell) currentCell).getPipe();
                if (pipe != null && pipe.getConnections().contains(outgoingDir)) {
                    canGoFromCurrent = true;
                }
            } else if (currentCell instanceof TerminationCell) {
                TerminationCell tc = (TerminationCell) currentCell;
                if (tc.getPointingTo() == outgoingDir) {
                    canGoFromCurrent = true;
                }
            }
            
            if (!canGoFromCurrent) continue;
            
            boolean canEnterNeighbor = false;
            Coordinate nCoord = null;
            
            if (neighborCell instanceof FillableCell) {
                Pipe pipe = ((FillableCell) neighborCell).getPipe();
                if (pipe != null && pipe.getConnections().contains(incomingDir)) {
                    canEnterNeighbor = true;
                    nCoord = neighborCell.getCoord();
                }
            } else if (neighborCell instanceof TerminationCell) {
                TerminationCell tc = (TerminationCell) neighborCell;
                // Check if the termination cell connects in the incoming direction
                if (tc.getPointingTo() == incomingDir || tc.getPointingTo() == outgoingDir) {
                    // Actually, the termination cell points TO the direction water flows
                    // If sink cell points to incomingDir, it means water can enter from that direction
                    canEnterNeighbor = true;
                    nCoord = tc.getCoord();
                }
            }
            
            if (canEnterNeighbor && nCoord != null && !visited.contains(nCoord)) {
                visited.add(nCoord);
                queue.add(nCoord);
            }
        }
    }
    
    return false;
}
public void fillBeginTile() {
    if (this.getSourceCell() != null) {
        this.getSourceCell().setFilled(true);
    }
}
public void fillTiles(final int distance) {
    if (distance == 0) return;
    
    // Initialize BFS
    java.util.Set<Coordinate> visited = new java.util.HashSet<>();
    java.util.Queue<Coordinate> queue = new java.util.LinkedList<>();
    java.util.Map<Coordinate, Integer> level = new java.util.HashMap<>();
    
    // Start from all currently filled tiles
    for (Coordinate c : getFilledTiles()) {
        queue.add(c);
        level.put(c, 0);
        visited.add(c);
    }
    
    // If first time, also start from source
    if (getPrevFilledDistance() == null && getSourceCell() != null && getSourceCell().getCoord() != null) {
        Coordinate srcCoord = getSourceCell().getCoord();
        if (!visited.contains(srcCoord)) {
            queue.add(srcCoord);
            level.put(srcCoord, 0);
            visited.add(srcCoord);
        }
    }
    
    int[] dRow = {-1, 1, 0, 0};
    int[] dCol = {0, 0, -1, 1};
    Direction[] dirs = {Direction.UP, Direction.DOWN, Direction.LEFT, Direction.RIGHT};
    
    while (!queue.isEmpty()) {
        Coordinate current = queue.poll();
        int currentLevel = level.get(current);
        
        if (currentLevel >= distance) continue;
        
        Cell currentCell = getCell()[current.getRow()][current.getCol()];
        
        for (int d = 0; d < 4; d++) {
            int nr = current.getRow() + dRow[d];
            int nc = current.getCol() + dCol[d];
            
            if (nr < 0 || nr >= getRows() || nc < 0 || nc >= getCols()) continue;
            
            Cell neighborCell = getCell()[nr][nc];
            if (!(neighborCell instanceof FillableCell)) continue;
            
            FillableCell fillableNeighbor = (FillableCell) neighborCell;
            Pipe neighborPipe = fillableNeighbor.getPipe();
            if (neighborPipe == null || neighborPipe.isFilled()) continue;
            
            Direction outgoingDir = dirs[d];
            Direction incomingDir = getOppositeDirection(outgoingDir);
            
            // Check if current cell connects in the outgoing direction
            boolean currentConnects = false;
            if (currentCell instanceof FillableCell) {
                Pipe currentPipe = ((FillableCell) currentCell).getPipe();
                if (currentPipe != null && currentPipe.getConnections().contains(outgoingDir)) {
                    currentConnects = true;
                }
            } else if (currentCell instanceof TerminationCell) {
                TerminationCell tc = (TerminationCell) currentCell;
                if (tc.getPointingTo() == outgoingDir) {
                    currentConnects = true;
                }
            }
            
            if (!currentConnects) continue;
            
            // Check if neighbor pipe connects in the incoming direction
            if (neighborPipe.getConnections().contains(incomingDir)) {
                neighborPipe.setFilled(true);
                Coordinate nCoord = fillableNeighbor.getCoord();
                getFilledTiles().add(nCoord);
                visited.add(nCoord);
                queue.add(nCoord);
                level.put(nCoord, currentLevel + 1);
            }
        }
    }
    
    // Update tracking fields
    prevFilledDistance = distance;
    prevFilledTiles = getFilledTiles().size();
}

  /**
```java
   * <!-- begin-user-doc -->
   * <!-- end-user-doc -->
   * <!-- begin-model-doc -->
   * Summary: Expands water filling to the specified distance from the source using BFS.
   * Algorithm: 
   *   1. If distance == 0, do nothing.
   *   2. Use BFS starting from all currently filled tiles (or from source if first time).
   *   3. For each tile at current distance, check all 4 directions:
   *      a. Get neighboring cell.
   *      b. If neighbor is FillableCell with a pipe:
   *         - Check if current cell's outgoing direction connects to neighbor's incoming direction (opposite direction).
   *         - If connected and neighbor pipe not filled, mark it as filled.
   *   4. Update prevFilledDistance and prevFilledTiles.
   * Related Features: filledTiles, sourceCell, sinkCell, prevFilledDistance, prevFilledTiles
   * Related Classes: Coordinate, FillableCell, Pipe, Direction, TerminationCell
   * Input: distance : int - the current water expansion distance.
   * Output: void
   * Pre-condition: distance >= 0
   * Post-condition: All reachable pipes within the given distance from source are marked as filled if connections allow.
   * <!-- end-model-doc -->
   * @model annotation="http://www.ustb.edu.cn/sei/mde/EnhancedCodeGen generated='true'"
```

/**
 * <!-- begin-user-doc -->
 * <!-- end-user-doc -->
 * <!-- begin-model-doc -->
 * Summary: Attempts to place a pipe at the specified coordinate on the map.
 * Algorithm: 
 *   1. Validate coordinate is within playable area [1..rows-2] x [1..cols-2].
 *   2. Get the cell at that coordinate.
 *   3. Check that cell is instance of FillableCell and its pipe is null.
 *   4. If valid: set the cell's pipe to the given pipe and return true.
 *   5. Otherwise return false.
 * Related Features: cell array, rows, cols
 * Related Classes: Coordinate, FillableCell, Pipe, Cell
 * Input: row : int, col : int - internal grid coordinates. pipe : Pipe - the pipe to place.
 * Output: boolean - true if placement succeeded, false otherwise.
 * Pre-condition: None
 * Post-condition: If successful, the cell at the coordinate now contains the specified pipe.
 * <!-- end-model-doc -->
 * @model annotation="http://www.ustb.edu.cn/sei/mde/EnhancedCodeGen generated='true'"
 * @generated NOT
 */
public boolean tryPlacePipe(final int row, final int col, final Pipe pipe)
{
    if (row < 1 || row > getRows() - 2 || col < 1 || col > getCols() - 2) {
        return false;
    }
    Cell targetCell = getCell()[row][col];
    if (targetCell instanceof FillableCell && ((FillableCell) targetCell).getPipe() == null) {
        ((FillableCell) targetCell).setPipe(pipe);
        return true;
    }
    return false;
}

 * Summary: Removes a pipe from the specified coordinate, restoring the cell to empty state.

 * Input: coord : Coordinate - the coordinate to clear.

public void undo(final Coordinate coord)
{
    Cell targetCell = getCell()[coord.getRow()][coord.getCol()];
    if (targetCell instanceof FillableCell) {
        ((FillableCell) targetCell).setPipe(null);
    }
    getFilledTiles().remove(coord);
}
/**
 * <!-- begin-user-doc -->
 * <!-- end-user-doc -->
 * <!-- begin-model-doc -->
 * Summary: Expands water filling to the specified distance from the source using BFS.
 * Algorithm: 
 *   1. If distance == 0, do nothing.
 *   2. Use BFS starting from all currently filled tiles (or from source if first time).
 *   3. For each tile at current distance, check all 4 directions:
 *      a. Get neighboring cell.
 *      b. If neighbor is FillableCell with a pipe:
 *         - Check if current cell's outgoing direction connects to neighbor's incoming direction (opposite direction).
 *         - If connected and neighbor pipe not filled, mark it as filled.
 *   4. Update prevFilledDistance and prevFilledTiles.
 * Related Features: filledTiles, sourceCell, sinkCell, prevFilledDistance, prevFilledTiles
 * Related Classes: Coordinate, FillableCell, Pipe, Direction, TerminationCell
 * Input: distance : int - the current water expansion distance.
 * Output: void
 * Pre-condition: distance >= 0
 * Post-condition: All reachable pipes within the given distance from source are marked as filled if connections allow.
 * <!-- end-model-doc -->
 * @model annotation="http://www.ustb.edu.cn/sei/mde/EnhancedCodeGen generated='true'"
 * @generated NOT
 */
public void fillTiles(final int distance)
{
    if (distance == 0) {
        return;
    }
    
    // Save previous state
    this.prevFilledTiles = getFilledTiles().size();
    this.prevFilledDistance = distance;
    
    // BFS: start from currently filled tiles
    // We'll use a queue of coordinates to process
    EList<Coordinate> queue = new BasicEList<Coordinate>();
    EList<Coordinate> visited = new BasicEList<Coordinate>();
    
    // Initialize queue with all currently filled tiles
    // If no filled tiles yet, start from source cell
    if (getFilledTiles().isEmpty()) {
        if (getSourceCell() != null) {
            Coordinate sourceCoord = getSourceCell().getCoord();
            queue.add(sourceCoord);
            visited.add(sourceCoord);
        }
    } else {
        queue.addAll(getFilledTiles());
        visited.addAll(getFilledTiles());
    }
    
    // BFS for the given distance
    int currentDist = 0;
    while (!queue.isEmpty() && currentDist < distance) {
        int levelSize = queue.size();
        for (int i = 0; i < levelSize; i++) {
            Coordinate current = queue.get(0);
            queue.remove(0);
            
            Cell currentCell = getCell()[current.getRow()][current.getCol()];
            Pipe currentPipe = null;
            if (currentCell instanceof FillableCell) {
                currentPipe = ((FillableCell) currentCell).getPipe();
            } else if (currentCell instanceof TerminationCell) {
                // Termination cells don't have pipes but can propagate water
                // through their pointingTo direction
            }
            
            // Check all 4 directions
            Direction[] directions = {Direction.UP, Direction.DOWN, Direction.LEFT, Direction.RIGHT};
            for (Direction dir : directions) {
                Coordinate offset = getOffset(dir);
                int neighborRow = current.getRow() + offset.getRow();
                int neighborCol = current.getCol() + offset.getCol();
                
                // Check bounds
                if (neighborRow < 0 || neighborRow >= getRows() || neighborCol < 0 || neighborCol >= getCols()) {
                    continue;
                }
                
                Coordinate neighborCoord = Pa19Factory.eINSTANCE.createCoordinate();
                neighborCoord.setRow(neighborRow);
                neighborCoord.setCol(neighborCol);
                
                if (visited.contains(neighborCoord)) {
                    continue;
                }
                
                Cell neighborCell = getCell()[neighborRow][neighborCol];
                if (neighborCell instanceof FillableCell) {
                    Pipe neighborPipe = ((FillableCell) neighborCell).getPipe();
                    if (neighborPipe != null && !neighborPipe.isFilled()) {
                        // Check if current cell's outgoing direction connects to neighbor's incoming direction
                        boolean connected = false;
                        
                        if (currentCell instanceof FillableCell && currentPipe != null) {
                            // Current cell has a pipe, check if it has this direction
                            if (currentPipe.getConnections().contains(dir)) {
                                // Check if neighbor pipe has the opposite direction
                                Direction opposite = getOpposite(dir);
                                if (neighborPipe.getConnections().contains(opposite)) {
                                    connected = true;
                                }
                            }
                        } else if (currentCell instanceof TerminationCell) {
                            TerminationCell termCell = (TerminationCell) currentCell;
                            // If termination cell's pointingTo matches dir, it connects
                            if (termCell.getPointingTo() == dir) {
                                Direction opposite = getOpposite(dir);
                                if (neighborPipe.getConnections().contains(opposite)) {
                                    connected = true;
                                }
                            }
                        }
                        
                        if (connected) {
                            neighborPipe.setFilled(true);
                            getFilledTiles().add(neighborCoord);
                            visited.add(neighborCoord);
                            queue.add(neighborCoord);
                        }
                    }
                } else if (neighborCell instanceof TerminationCell) {
                    TerminationCell termCell = (TerminationCell) neighborCell;
                    if (!termCell.isFilled()) {
                        // Check connection from current cell
                        boolean connected = false;
                        if (currentCell instanceof FillableCell && currentPipe != null) {
                            if (currentPipe.getConnections().contains(dir)) {
                                Direction opposite = getOpposite(dir);
                                if (termCell.getPointingTo() == opposite) {
                                    connected = true;
                                }
                            }
                        } else if (currentCell instanceof TerminationCell) {
                            TerminationCell currTerm = (TerminationCell) currentCell;
                            if (currTerm.getPointingTo() == dir) {
                                Direction opposite = getOpposite(dir);
                                if (termCell.getPointingTo() == opposite) {
                                    connected = true;
                                }
                            }
                        }
                        
                        if (connected) {
                            termCell.setFilled(true);
                            visited.add(neighborCoord);
                            queue.add(neighborCoord);
                        }
                    }
                }
            }
        }
        currentDist++;
    }
}
private Direction getOpposite(Direction dir) {
    switch (dir) {
        case UP: return Direction.DOWN;
        case DOWN: return Direction.UP;
        case LEFT: return Direction.RIGHT;
        case RIGHT: return Direction.LEFT;
    }
    return null;
}
private Coordinate getOffset(Direction dir) {
    Coordinate offset = Pa19Factory.eINSTANCE.createCoordinate();
    switch (dir) {
        case UP:
            offset.setRow(-1);
            offset.setCol(0);
            break;
        case DOWN:
            offset.setRow(1);
            offset.setCol(0);
            break;
        case LEFT:
            offset.setRow(0);
            offset.setCol(-1);
            break;
        case RIGHT:
            offset.setRow(0);
            offset.setCol(1);
            break;
    }
    return offset;
}

/**
 * <!-- begin-user-doc -->
 * <!-- end-user-doc -->
 * <!-- begin-model-doc -->
 * Summary: Attempts to place a pipe at the specified coordinate on the map.
 * Algorithm: 
 *   1. Validate coordinate is within playable area [1..rows-2] x [1..cols-2].
 *   2. Get the cell at that coordinate.
 *   3. Check that cell is instance of FillableCell and its pipe is null.
 *   4. If valid: set the cell's pipe to the given pipe and return true.
 *   5. Otherwise return false.
 * Related Features: cell array, rows, cols
 * Related Classes: Coordinate, FillableCell, Pipe, Cell
 * Input: row : int, col : int - internal grid coordinates. pipe : Pipe - the pipe to place.
 * Output: boolean - true if placement succeeded, false otherwise.
 * Pre-condition: None
 * Post-condition: If successful, the cell at the coordinate now contains the specified pipe.
 * <!-- end-model-doc -->
 * @model annotation="http://www.ustb.edu.cn/sei/mde/EnhancedCodeGen generated='true'"
 * @generated NOT
 */
public boolean tryPlacePipe(final int row, final int col, final Pipe pipe)
{
    if (row < 1 || row > getRows() - 2 || col < 1 || col > getCols() - 2) {
        return false;
    }
    Cell targetCell = getCell()[row][col];
    if (targetCell instanceof FillableCell && ((FillableCell) targetCell).getPipe() == null) {
        ((FillableCell) targetCell).setPipe(pipe);
        return true;
    }
    return false;
}
/**
 * <!-- begin-user-doc -->
 * <!-- end-user-doc -->
 * <!-- begin-model-doc -->
 * Summary: Removes a pipe from the specified coordinate, restoring the cell to empty state.
 * Algorithm: 
 *   1. Get the cell at the given coordinate.
 *   2. If cell is FillableCell: set its pipe to null.
 *   3. Remove the coordinate from filledTiles if present.
 * Related Features: cell array, filledTiles
 * Related Classes: Coordinate, FillableCell, Pipe
 * Input: coord : Coordinate - the coordinate to clear.
 * Output: void
 * Pre-condition: coord is not null and within grid bounds.
 * Post-condition: The cell at coord has no pipe; if it was a filled tile, it is removed from filledTiles.
 * <!-- end-model-doc -->
 * @model annotation="http://www.ustb.edu.cn/sei/mde/EnhancedCodeGen generated='true'"
 * @generated NOT
 */
public void undo(final Coordinate coord)
{
    Cell targetCell = getCell()[coord.getRow()][coord.getCol()];
    if (targetCell instanceof FillableCell) {
        ((FillableCell) targetCell).setPipe(null);
    }
    getFilledTiles().remove(coord);
}
/**
 * <!-- begin-user-doc -->
 * <!-- end-user-doc -->
 * <!-- begin-model-doc -->
 * Summary: Expands water filling to the specified distance from the source using BFS.
 * Algorithm: 
 *   1. If distance == 0, do nothing.
 *   2. Use BFS starting from all currently filled tiles (or from source if first time).
 *   3. For each tile at current distance, check all 4 directions:
 *      a. Get neighboring cell.
 *      b. If neighbor is FillableCell with a pipe:
 *         - Check if current cell's outgoing direction connects to neighbor's incoming direction (opposite direction).
 *         - If connected and neighbor pipe not filled, mark it as filled.
 *   4. Update prevFilledDistance and prevFilledTiles.
 * Related Features: filledTiles, sourceCell, sinkCell, prevFilledDistance, prevFilledTiles
 * Related Classes: Coordinate, FillableCell, Pipe, Direction, TerminationCell
 * Input: distance : int - the current water expansion distance.
 * Output: void
 * Pre-condition: distance >= 0
 * Post-condition: All reachable pipes within the given distance from source are marked as filled if connections allow.
 * <!-- end-model-doc -->
 * @model annotation="http://www.ustb.edu.cn/sei/mde/EnhancedCodeGen generated='true'"
 * @generated NOT
 */
public void fillTiles(final int distance)
{
    if (distance == 0) {
        return;
    }
    
    // Save previous state
    prevFilledTiles = getFilledTiles().size();
    prevFilledDistance = distance;
    
    // BFS queue and visited set
    EList<Coordinate> queue = new BasicEList<Coordinate>();
    EList<Coordinate> visited = new BasicEList<Coordinate>();
    
    // Initialize BFS from currently filled tiles or source
    if (getFilledTiles().isEmpty()) {
        if (getSourceCell() != null && getSourceCell().getCoord() != null) {
            queue.add(getSourceCell().getCoord());
            visited.add(getSourceCell().getCoord());
        }
    } else {
        queue.addAll(getFilledTiles());
        visited.addAll(getFilledTiles());
    }
    
    // BFS level by level up to the given distance
    int currentDist = 0;
    while (!queue.isEmpty() && currentDist < distance) {
        int levelSize = queue.size();
        for (int i = 0; i < levelSize; i++) {
            Coordinate current = queue.get(0);
            queue.remove(0);
            
            Cell currentCell = getCell()[current.getRow()][current.getCol()];
            
            // Check all 4 directions
            // UP: row-1, DOWN: row+1, LEFT: col-1, RIGHT: col+1
            int[][] offsets = {{-1, 0, 0}, {1, 0, 1}, {0, -1, 2}, {0, 1, 3}}; // {dRow, dCol, dirIndex}
            
            for (int[] offset : offsets) {
                int neighborRow = current.getRow() + offset[0];
                int neighborCol = current.getCol() + offset[1];
                int dirIndex = offset[2];
                
                // Check bounds
                if (neighborRow < 0 || neighborRow >= getRows() || neighborCol < 0 || neighborCol >= getCols()) {
                    continue;
                }
                
                // Determine direction from current to neighbor
                Direction dir = null;
                switch (dirIndex) {
                    case 0: dir = Direction.UP; break;
                    case 1: dir = Direction.DOWN; break;
                    case 2: dir = Direction.LEFT; break;
                    case 3: dir = Direction.RIGHT; break;
                }
                
                // Create neighbor coordinate for checking
                Coordinate neighborCoord = Pa19Factory.eINSTANCE.createCoordinate();
                neighborCoord.setRow(neighborRow);
                neighborCoord.setCol(neighborCol);
                
                if (visited.contains(neighborCoord)) {
                    continue;
                }
                
                Cell neighborCell = getCell()[neighborRow][neighborCol];
                
                // Check if current cell can connect to neighbor in this direction
                boolean currentConnects = false;
                if (currentCell instanceof FillableCell) {
                    Pipe currentPipe = ((FillableCell) currentCell).getPipe();
                    if (currentPipe != null && currentPipe.getConnections().contains(dir)) {
                        currentConnects = true;
                    }
                } else if (currentCell instanceof TerminationCell) {
                    if (((TerminationCell) currentCell).getPointingTo() == dir) {
                        currentConnects = true;
                    }
                }
                
                if (!currentConnects) {
                    continue;
                }
                
                // Determine opposite direction (neighbor's incoming direction)
                Direction oppositeDir = null;
                switch (dirIndex) {
                    case 0: oppositeDir = Direction.DOWN; break;
                    case 1: oppositeDir = Direction.UP; break;
                    case 2: oppositeDir = Direction.RIGHT; break;
                    case 3: oppositeDir = Direction.LEFT; break;
                }
                
                if (neighborCell instanceof FillableCell) {
                    Pipe neighborPipe = ((FillableCell) neighborCell).getPipe();
                    if (neighborPipe != null && !neighborPipe.isFilled()) {
                        if (neighborPipe.getConnections().contains(oppositeDir)) {
                            neighborPipe.setFilled(true);
                            getFilledTiles().add(neighborCoord);
                            visited.add(neighborCoord);
                            queue.add(neighborCoord);
                        }
                    }
                } else if (neighborCell instanceof TerminationCell) {
                    TerminationCell termCell = (TerminationCell) neighborCell;
                    if (!termCell.isFilled() && termCell.getPointingTo() == oppositeDir) {
                        termCell.setFilled(true);
                        visited.add(neighborCoord);
                        queue.add(neighborCoord);
                    }
                }
            }
        }
        currentDist++;
    }
}
/**
 * <!-- begin-user-doc -->
 * <!-- end-user-doc -->
 * <!-- begin-model-doc -->
 * Uses BFS to check if a path exists from sourceCell to sinkCell
 * <!-- end-model-doc -->
 * @model
 * @generated NOT
 */
public boolean checkPath()
{
    if (getSourceCell() == null || getSinkCell() == null) {
        return false;
    }
    
    EList<Coordinate> queue = new BasicEList<Coordinate>();
    EList<Coordinate> visited = new BasicEList<Coordinate>();
    
    Coordinate sourceCoord = getSourceCell().getCoord();
    queue.add(sourceCoord);
    visited.add(sourceCoord);
    
    while (!queue.isEmpty()) {
        Coordinate current = queue.get(0);
        queue.remove(0);
        
        // Check if we reached the sink
        if (current.getRow() == getSinkCell().getCoord().getRow() && 
            current.getCol() == getSinkCell().getCoord().getCol()) {
            return true;
        }
        
        Cell currentCell = getCell()[current.getRow()][current.getCol()];
        
        // Check all 4 directions
        int[][] offsets = {{-1, 0, 0}, {1, 0, 1}, {0, -1, 2}, {0, 1, 3}};
        
        for (int[] offset : offsets) {
            int neighborRow = current.getRow() + offset[0];
            int neighborCol = current.getCol() + offset[1];
            int dirIndex = offset[2];
            
            if (neighborRow < 0 || neighborRow >= getRows() || neighborCol < 0 || neighborCol >= getCols()) {
                continue;
            }
            
            Direction dir = null;
            switch (dirIndex) {
                case 0: dir = Direction.UP; break;
                case 1: dir = Direction.DOWN; break;
                case 2: dir = Direction.LEFT; break;
                case 3: dir = Direction.RIGHT; break;
            }
            
            Coordinate neighborCoord = Pa19Factory.eINSTANCE.createCoordinate();
            neighborCoord.setRow(neighborRow);
            neighborCoord.setCol(neighborCol);
            
            if (visited.contains(neighborCoord)) {
                continue;
            }
            
            Cell neighborCell = getCell()[neighborRow][neighborCol];
            
            // Check if current cell connects in this direction
            boolean currentConnects = false;
            if (currentCell instanceof FillableCell) {
                Pipe currentPipe = ((FillableCell) currentCell).getPipe();
                if (currentPipe != null && currentPipe.getConnections().contains(dir)) {
                    currentConnects = true;
                }
            } else if (currentCell instanceof TerminationCell) {
                if (((TerminationCell) currentCell).getPointingTo() == dir) {
                    currentConnects = true;
                }
            }
            
            if (!currentConnects) {
                continue;
            }
            
            Direction oppositeDir = null;
            switch (dirIndex) {
                case 0: oppositeDir = Direction.DOWN; break;
                case 1: oppositeDir = Direction.UP; break;
                case 2: oppositeDir = Direction.RIGHT; break;
                case 3: oppositeDir = Direction.LEFT; break;
            }
            
            boolean neighborConnects = false;
            if (neighborCell instanceof FillableCell) {
                Pipe neighborPipe = ((FillableCell) neighborCell).getPipe();
                if (neighborPipe != null && neighborPipe.getConnections().contains(oppositeDir)) {
                    neighborConnects = true;
                }
            } else if (neighborCell instanceof TerminationCell) {
                if (((TerminationCell) neighborCell).getPointingTo() == oppositeDir) {
                    neighborConnects = true;
                }
            }
            
            if (neighborConnects) {
                visited.add(neighborCoord);
                queue.add(neighborCoord);
            }
        }
    }
    
    return false;
}
/**
 * <!-- begin-user-doc -->
 * <!-- end-user-doc -->
 * <!-- begin-model-doc -->
 * Summary: Checks if the player has lost (water flow stopped making progress).
 * Algorithm: 
 *   1. If prevFilledDistance is not null and prevFilledDistance > 0:
 *      a. If prevFilledTiles == filledTiles.size(): return true.
 *   2. Return false.
 * Related Features: prevFilledDistance, prevFilledTiles, filledTiles
 * Related Classes: None
 * Input: None
 * Output: boolean - true if no new tiles were filled in the last water update, false otherwise.
 * Pre-condition: None
 * Post-condition: Returns whether water flow has stalled.
 * <!-- end-model-doc -->
 * @model annotation="http://www.ustb.edu.cn/sei/mde/EnhancedCodeGen generated='true'"
 * @generated NOT
 */
public boolean hasLost()
{
    if (getPrevFilledDistance() != null && getPrevFilledDistance() > 0) {
        if (getPrevFilledTiles() == getFilledTiles().size()) {
            return true;
        }
    }
    return false;
}

```java
  /**
   * <!-- begin-user-doc -->
   * <!-- end-user-doc -->
   * <!-- begin-model-doc -->
   * Summary: Expands water filling to the specified distance from the source using BFS.
   * Algorithm: 
   *   1. If distance == 0, do nothing.
   *   2. Use BFS starting from all currently filled tiles (or from source if first time).
   *   3. For each tile at current distance, check all 4 directions:
   *      a. Get neighboring cell.
   *      b. If neighbor is FillableCell with a pipe:
   *         - Check if current cell's outgoing direction connects to neighbor's incoming direction (opposite direction).
   *         - If connected and neighbor pipe not filled, mark it as filled.
   *   4. Update prevFilledDistance and prevFilledTiles.
   * Related Features: filledTiles, sourceCell, sinkCell, prevFilledDistance, prevFilledTiles
   * Related Classes: Coordinate, FillableCell, Pipe, Direction, TerminationCell
   * Input: distance : int - the current water expansion distance.
   * Output: void
   * Pre-condition: distance >= 0
   * Post-condition: All reachable pipes within the given distance from source are marked as filled if connections allow.
   * <!-- end-model-doc -->
   * @model annotation="http://www.ustb.edu.cn/sei/mde/EnhancedCodeGen generated='true'"
```

public boolean tryPlacePipe(final int row, final int col, final Pipe pipe)
{
    // Validate coordinate is within playable area [1..rows-2] x [1..cols-2]

        return false;
    }

    return false;

public void fillTiles(final int distance) {
    if (distance == 0) return;
    
    // Get the source cell's coordinate
    Coordinate sourceCoord = getSourceCell().getCoord();
    
    // Use a queue for BFS
    java.util.Queue<Coordinate> queue = new java.util.LinkedList<>();
    java.util.Set<Coordinate> visited = new java.util.HashSet<>();
    
    // Start from the source cell
    queue.add(sourceCoord);
    visited.add(sourceCoord);
    
    int currentDistance = 0;
    
    while (!queue.isEmpty() && currentDistance < distance) {
        int levelSize = queue.size();
        currentDistance++;
        
        for (int i = 0; i < levelSize; i++) {
            Coordinate current = queue.poll();
            int row = current.getRow();
            int col = current.getCol();
            
            Cell currentCell = getCell()[row][col];
            
            // Determine which directions to check
            java.util.List<Direction> directionsToCheck = new java.util.ArrayList<>();
            
            if (currentCell instanceof TerminationCell) {
                // Only check the direction the termination cell points to
                TerminationCell termCell = (TerminationCell) currentCell;
                if (termCell.isFilled()) {
                    directionsToCheck.add(termCell.getPointingTo());
                }
            } else if (currentCell instanceof FillableCell) {
                FillableCell fillCell = (FillableCell) currentCell;
                Pipe pipe = fillCell.getPipe();
                if (pipe != null && pipe.isFilled()) {
                    // Check all directions the pipe connects to
                    directionsToCheck.addAll(pipe.getConnections());
                }
            }
            
            for (Direction dir : directionsToCheck) {
                int newRow = row;
                int newCol = col;
                
                switch (dir) {
                    case UP: newRow--; break;
                    case DOWN: newRow++; break;
                    case LEFT: newCol--; break;
                    case RIGHT: newCol++; break;
                }
                
                // Check bounds
                if (newRow < 0 || newRow >= getRows() || newCol < 0 || newCol >= getCols()) {
                    continue;
                }
                
                Coordinate neighborCoord = null;
                // Find or create coordinate for the neighbor
                // Actually, cells have coordinates, let me use that
                Cell neighborCell = getCell()[newRow][newCol];
                if (neighborCell == null) continue;
                
                Coordinate neighborPos = neighborCell.getCoord();
                if (neighborPos == null || visited.contains(neighborPos)) continue;
                
                if (neighborCell instanceof FillableCell) {
                    FillableCell neighborFill = (FillableCell) neighborCell;
                    Pipe neighborPipe = neighborFill.getPipe();
                    if (neighborPipe != null && !neighborPipe.isFilled()) {
                        // Check if neighbor pipe has the opposite direction
                        Direction oppositeDir = getOppositeDirection(dir);
                        if (neighborPipe.getConnections().contains(oppositeDir)) {
                            // Fill the pipe
                            neighborPipe.setFilled(true);
                            // Add to filledTiles
                            getFilledTiles().add(neighborPos);
                            // Add to queue for next level
                            queue.add(neighborPos);
                            visited.add(neighborPos);
                        }
                    }
                } else if (neighborCell instanceof TerminationCell) {
                    TerminationCell neighborTerm = (TerminationCell) neighborCell;
                    Direction oppositeDir = getOppositeDirection(dir);
                    if (neighborTerm.getPointingTo() == oppositeDir && !neighborTerm.isFilled()) {
                        neighborTerm.setFilled(true);
                        queue.add(neighborPos);
                        visited.add(neighborPos);
                    }
                }
            }
        }
    }
    
    // Update prevFilledDistance and prevFilledTiles
    setPrevFilledDistance(distance);
    setPrevFilledTiles(getFilledTiles().size());
}
public boolean checkPath() {
    // BFS from sourceCell to sinkCell
    if (getSourceCell() == null || getSinkCell() == null) return false;
    
    Coordinate sourceCoord = getSourceCell().getCoord();
    Coordinate sinkCoord = getSinkCell().getCoord();
    
    java.util.Queue<Coordinate> queue = new java.util.LinkedList<>();
    java.util.Set<Coordinate> visited = new java.util.HashSet<>();
    
    queue.add(sourceCoord);
    visited.add(sourceCoord);
    
    while (!queue.isEmpty()) {
        Coordinate current = queue.poll();
        
        if (current.equals(sinkCoord)) return true;
        
        int row = current.getRow();
        int col = current.getCol();
        
        Cell currentCell = getCell()[row][col];
        
        java.util.List<Direction> directionsToCheck = new java.util.ArrayList<>();
        
        if (currentCell instanceof TerminationCell) {
            TerminationCell termCell = (TerminationCell) currentCell;
            directionsToCheck.add(termCell.getPointingTo());
        } else if (currentCell instanceof FillableCell) {
            FillableCell fillCell = (FillableCell) currentCell;
            Pipe pipe = fillCell.getPipe();
            if (pipe != null) {
                directionsToCheck.addAll(pipe.getConnections());
            }
        }
        
        for (Direction dir : directionsToCheck) {
            int newRow = row;
            int newCol = col;
            
            switch (dir) {
                case UP: newRow--; break;
                case DOWN: newRow++; break;
                case LEFT: newCol--; break;
                case RIGHT: newCol++; break;
            }
            
            if (newRow < 0 || newRow >= getRows() || newCol < 0 || newCol >= getCols()) continue;
            
            Cell neighborCell = getCell()[newRow][newCol];
            if (neighborCell == null) continue;
            
            Coordinate neighborPos = neighborCell.getCoord();
            if (neighborPos == null || visited.contains(neighborPos)) continue;
            
            if (neighborCell instanceof FillableCell) {
                FillableCell neighborFill = (FillableCell) neighborCell;
                Pipe neighborPipe = neighborFill.getPipe();
                if (neighborPipe != null) {
                    Direction oppositeDir = getOppositeDirection(dir);
                    if (neighborPipe.getConnections().contains(oppositeDir)) {
                        queue.add(neighborPos);
                        visited.add(neighborPos);
                    }
                }
            } else if (neighborCell instanceof TerminationCell) {
                TerminationCell neighborTerm = (TerminationCell) neighborCell;
                Direction oppositeDir = getOppositeDirection(dir);
                if (neighborTerm.getPointingTo() == oppositeDir) {
                    queue.add(neighborPos);
                    visited.add(neighborPos);
                }
            }
        }
    }
    
    return false;
}
private Direction getOppositeDirection(Direction dir) {
    switch (dir) {
        case UP: return Direction.DOWN;
        case DOWN: return Direction.UP;
        case LEFT: return Direction.RIGHT;
        case RIGHT: return Direction.LEFT;
        default: return null;
    }
}
public boolean hasLost() {
    if (getPrevFilledDistance() != null && getPrevFilledDistance() > 0) {
        if (getPrevFilledTiles() == getFilledTiles().size()) {
            return true;
        }
    }
    return false;
}

public void fillTiles(final int distance) {
    if (distance == 0) return;
    
    // BFS starting from all currently filled tiles
    // Use a queue for BFS
    java.util.LinkedList<Coordinate> queue = new java.util.LinkedList<>();
    java.util.HashSet<Coordinate> visited = new java.util.HashSet<>();
    
    // Start from source cell
    Coordinate sourceCoord = getSourceCell().getCoord();
    queue.add(sourceCoord);
    visited.add(sourceCoord);
    
    // Also add all currently filled tiles
    for (Coordinate coord : getFilledTiles()) {
        if (!visited.contains(coord)) {
            queue.add(coord);
            visited.add(coord);
        }
    }
    
    int currentDist = 0;
    
    while (!queue.isEmpty() && currentDist < distance) {
        int levelSize = queue.size();
        currentDist++;
        
        for (int i = 0; i < levelSize; i++) {
            Coordinate current = queue.poll();
            int row = current.getRow();
            int col = current.getCol();
            
            Cell currentCell = getCell()[row][col];
            
            // Determine which directions to check
            java.util.List<Direction> dirsToCheck = new java.util.ArrayList<>();
            dirsToCheck.add(Direction.UP);
            dirsToCheck.add(Direction.DOWN);
            dirsToCheck.add(Direction.LEFT);
            dirsToCheck.add(Direction.RIGHT);
            
            for (Direction dir : dirsToCheck) {
                // Check if current cell can connect in this direction
                boolean canConnect = false;
                if (currentCell instanceof TerminationCell) {
                    TerminationCell termCell = (TerminationCell) currentCell;
                    canConnect = termCell.isFilled() && termCell.getPointingTo() == dir;
                } else if (currentCell instanceof FillableCell) {
                    FillableCell fillCell = (FillableCell) currentCell;
                    Pipe pipe = fillCell.getPipe();
                    canConnect = pipe != null && pipe.isFilled() && pipe.getConnections().contains(dir);
                }
                
                if (!canConnect) continue;
                
                int newRow = row;
                int newCol = col;
                switch (dir) {
                    case UP: newRow--; break;
                    case DOWN: newRow++; break;
                    case LEFT: newCol--; break;
                    case RIGHT: newCol++; break;
                }
                
                if (newRow < 0 || newRow >= getRows() || newCol < 0 || newCol >= getCols()) continue;
                
                Cell neighborCell = getCell()[newRow][newCol];
                if (neighborCell == null) continue;
                
                Coordinate neighborCoord = neighborCell.getCoord();
                if (neighborCoord == null || visited.contains(neighborCoord)) continue;
                
                Direction oppositeDir = getOppositeDirection(dir);
                
                if (neighborCell instanceof FillableCell) {
                    FillableCell neighborFill = (FillableCell) neighborCell;
                    Pipe neighborPipe = neighborFill.getPipe();
                    if (neighborPipe != null && !neighborPipe.isFilled() && neighborPipe.getConnections().contains(oppositeDir)) {
                        neighborPipe.setFilled(true);
                        getFilledTiles().add(neighborCoord);
                        queue.add(neighborCoord);
                        visited.add(neighborCoord);
                    }
                } else if (neighborCell instanceof TerminationCell) {
                    TerminationCell neighborTerm = (TerminationCell) neighborCell;
                    if (!neighborTerm.isFilled() && neighborTerm.getPointingTo() == oppositeDir) {
                        neighborTerm.setFilled(true);
                        queue.add(neighborCoord);
                        visited.add(neighborCoord);
                    }
                }
            }
        }
    }
    
    // Update prevFilledDistance and prevFilledTiles
    setPrevFilledDistance(distance);
    setPrevFilledTiles(getFilledTiles().size());
}

# Task
You will be given a **Requirement** and a **Class Diagram** in PlantUML. Your task is to annotate every operation listed in **Operations** with a specification.

An operation specification must describe the following sections about the operation:
1. Summary: the summary of functionality;
2. Algorithm: algorithm or pseudo code;
3. Related Features: a list of structural or behavior features within this class that shall be accessed;
4. Related Classes: a list of classes and data types defined in **Class Diagram** that shall be accessed, in the format of `Related Classes: ClsA, CLsB, ...` or `Related Classes: None`;
5. Input: the input parameters, including the meaning, the format, and the value ranges if necessary;
6. Output: output value, including the meaning, the format, and the value ranges if necessary;
7. Pre-condition: the condition that the system and the input must satisfy before the operation is executed;
8. Post-condition: the condition that the system and the output must satisfy after the operation is executed.

Finish this task by following the guidelines below.
1. Take the principle of modularization into account.
2. For each operation, determine its functional boundary based on the given requirement. Ensure high cohesion and low coupling.
3. If there is any unspecified details, such as undefined constants, rates, and ratios, then you must infer them.
4. Make sure that all requirements can be covered.

# Requirement
```text
Overall / Domain Description
This is a console pipe-connection game. The game board is a grid surrounded by outer walls. Inside the board there is one source, and on the border there is one sink. The player places pipes from a pipe queue. After an initial delay, water begins to flow through connected pipes.
The board uses zero-based internal array indices. However, index 0 and the last row/column are occupied by the outer wall border. Therefore, the playable area starts from internal index 1 and ends at rows - 2 / cols - 2.
Player-facing coordinates intentionally align with these playable internal indices:
row 1 refers to internal row 1, and column 'A' refers to internal column 1. No row-minus-one or column-minus-one conversion is applied, except that column letters are mapped so that 'A' becomes 1.
Directions include up, down, left, and right. Each direction has a corresponding opposite direction and a unit movement offset(class PA19Helper will help class Direction to provide these functions). Pipe shapes define which directions they connect to. Termination type distinguishes source and sink.

Functional Requirements

Coordinate and Direction
A coordinate stores the internal row and column used directly to access the cell grid. A cell stored at a given grid position should carry the same coordinate value.
Because the outer border occupies index 0, playable cells naturally begin at index 1. This allows user input to align directly with the playable internal grid.
Directions support movement calculations through their unit offsets and can be compared against their opposite direction when checking pipe connectivity.

Game
The game supports placing the current pipe, skipping the current pipe, undoing the latest placement, advancing the water state, checking whether the player has won, checking whether the player has lost, and tracking the number of player steps.
When the player places a pipe, the row value is used directly. The column letter is converted so that 'A' maps to column 1, 'B' maps to column 2, and so on. For example, row 1 and column 'A' target the internal cell at [1][1].
Skipping removes the current pipe from the front of the queue and counts as one step.
Undo restores the latest placed pipe to the front of the queue, clears that pipe from the board, and counts as one step. If there is no previous placement to undo, the operation fails without changing the board.

Map
The map stores cells in a two-dimensional grid with indices from [0..rows-1] and [0..cols-1]. The outermost row and column positions are walls. The playable area is [1..rows-2] by [1..cols-2].
A pipe may be placed only when all of the following are true:
1. The target coordinate is inside the playable area.
2. The target cell is a fillable cell.
3. The target cell does not already contain a pipe.

Cell Family
Cells are parsed from map characters into concrete cell types.
A fillable cell may contain a pipe or be empty. Empty fillable cells render as a dot.
A termination cell represents either the source or the sink. It stores the direction it points toward and whether it has been filled by water.
A wall cell represents the board boundary and renders using the wall character.

Termination Cell Rendering
A termination cell renders as an arrow based on its direction and filled state. Filled and unfilled arrows come from the shared rendering constants.
Both source and sink use their stored pointing direction directly. The direction is not reversed for either type.
Throws IllegalStateException("Invalid pointingTo value!") for unknown direction.

Pipe
A pipe has a shape and a filled state. Its shape determines the directions it connects to.
Supported pipe shapes include horizontal, vertical, the four corner shapes, and cross.
Pipe rendering depends on both shape and filled state. The rendered character should come from the shared rendering constants rather than hardcoded glyphs.
Short pipe codes include HZ, VT, TL, TR, BL, BR, and CR.

Water Flow
At the beginning of water flow, the source is marked as filled.
Water expands outward from the source by distance. Each update increases the reachable fill distance by one.
Water may move from one pipe to an adjacent pipe only when both sides connect to each other: the outgoing direction of one pipe must match the opposite direction of the neighboring pipe.
The filling process follows breadth-first expansion from the source.

Win and Loss Conditions
The player wins if there is a connected path from the source to the sink.
Path checking starts from the source by moving once in the source’s pointing direction. From each pipe, traversal continues through that pipe’s connection directions. The path does not require pipes to already be filled. Reaching the sink means the game is won.
The player loses when a water-flow update fills no new pipes. Loss is checked only after the initial delay has ended and water has actually started advancing.

Pipe Queue
The pipe queue stores upcoming pipes. The player always interacts with the pipe at the front.
When a pipe is consumed, the queue is automatically refilled up to a fixed maximum length using randomly generated pipe shapes.
Undo places the restored pipe back at the front of the queue.

Delay Bar
The delay bar starts with an initial value and decreases once per round.
While the value is still positive, water has not begun flowing. Once the countdown passes zero, the corresponding positive distance indicates how far water should expand from the source.

Cell Stack
The placement history records successfully placed cells in order.
Undo uses the most recent placement. The undo counter represents the number of successful undo actions, not the current size of the placement history.

External / Tool Classes
Pa19Helper is a handwritten helper and assembly class in the pa19 package. It is responsible for constructing core game objects from provided inputs, wiring together the map, pipe queue, delay bar, and placement history. It also centralizes basic parsing and direction utility behavior.
Deserializer is responsible for reading game input from a file and producing runtime game objects. It validates that the input file exists, reads the board size, delay value, map lines, and optional default pipes. If the input ends unexpectedly or an I/O error occurs, it returns no game object and logs the error.
When parsing map text, border cells are treated as sink-side termination candidates, while inner termination symbols are treated as source-side candidates.
Deserializer ignores blank lines and comment lines beginning with # when reading meaningful input.
PipePatterns is a final utility-style constant holder for all rendering characters. It contains the wall character and grouped constants for filled and unfilled arrows and pipe shapes. Rendering logic should rely on these constants instead of hardcoded characters.
StringUtils is a lightweight utility-style class for string helpers and should not be instantiated.
```

```text
row 1 refers to internal row 1, and column 'A' refers to internal column 1. No row-minus-one or column-minus-one conversion is applied, except that column letters are mapped so that 'A' becomes 1.
Directions include up, down, left, and right. Each direction has a corresponding opposite direction and a unit movement offset(class PA19Helper will help class Direction to provide these functions). Pipe shapes define which directions they connect to. Termination type distinguishes source and sink.

Functional Requirements

Coordinate and Direction
A coordinate stores the internal row and column used directly to access the cell grid. A cell stored at a given grid position should carry the same coordinate value.
Because the outer border occupies index 0, playable cells naturally begin at index 1. This allows user input to align directly with the playable internal grid.
Directions support movement calculations through their unit offsets and can be compared against their opposite direction when checking pipe connectivity.

Game
The game supports placing the current pipe, skipping the current pipe, undoing the latest placement, advancing the water state, checking whether the player has won, checking whether the player has lost, and tracking the number of player steps.
When the player places a pipe, the row value is used directly. The column letter is converted so that 'A' maps to column 1, 'B' maps to column 2, and so on. For example, row 1 and column 'A' target the internal cell at [1][1].
Skipping removes the current pipe from the front of the queue and counts as one step.
Undo restores the latest placed pipe to the front of the queue, clears that pipe from the board, and counts as one step. If there is no previous placement to undo, the operation fails without changing the board.

Map
The map stores cells in a two-dimensional grid with indices from [0..rows-1] and [0..cols-1]. The outermost row and column positions are walls. The playable area is [1..rows-2] by [1..cols-2].
A pipe may be placed only when all of the following are true:
1. The target coordinate is inside the playable area.
2. The target cell is a fillable cell.
3. The target cell does not already contain a pipe.

Cell Family
Cells are parsed from map characters into concrete cell types.
A fillable cell may contain a pipe or be empty. Empty fillable cells render as a dot.
A termination cell represents either the source or the sink. It stores the direction it points toward and whether it has been filled by water.
A wall cell represents the board boundary and renders using the wall character.

Termination Cell Rendering
A termination cell renders as an arrow based on its direction and filled state. Filled and unfilled arrows come from the shared rendering constants.
Both source and sink use their stored pointing direction directly. The direction is not reversed for either type.
Throws IllegalStateException("Invalid pointingTo value!") for unknown direction.

Pipe
A pipe has a shape and a filled state. Its shape determines the directions it connects to.
Supported pipe shapes include horizontal, vertical, the four corner shapes, and cross.
Pipe rendering depends on both shape and filled state. The rendered character should come from the shared rendering constants rather than hardcoded glyphs.
Short pipe codes include HZ, VT, TL, TR, BL, BR, and CR.

Water Flow
At the beginning of water flow, the source is marked as filled.
Water expands outward from the source by distance. Each update increases the reachable fill distance by one.
Water may move from one pipe to an adjacent pipe only when both sides connect to each other: the outgoing direction of one pipe must match the opposite direction of the neighboring pipe.
The filling process follows breadth-first expansion from the source.

Win and Loss Conditions
The player wins if there is a connected path from the source to the sink.
Path checking starts from the source by moving once in the source’s pointing direction. From each pipe, traversal continues through that pipe’s connection directions. The path does not require pipes to already be filled. Reaching the sink means the game is won.
The player loses when a water-flow update fills no new pipes. Loss is checked only after the initial delay has ended and water has actually started advancing.

Pipe Queue
The pipe queue stores upcoming pipes. The player always interacts with the pipe at the front.
When a pipe is consumed, the queue is automatically refilled up to a fixed maximum length using randomly generated pipe shapes.
Undo places the restored pipe back at the front of the queue.

Delay Bar
The delay bar starts with an initial value and decreases once per round.
While the value is still positive, water has not begun flowing. Once the countdown passes zero, the corresponding positive distance indicates how far water should expand from the source.

Cell Stack
The placement history records successfully placed cells in order.
Undo uses the most recent placement. The undo counter represents the number of successful undo actions, not the current size of the placement history.

External / Tool Classes
Pa19Helper is a handwritten helper and assembly class in the pa19 package. It is responsible for constructing core game objects from provided inputs, wiring together the map, pipe queue, delay bar, and placement history. It also centralizes basic parsing and direction utility behavior.
Deserializer is responsible for reading game input from a file and producing runtime game objects. It validates that the input file exists, reads the board size, delay value, map lines, and optional default pipes. If the input ends unexpectedly or an I/O error occurs, it returns no game object and logs the error.
When parsing map text, border cells are treated as sink-side termination candidates, while inner termination symbols are treated as source-side candidates.
Deserializer ignores blank lines and comment lines beginning with # when reading meaningful input.
PipePatterns is a final utility-style constant holder for all rendering characters. It contains the wall character and grouped constants for filled and unfilled arrows and pipe shapes. Rendering logic should rely on these constants instead of hardcoded characters.
StringUtils is a lightweight utility-style class for string helpers and should not be instantiated.
```

# Requirement
```text
Overall / Domain Description
This is a console pipe-connection game. The game board is a grid surrounded by outer walls. Inside the board there is one source, and on the border there is one sink. The player places pipes from a pipe queue. After an initial delay, water begins to flow through connected pipes.
The board uses zero-based internal array indices. However, index 0 and the last row/column are occupied by the outer wall border. Therefore, the playable area starts from internal index 1 and ends at rows - 2 / cols - 2.
Player-facing coordinates intentionally align with these playable internal indices:
row 1 refers to internal row 1, and column 'A' refers to internal column 1. No row-minus-one or column-minus-one conversion is applied, except that column letters are mapped so that 'A' becomes 1.
Directions include up, down, left, and right. Each direction has a corresponding opposite direction and a unit movement offset(class PA19Helper will help class Direction to provide these functions). Pipe shapes define which directions they connect to. Termination type distinguishes source and sink.

Functional Requirements

Coordinate and Direction
A coordinate stores the internal row and column used directly to access the cell grid. A cell stored at a given grid position should carry the same coordinate value.
Because the outer border occupies index 0, playable cells naturally begin at index 1. This allows user input to align directly with the playable internal grid.
Directions support movement calculations through their unit offsets and can be compared against their opposite direction when checking pipe connectivity.

Game
The game supports placing the current pipe, skipping the current pipe, undoing the latest placement, advancing the water state, checking whether the player has won, checking whether the player has lost, and tracking the number of player steps.
When the player places a pipe, the row value is used directly. The column letter is converted so that 'A' maps to column 1, 'B' maps to column 2, and so on. For example, row 1 and column 'A' target the internal cell at [1][1].
Skipping removes the current pipe from the front of the queue and counts as one step.
Undo restores the latest placed pipe to the front of the queue, clears that pipe from the board, and counts as one step. If there is no previous placement to undo, the operation fails without changing the board.

Map
The map stores cells in a two-dimensional grid with indices from [0..rows-1] and [0..cols-1]. The outermost row and column positions are walls. The playable area is [1..rows-2] by [1..cols-2].
A pipe may be placed only when all of the following are true:
1. The target coordinate is inside the playable area.
2. The target cell is a fillable cell.
3. The target cell does not already contain a pipe.

Cell Family
Cells are parsed from map characters into concrete cell types.
A fillable cell may contain a pipe or be empty. Empty fillable cells render as a dot.
A termination cell represents either the source or the sink. It stores the direction it points toward and whether it has been filled by water.
A wall cell represents the board boundary and renders using the wall character.

Termination Cell Rendering
A termination cell renders as an arrow based on its direction and filled state. Filled and unfilled arrows come from the shared rendering constants.
Both source and sink use their stored pointing direction directly. The direction is not reversed for either type.
Throws IllegalStateException("Invalid pointingTo value!") for unknown direction.

Pipe
A pipe has a shape and a filled state. Its shape determines the directions it connects to.
Supported pipe shapes include horizontal, vertical, the four corner shapes, and cross.
Pipe rendering depends on both shape and filled state. The rendered character should come from the shared rendering constants rather than hardcoded glyphs.
Short pipe codes include HZ, VT, TL, TR, BL, BR, and CR.

Water Flow
At the beginning of water flow, the source is marked as filled.
Water expands outward from the source by distance. Each update increases the reachable fill distance by one.
Water may move from one pipe to an adjacent pipe only when both sides connect to each other: the outgoing direction of one pipe must match the opposite direction of the neighboring pipe.
The filling process follows breadth-first expansion from the source.

Win and Loss Conditions
The player wins if there is a connected path from the source to the sink.
Path checking starts from the source by moving once in the source’s pointing direction. From each pipe, traversal continues through that pipe’s connection directions. The path does not require pipes to already be filled. Reaching the sink means the game is won.
The player loses when a water-flow update fills no new pipes. Loss is checked only after the initial delay has ended and water has actually started advancing.

Pipe Queue
The pipe queue stores upcoming pipes. The player always interacts with the pipe at the front.
When a pipe is consumed, the queue is automatically refilled up to a fixed maximum length using randomly generated pipe shapes.
Undo places the restored pipe back at the front of the queue.

Delay Bar
The delay bar starts with an initial value and decreases once per round.
While the value is still positive, water has not begun flowing. Once the countdown passes zero, the corresponding positive distance indicates how far water should expand from the source.

Cell Stack
The placement history records successfully placed cells in order.
Undo uses the most recent placement. The undo counter represents the number of successful undo actions, not the current size of the placement history.

External / Tool Classes
Pa19Helper is a handwritten helper and assembly class in the pa19 package. It is responsible for constructing core game objects from provided inputs, wiring together the map, pipe queue, delay bar, and placement history. It also centralizes basic parsing and direction utility behavior.
Deserializer is responsible for reading game input from a file and producing runtime game objects. It validates that the input file exists, reads the board size, delay value, map lines, and optional default pipes. If the input ends unexpectedly or an I/O error occurs, it returns no game object and logs the error.
When parsing map text, border cells are treated as sink-side termination candidates, while inner termination symbols are treated as source-side candidates.
Deserializer ignores blank lines and comment lines beginning with # when reading meaningful input.
PipePatterns is a final utility-style constant holder for all rendering characters. It contains the wall character and grouped constants for filled and unfilled arrows and pipe shapes. Rendering logic should rely on these constants instead of hardcoded characters.
StringUtils is a lightweight utility-style class for string helpers and should not be instantiated.
```
