# Requirement
```text
Overall / Domain Description
This is a console pipe-connection game. The game board is a grid surrounded by outer walls. Inside the board there is one source, and on the border there is one sink. The player places pipes from a pipe queue. After an initial delay, water begins to flow through connected pipes.
The board uses zero-based internal array indices. However, index 0 and the last row/column are occupied by the outer wall border. Therefore, the playable area starts from internal index 1 and ends at rows - 2 / cols - 2.
Player-facing coordinates intentionally align with these playable internal indices:
row 1 refers to internal row 1, and column 'A' refers to internal column 1. No row-minus-one or column-minus-one conversion is applied, except that column letters are mapped so that 'A' becomes 1.
Directions include up, down, left, and right. Each direction has a corresponding opposite direction and a unit movement offset(class PA19Helper will help class Direction to provide these functions). Pipe shapes define which directions they connect to. Termination type distinguishes source and sink.

Functional Requirements

Coordinate and Direction
A coordinate stores the internal row and column used directly to access the cell grid. A cell stored at a given grid position should carry the same coordinate value.
Because the outer border occupies index 0, playable cells naturally begin at index 1. This allows user input to align directly with the playable internal grid.
Directions support movement calculations through their unit offsets and can be compared against their opposite direction when checking pipe connectivity.

Game
The game supports placing the current pipe, skipping the current pipe, undoing the latest placement, advancing the water state, checking whether the player has won, checking whether the player has lost, and tracking the number of player steps.
When the player places a pipe, the row value is used directly. The column letter is converted so that 'A' maps to column 1, 'B' maps to column 2, and so on. For example, row 1 and column 'A' target the internal cell at [1][1].
Skipping removes the current pipe from the front of the queue and counts as one step.
Undo restores the latest placed pipe to the front of the queue, clears that pipe from the board, and counts as one step. If there is no previous placement to undo, the operation fails without changing the board.

Map
The map stores cells in a two-dimensional grid with indices from [0..rows-1] and [0..cols-1]. The outermost row and column positions are walls. The playable area is [1..rows-2] by [1..cols-2].
A pipe may be placed only when all of the following are true:
1. The target coordinate is inside the playable area.
2. The target cell is a fillable cell.
3. The target cell does not already contain a pipe.

Cell Family
Cells are parsed from map characters into concrete cell types.
A fillable cell may contain a pipe or be empty. Empty fillable cells render as a dot.
A termination cell represents either the source or the sink. It stores the direction it points toward and whether it has been filled by water.
A wall cell represents the board boundary and renders using the wall character.

Termination Cell Rendering
A termination cell renders as an arrow based on its direction and filled state. Filled and unfilled arrows come from the shared rendering constants.
Both source and sink use their stored pointing direction directly. The direction is not reversed for either type.
Throws IllegalStateException("Invalid pointingTo value!") for unknown direction.

Pipe
A pipe has a shape and a filled state. Its shape determines the directions it connects to.
Supported pipe shapes include horizontal, vertical, the four corner shapes, and cross.
Pipe rendering depends on both shape and filled state. The rendered character should come from the shared rendering constants rather than hardcoded glyphs.
Short pipe codes include HZ, VT, TL, TR, BL, BR, and CR.

Water Flow
At the beginning of water flow, the source is marked as filled.
Water expands outward from the source by distance. Each update increases the reachable fill distance by one.
Water may move from one pipe to an adjacent pipe only when both sides connect to each other: the outgoing direction of one pipe must match the opposite direction of the neighboring pipe.
The filling process follows breadth-first expansion from the source.

Win and Loss Conditions
The player wins if there is a connected path from the source to the sink.
Path checking starts from the source by moving once in the source’s pointing direction. From each pipe, traversal continues through that pipe’s connection directions. The path does not require pipes to already be filled. Reaching the sink means the game is won.
The player loses when a water-flow update fills no new pipes. Loss is checked only after the initial delay has ended and water has actually started advancing.

Pipe Queue
The pipe queue stores upcoming pipes. The player always interacts with the pipe at the front.
When a pipe is consumed, the queue is automatically refilled up to a fixed maximum length using randomly generated pipe shapes.
Undo places the restored pipe back at the front of the queue.

Delay Bar
The delay bar starts with an initial value and decreases once per round.
While the value is still positive, water has not begun flowing. Once the countdown passes zero, the corresponding positive distance indicates how far water should expand from the source.

Cell Stack
The placement history records successfully placed cells in order.
Undo uses the most recent placement. The undo counter represents the number of successful undo actions, not the current size of the placement history.

External / Tool Classes
Pa19Helper is a handwritten helper and assembly class in the pa19 package. It is responsible for constructing core game objects from provided inputs, wiring together the map, pipe queue, delay bar, and placement history. It also centralizes basic parsing and direction utility behavior.
Deserializer is responsible for reading game input from a file and producing runtime game objects. It validates that the input file exists, reads the board size, delay value, map lines, and optional default pipes. If the input ends unexpectedly or an I/O error occurs, it returns no game object and logs the error.
When parsing map text, border cells are treated as sink-side termination candidates, while inner termination symbols are treated as source-side candidates.
Deserializer ignores blank lines and comment lines beginning with # when reading meaningful input.
PipePatterns is a final utility-style constant holder for all rendering characters. It contains the wall character and grouped constants for filled and unfilled arrows and pipe shapes. Rendering logic should rely on these constants instead of hardcoded characters.
StringUtils is a lightweight utility-style class for string helpers and should not be instantiated.
```

# Operation Specifications
DelayBar::countdown
Summary: Decrements the current delay value by 1, representing one round of time passing before water flow begins.
Algorithm: currentValue = currentValue - 1
Related Features: currentValue (int)
Related Classes: None
Input: None
Output: void
Pre-condition: currentValue > 0
Post-condition: currentValue is decreased by 1. If currentValue becomes 0 or negative, water flow can begin.

DelayBar::distance
Summary: Returns the current water flow distance based on the delay bar state.
Algorithm: If currentValue > 0, return 0 (water has not started flowing). Otherwise, return -currentValue (the number of steps since water started).
Related Features: currentValue (int)
Related Classes: None
Input: None
Output: int - the distance water should expand (0 if delay not expired, positive integer otherwise)
Pre-condition: None
Post-condition: Returns 0 if currentValue > 0, otherwise returns -currentValue.

# Requirement
```text
Overall / Domain Description
This is a console pipe-connection game. The game board is a grid surrounded by outer walls. Inside the board there is one source, and on the border there is one sink. The player places pipes from a pipe queue. After an initial delay, water begins to flow through connected pipes.
The board uses zero-based internal array indices. However, index 0 and the last row/column are occupied by the outer wall border. Therefore, the playable area starts from internal index 1 and ends at rows - 2 / cols - 2.
Player-facing coordinates intentionally align with these playable internal indices:
row 1 refers to internal row 1, and column 'A' refers to internal column 1. No row-minus-one or column-minus-one conversion is applied, except that column letters are mapped so that 'A' becomes 1.
Directions include up, down, left, and right. Each direction has a corresponding opposite direction and a unit movement offset(class PA19Helper will help class Direction to provide these functions). Pipe shapes define which directions they connect to. Termination type distinguishes source and sink.

Functional Requirements

Coordinate and Direction
A coordinate stores the internal row and column used directly to access the cell grid. A cell stored at a given grid position should carry the same coordinate value.
Because the outer border occupies index 0, playable cells naturally begin at index 1. This allows user input to align directly with the playable internal grid.
Directions support movement calculations through their unit offsets and can be compared against their opposite direction when checking pipe connectivity.

Game
The game supports placing the current pipe, skipping the current pipe, undoing the latest placement, advancing the water state, checking whether the player has won, checking whether the player has lost, and tracking the number of player steps.
When the player places a pipe, the row value is used directly. The column letter is converted so that 'A' maps to column 1, 'B' maps to column 2, and so on. For example, row 1 and column 'A' target the internal cell at [1][1].
Skipping removes the current pipe from the front of the queue and counts as one step.
Undo restores the latest placed pipe to the front of the queue, clears that pipe from the board, and counts as one step. If there is no previous placement to undo, the operation fails without changing the board.

Map
The map stores cells in a two-dimensional grid with indices from [0..rows-1] and [0..cols-1]. The outermost row and column positions are walls. The playable area is [1..rows-2] by [1..cols-2].
A pipe may be placed only when all of the following are true:
1. The target coordinate is inside the playable area.
2. The target cell is a fillable cell.
3. The target cell does not already contain a pipe.

Cell Family
Cells are parsed from map characters into concrete cell types.
A fillable cell may contain a pipe or be empty. Empty fillable cells render as a dot.
A termination cell represents either the source or the sink. It stores the direction it points toward and whether it has been filled by water.
A wall cell represents the board boundary and renders using the wall character.

Termination Cell Rendering
A termination cell renders as an arrow based on its direction and filled state. Filled and unfilled arrows come from the shared rendering constants.
Both source and sink use their stored pointing direction directly. The direction is not reversed for either type.
Throws IllegalStateException("Invalid pointingTo value!") for unknown direction.

Pipe
A pipe has a shape and a filled state. Its shape determines the directions it connects to.
Supported pipe shapes include horizontal, vertical, the four corner shapes, and cross.
Pipe rendering depends on both shape and filled state. The rendered character should come from the shared rendering constants rather than hardcoded glyphs.
Short pipe codes include HZ, VT, TL, TR, BL, BR, and CR.

Water Flow
At the beginning of water flow, the source is marked as filled.
Water expands outward from the source by distance. Each update increases the reachable fill distance by one.
Water may move from one pipe to an adjacent pipe only when both sides connect to each other: the outgoing direction of one pipe must match the opposite direction of the neighboring pipe.
The filling process follows breadth-first expansion from the source.

Win and Loss Conditions
The player wins if there is a connected path from the source to the sink.
Path checking starts from the source by moving once in the source’s pointing direction. From each pipe, traversal continues through that pipe’s connection directions. The path does not require pipes to already be filled. Reaching the sink means the game is won.
The player loses when a water-flow update fills no new pipes. Loss is checked only after the initial delay has ended and water has actually started advancing.

Pipe Queue
The pipe queue stores upcoming pipes. The player always interacts with the pipe at the front.
When a pipe is consumed, the queue is automatically refilled up to a fixed maximum length using randomly generated pipe shapes.
Undo places the restored pipe back at the front of the queue.

Delay Bar
The delay bar starts with an initial value and decreases once per round.
While the value is still positive, water has not begun flowing. Once the countdown passes zero, the corresponding positive distance indicates how far water should expand from the source.

Cell Stack
The placement history records successfully placed cells in order.
Undo uses the most recent placement. The undo counter represents the number of successful undo actions, not the current size of the placement history.

External / Tool Classes
Pa19Helper is a handwritten helper and assembly class in the pa19 package. It is responsible for constructing core game objects from provided inputs, wiring together the map, pipe queue, delay bar, and placement history. It also centralizes basic parsing and direction utility behavior.
Deserializer is responsible for reading game input from a file and producing runtime game objects. It validates that the input file exists, reads the board size, delay value, map lines, and optional default pipes. If the input ends unexpectedly or an I/O error occurs, it returns no game object and logs the error.
When parsing map text, border cells are treated as sink-side termination candidates, while inner termination symbols are treated as source-side candidates.
Deserializer ignores blank lines and comment lines beginning with # when reading meaningful input.
PipePatterns is a final utility-style constant holder for all rendering characters. It contains the wall character and grouped constants for filled and unfilled arrows and pipe shapes. Rendering logic should rely on these constants instead of hardcoded characters.
StringUtils is a lightweight utility-style class for string helpers and should not be instantiated.
```

```plantuml
Map --> TerminationCell : sourceCell
Pipe --|> MapElement

TerminationCell --|> Cell
```

# Operation Specifications
PipeQueue::generateNewPipe
Summary: Creates a new random pipe and adds it to the end of the queue.
Algorithm: Randomly select a PipeShape (from the seven possible shapes). Create a new Pipe with that shape and filled=false. Append it to pipeQueue list.
Related Features: pipeQueue (List<Pipe>)
Related Classes: Pipe, PipeShape
Input: None
Output: void
Pre-condition: None
Post-condition: A new random pipe is appended to the end of the queue.

PipeQueue::peek
Summary: Returns the front pipe of the queue without removing it.
Algorithm: Return the first element of pipeQueue list.
Related Features: pipeQueue (List<Pipe>)
Related Classes: Pipe
Input: None
Output: Pipe - the front pipe of the queue
Pre-condition: pipeQueue is not empty
Post-condition: Returns the front pipe without modifying the queue.

PipeQueue::undo
Summary: Restores a pipe to the front of the queue (for undo operations).
Algorithm: Insert the given pipe at index 0 of pipeQueue list.
Related Features: pipeQueue (List<Pipe>)
Related Classes: Pipe
Input: pipe: Pipe - the pipe to restore to the front
Output: void
Pre-condition: pipe is not null
Post-condition: The given pipe is placed at the front of the queue.

PipeQueue::consume
Summary: Removes the front pipe from the queue and refills the queue if necessary.
Algorithm: Remove the first element from pipeQueue list. If the queue size is less than maxGenLength after removal, call generateNewPipe() repeatedly until the queue reaches maxGenLength.
Related Features: pipeQueue (List<Pipe>), maxGenLength (int)
Related Classes: Pipe
Input: None
Output: void
Pre-condition: pipeQueue is not empty
Post-condition: The front pipe is removed, and the queue is refilled to maxGenLength if needed.

# Requirement
```text
Overall / Domain Description
This is a console pipe-connection game. The game board is a grid surrounded by outer walls. Inside the board there is one source, and on the border there is one sink. The player places pipes from a pipe queue. After an initial delay, water begins to flow through connected pipes.
The board uses zero-based internal array indices. However, index 0 and the last row/column are occupied by the outer wall border. Therefore, the playable area starts from internal index 1 and ends at rows - 2 / cols - 2.
Player-facing coordinates intentionally align with these playable internal indices:
row 1 refers to internal row 1, and column 'A' refers to internal column 1. No row-minus-one or column-minus-one conversion is applied, except that column letters are mapped so that 'A' becomes 1.
Directions include up, down, left, and right. Each direction has a corresponding opposite direction and a unit movement offset(class PA19Helper will help class Direction to provide these functions). Pipe shapes define which directions they connect to. Termination type distinguishes source and sink.

Functional Requirements

Coordinate and Direction
A coordinate stores the internal row and column used directly to access the cell grid. A cell stored at a given grid position should carry the same coordinate value.
Because the outer border occupies index 0, playable cells naturally begin at index 1. This allows user input to align directly with the playable internal grid.
Directions support movement calculations through their unit offsets and can be compared against their opposite direction when checking pipe connectivity.

Game
The game supports placing the current pipe, skipping the current pipe, undoing the latest placement, advancing the water state, checking whether the player has won, checking whether the player has lost, and tracking the number of player steps.
When the player places a pipe, the row value is used directly. The column letter is converted so that 'A' maps to column 1, 'B' maps to column 2, and so on. For example, row 1 and column 'A' target the internal cell at [1][1].
Skipping removes the current pipe from the front of the queue and counts as one step.
Undo restores the latest placed pipe to the front of the queue, clears that pipe from the board, and counts as one step. If there is no previous placement to undo, the operation fails without changing the board.

Map
The map stores cells in a two-dimensional grid with indices from [0..rows-1] and [0..cols-1]. The outermost row and column positions are walls. The playable area is [1..rows-2] by [1..cols-2].
A pipe may be placed only when all of the following are true:
1. The target coordinate is inside the playable area.
2. The target cell is a fillable cell.
3. The target cell does not already contain a pipe.

Cell Family
Cells are parsed from map characters into concrete cell types.
A fillable cell may contain a pipe or be empty. Empty fillable cells render as a dot.
A termination cell represents either the source or the sink. It stores the direction it points toward and whether it has been filled by water.
A wall cell represents the board boundary and renders using the wall character.

Termination Cell Rendering
A termination cell renders as an arrow based on its direction and filled state. Filled and unfilled arrows come from the shared rendering constants.
Both source and sink use their stored pointing direction directly. The direction is not reversed for either type.
Throws IllegalStateException("Invalid pointingTo value!") for unknown direction.

Pipe
A pipe has a shape and a filled state. Its shape determines the directions it connects to.
Supported pipe shapes include horizontal, vertical, the four corner shapes, and cross.
Pipe rendering depends on both shape and filled state. The rendered character should come from the shared rendering constants rather than hardcoded glyphs.
Short pipe codes include HZ, VT, TL, TR, BL, BR, and CR.

Water Flow
At the beginning of water flow, the source is marked as filled.
Water expands outward from the source by distance. Each update increases the reachable fill distance by one.
Water may move from one pipe to an adjacent pipe only when both sides connect to each other: the outgoing direction of one pipe must match the opposite direction of the neighboring pipe.
The filling process follows breadth-first expansion from the source.

Win and Loss Conditions
The player wins if there is a connected path from the source to the sink.
Path checking starts from the source by moving once in the source’s pointing direction. From each pipe, traversal continues through that pipe’s connection directions. The path does not require pipes to already be filled. Reaching the sink means the game is won.
The player loses when a water-flow update fills no new pipes. Loss is checked only after the initial delay has ended and water has actually started advancing.

Pipe Queue
The pipe queue stores upcoming pipes. The player always interacts with the pipe at the front.
When a pipe is consumed, the queue is automatically refilled up to a fixed maximum length using randomly generated pipe shapes.
Undo places the restored pipe back at the front of the queue.

Delay Bar
The delay bar starts with an initial value and decreases once per round.
While the value is still positive, water has not begun flowing. Once the countdown passes zero, the corresponding positive distance indicates how far water should expand from the source.

Cell Stack
The placement history records successfully placed cells in order.
Undo uses the most recent placement. The undo counter represents the number of successful undo actions, not the current size of the placement history.

External / Tool Classes
Pa19Helper is a handwritten helper and assembly class in the pa19 package. It is responsible for constructing core game objects from provided inputs, wiring together the map, pipe queue, delay bar, and placement history. It also centralizes basic parsing and direction utility behavior.
Deserializer is responsible for reading game input from a file and producing runtime game objects. It validates that the input file exists, reads the board size, delay value, map lines, and optional default pipes. If the input ends unexpectedly or an I/O error occurs, it returns no game object and logs the error.
When parsing map text, border cells are treated as sink-side termination candidates, while inner termination symbols are treated as source-side candidates.
Deserializer ignores blank lines and comment lines beginning with # when reading meaningful input.
PipePatterns is a final utility-style constant holder for all rendering characters. It contains the wall character and grouped constants for filled and unfilled arrows and pipe shapes. Rendering logic should rely on these constants instead of hardcoded characters.
StringUtils is a lightweight utility-style class for string helpers and should not be instantiated.
```

# Operation Specifications

You will be given a **Requirement**, a **Class Diagram** in PlantUML, and a list of operation specifications. Your task is to correct the specifications that are inconsistent with the requirement.

# Requirement
```text
Overall / Domain Description
This is a console pipe-connection game. The game board is a grid surrounded by outer walls. Inside the board there is one source, and on the border there is one sink. The player places pipes from a pipe queue. After an initial delay, water begins to flow through connected pipes.
The board uses zero-based internal array indices. However, index 0 and the last row/column are occupied by the outer wall border. Therefore, the playable area starts from internal index 1 and ends at rows - 2 / cols - 2.
Player-facing coordinates intentionally align with these playable internal indices:
row 1 refers to internal row 1, and column 'A' refers to internal column 1. No row-minus-one or column-minus-one conversion is applied, except that column letters are mapped so that 'A' becomes 1.
Directions include up, down, left, and right. Each direction has a corresponding opposite direction and a unit movement offset(class PA19Helper will help class Direction to provide these functions). Pipe shapes define which directions they connect to. Termination type distinguishes source and sink.

Functional Requirements

Coordinate and Direction
A coordinate stores the internal row and column used directly to access the cell grid. A cell stored at a given grid position should carry the same coordinate value.
Because the outer border occupies index 0, playable cells naturally begin at index 1. This allows user input to align directly with the playable internal grid.
Directions support movement calculations through their unit offsets and can be compared against their opposite direction when checking pipe connectivity.

Game
The game supports placing the current pipe, skipping the current pipe, undoing the latest placement, advancing the water state, checking whether the player has won, checking whether the player has lost, and tracking the number of player steps.
When the player places a pipe, the row value is used directly. The column letter is converted so that 'A' maps to column 1, 'B' maps to column 2, and so on. For example, row 1 and column 'A' target the internal cell at [1][1].
Skipping removes the current pipe from the front of the queue and counts as one step.
Undo restores the latest placed pipe to the front of the queue, clears that pipe from the board, and counts as one step. If there is no previous placement to undo, the operation fails without changing the board.

Map
The map stores cells in a two-dimensional grid with indices from [0..rows-1] and [0..cols-1]. The outermost row and column positions are walls. The playable area is [1..rows-2] by [1..cols-2].
A pipe may be placed only when all of the following are true:
1. The target coordinate is inside the playable area.
2. The target cell is a fillable cell.
3. The target cell does not already contain a pipe.

Cell Family
Cells are parsed from map characters into concrete cell types.
A fillable cell may contain a pipe or be empty. Empty fillable cells render as a dot.
A termination cell represents either the source or the sink. It stores the direction it points toward and whether it has been filled by water.
A wall cell represents the board boundary and renders using the wall character.

Termination Cell Rendering
A termination cell renders as an arrow based on its direction and filled state. Filled and unfilled arrows come from the shared rendering constants.
Both source and sink use their stored pointing direction directly. The direction is not reversed for either type.
Throws IllegalStateException("Invalid pointingTo value!") for unknown direction.

Pipe
A pipe has a shape and a filled state. Its shape determines the directions it connects to.
Supported pipe shapes include horizontal, vertical, the four corner shapes, and cross.
Pipe rendering depends on both shape and filled state. The rendered character should come from the shared rendering constants rather than hardcoded glyphs.
Short pipe codes include HZ, VT, TL, TR, BL, BR, and CR.

Water Flow
At the beginning of water flow, the source is marked as filled.
Water expands outward from the source by distance. Each update increases the reachable fill distance by one.
Water may move from one pipe to an adjacent pipe only when both sides connect to each other: the outgoing direction of one pipe must match the opposite direction of the neighboring pipe.
The filling process follows breadth-first expansion from the source.

Win and Loss Conditions
The player wins if there is a connected path from the source to the sink.
Path checking starts from the source by moving once in the source’s pointing direction. From each pipe, traversal continues through that pipe’s connection directions. The path does not require pipes to already be filled. Reaching the sink means the game is won.
The player loses when a water-flow update fills no new pipes. Loss is checked only after the initial delay has ended and water has actually started advancing.

Pipe Queue
The pipe queue stores upcoming pipes. The player always interacts with the pipe at the front.
When a pipe is consumed, the queue is automatically refilled up to a fixed maximum length using randomly generated pipe shapes.
Undo places the restored pipe back at the front of the queue.

Delay Bar
The delay bar starts with an initial value and decreases once per round.
While the value is still positive, water has not begun flowing. Once the countdown passes zero, the corresponding positive distance indicates how far water should expand from the source.

Cell Stack
The placement history records successfully placed cells in order.
Undo uses the most recent placement. The undo counter represents the number of successful undo actions, not the current size of the placement history.

External / Tool Classes
Pa19Helper is a handwritten helper and assembly class in the pa19 package. It is responsible for constructing core game objects from provided inputs, wiring together the map, pipe queue, delay bar, and placement history. It also centralizes basic parsing and direction utility behavior.
Deserializer is responsible for reading game input from a file and producing runtime game objects. It validates that the input file exists, reads the board size, delay value, map lines, and optional default pipes. If the input ends unexpectedly or an I/O error occurs, it returns no game object and logs the error.
When parsing map text, border cells are treated as sink-side termination candidates, while inner termination symbols are treated as source-side candidates.
Deserializer ignores blank lines and comment lines beginning with # when reading meaningful input.
PipePatterns is a final utility-style constant holder for all rendering characters. It contains the wall character and grouped constants for filled and unfilled arrows and pipe shapes. Rendering logic should rely on these constants instead of hardcoded characters.
StringUtils is a lightweight utility-style class for string helpers and should not be instantiated.
```

# Operation Specifications
Pipe::getConnections
Summary: Returns the list of directions that this pipe connects to based on its shape.
Algorithm: Switch on shape: HORIZONTAL returns [LEFT, RIGHT]; VERTICAL returns [UP, DOWN]; TOP_LEFT returns [UP, LEFT]; TOP_RIGHT returns [UP, RIGHT]; BOTTOM_LEFT returns [DOWN, LEFT]; BOTTOM_RIGHT returns [DOWN, RIGHT]; CROSS returns [UP, DOWN, LEFT, RIGHT].
Related Features: shape (PipeShape)
Related Classes: Direction, PipeShape
Input: None
Output: List<Direction> - the list of connection directions
Pre-condition: shape is a valid PipeShape value
Post-condition: Returns the appropriate list of directions for the pipe's shape.

# Requirement
```text
Overall / Domain Description
This is a console pipe-connection game. The game board is a grid surrounded by outer walls. Inside the board there is one source, and on the border there is one sink. The player places pipes from a pipe queue. After an initial delay, water begins to flow through connected pipes.
The board uses zero-based internal array indices. However, index 0 and the last row/column are occupied by the outer wall border. Therefore, the playable area starts from internal index 1 and ends at rows - 2 / cols - 2.
Player-facing coordinates intentionally align with these playable internal indices:
row 1 refers to internal row 1, and column 'A' refers to internal column 1. No row-minus-one or column-minus-one conversion is applied, except that column letters are mapped so that 'A' becomes 1.
Directions include up, down, left, and right. Each direction has a corresponding opposite direction and a unit movement offset(class PA19Helper will help class Direction to provide these functions). Pipe shapes define which directions they connect to. Termination type distinguishes source and sink.

Functional Requirements

Coordinate and Direction
A coordinate stores the internal row and column used directly to access the cell grid. A cell stored at a given grid position should carry the same coordinate value.
Because the outer border occupies index 0, playable cells naturally begin at index 1. This allows user input to align directly with the playable internal grid.
Directions support movement calculations through their unit offsets and can be compared against their opposite direction when checking pipe connectivity.

Game
The game supports placing the current pipe, skipping the current pipe, undoing the latest placement, advancing the water state, checking whether the player has won, checking whether the player has lost, and tracking the number of player steps.
When the player places a pipe, the row value is used directly. The column letter is converted so that 'A' maps to column 1, 'B' maps to column 2, and so on. For example, row 1 and column 'A' target the internal cell at [1][1].
Skipping removes the current pipe from the front of the queue and counts as one step.
Undo restores the latest placed pipe to the front of the queue, clears that pipe from the board, and counts as one step. If there is no previous placement to undo, the operation fails without changing the board.

Map
The map stores cells in a two-dimensional grid with indices from [0..rows-1] and [0..cols-1]. The outermost row and column positions are walls. The playable area is [1..rows-2] by [1..cols-2].
A pipe may be placed only when all of the following are true:
1. The target coordinate is inside the playable area.
2. The target cell is a fillable cell.
3. The target cell does not already contain a pipe.

Cell Family
Cells are parsed from map characters into concrete cell types.
A fillable cell may contain a pipe or be empty. Empty fillable cells render as a dot.
A termination cell represents either the source or the sink. It stores the direction it points toward and whether it has been filled by water.
A wall cell represents the board boundary and renders using the wall character.

Termination Cell Rendering
A termination cell renders as an arrow based on its direction and filled state. Filled and unfilled arrows come from the shared rendering constants.
Both source and sink use their stored pointing direction directly. The direction is not reversed for either type.
Throws IllegalStateException("Invalid pointingTo value!") for unknown direction.

Pipe
A pipe has a shape and a filled state. Its shape determines the directions it connects to.
Supported pipe shapes include horizontal, vertical, the four corner shapes, and cross.
Pipe rendering depends on both shape and filled state. The rendered character should come from the shared rendering constants rather than hardcoded glyphs.
Short pipe codes include HZ, VT, TL, TR, BL, BR, and CR.

Water Flow
At the beginning of water flow, the source is marked as filled.
Water expands outward from the source by distance. Each update increases the reachable fill distance by one.
Water may move from one pipe to an adjacent pipe only when both sides connect to each other: the outgoing direction of one pipe must match the opposite direction of the neighboring pipe.
The filling process follows breadth-first expansion from the source.

Win and Loss Conditions
The player wins if there is a connected path from the source to the sink.
Path checking starts from the source by moving once in the source’s pointing direction. From each pipe, traversal continues through that pipe’s connection directions. The path does not require pipes to already be filled. Reaching the sink means the game is won.
The player loses when a water-flow update fills no new pipes. Loss is checked only after the initial delay has ended and water has actually started advancing.

Pipe Queue
The pipe queue stores upcoming pipes. The player always interacts with the pipe at the front.
When a pipe is consumed, the queue is automatically refilled up to a fixed maximum length using randomly generated pipe shapes.
Undo places the restored pipe back at the front of the queue.

Delay Bar
The delay bar starts with an initial value and decreases once per round.
While the value is still positive, water has not begun flowing. Once the countdown passes zero, the corresponding positive distance indicates how far water should expand from the source.

Cell Stack
The placement history records successfully placed cells in order.
Undo uses the most recent placement. The undo counter represents the number of successful undo actions, not the current size of the placement history.

External / Tool Classes
Pa19Helper is a handwritten helper and assembly class in the pa19 package. It is responsible for constructing core game objects from provided inputs, wiring together the map, pipe queue, delay bar, and placement history. It also centralizes basic parsing and direction utility behavior.
Deserializer is responsible for reading game input from a file and producing runtime game objects. It validates that the input file exists, reads the board size, delay value, map lines, and optional default pipes. If the input ends unexpectedly or an I/O error occurs, it returns no game object and logs the error.
When parsing map text, border cells are treated as sink-side termination candidates, while inner termination symbols are treated as source-side candidates.
Deserializer ignores blank lines and comment lines beginning with # when reading meaningful input.
PipePatterns is a final utility-style constant holder for all rendering characters. It contains the wall character and grouped constants for filled and unfilled arrows and pipe shapes. Rendering logic should rely on these constants instead of hardcoded characters.
StringUtils is a lightweight utility-style class for string helpers and should not be instantiated.
```

Related Features: shape (PipeShape)
Related Classes: Direction, PipeShape
Input: None
Output: List<Direction> - the list of connection directions
Pre-condition: shape is a valid PipeShape value
Post-condition: Returns the appropriate list of directions for the pipe's shape.

# Operation Specifications
Game::hasWon
Summary: Checks whether the player has won the game by connecting source to sink.
Algorithm: Return map.checkPath()
Related Features: map (Map)
Related Classes: Map
Input: None
Output: boolean - true if a connected path exists from source to sink, false otherwise
Pre-condition: None
Post-condition: Returns the result of path checking on the current map state.

Game::undoStep
Summary: Undoes the most recent pipe placement, restoring the pipe to the front of the queue.
Algorithm: If cellStack is empty, return false. Otherwise, pop the most recent cell from cellStack, get its coordinate, call map.undo(coord) to clear the pipe, call pipeQueue.undo(pipe) to restore pipe to front, increment numOfSteps, and return true.
Related Features: cellStack (CellStack), map (Map), pipeQueue (PipeQueue), numOfSteps (int)
Related Classes: CellStack, Map, PipeQueue, FillableCell, Pipe, Coordinate
Input: None
Output: boolean - true if undo was successful, false if no placement to undo
Pre-condition: None
Post-condition: If successful, the latest placed pipe is removed from board and restored to queue front, step count increases.

Game::skipPipe
Summary: Removes the current pipe from the front of the queue without placing it.
Algorithm: Call pipeQueue.consume(). Increment numOfSteps by 1.
Related Features: pipeQueue (PipeQueue), numOfSteps (int)
Related Classes: PipeQueue
Input: None
Output: void
Pre-condition: pipeQueue is not empty
Post-condition: The front pipe is removed from the queue, and step count increases by 1.

Game::updateState
Summary: Advances the game state by one round: updates delay bar and water flow.
Algorithm: Call delayBar.countdown(). If delayBar.currentValue <= 0, call map.fillTiles(delayBar.distance()).
Related Features: delayBar (DelayBar), map (Map)
Related Classes: DelayBar, Map
Input: None
Output: void
Pre-condition: None
Post-condition: Delay bar is decremented. If delay expired, water expands to the current distance.

Game::hasLost
Summary: Checks whether the player has lost the game.
Algorithm: Return map.hasLost() && delayBar.currentValue <= 0 (loss only counts after water has started flowing).
Related Features: map (Map), delayBar (DelayBar)
Related Classes: Map, DelayBar
Input: None
Output: boolean - true if the player has lost, false otherwise
Pre-condition: None
Post-condition: Returns true if water has started flowing and a water update filled no new pipes.

Game::placePipe
Summary: Attempts to place the current pipe from the queue onto the board at the specified position.
Algorithm: Convert column letter to internal index (A=1, B=2, ...). Get current pipe from pipeQueue.peek(). Call map.tryPlacePipe(row, col, pipe). If successful, consume the pipe from queue, increment numOfSteps, push the cell onto cellStack, and return true. Otherwise return false.
Related Features: pipeQueue (PipeQueue), map (Map), numOfSteps (int), cellStack (CellStack)
Related Classes: PipeQueue, Map, CellStack, Pipe
Input: row: int (1-based playable row), col: char (letter A-Z mapping to 1-26)
Output: boolean - true if placement was successful, false otherwise
Pre-condition: row and col map to a valid playable cell coordinate
Post-condition: If successful, pipe is placed on the map, queue is consumed, step count increases, cell is recorded in stack.

You will be given a **Requirement**, a **Class Diagram** in PlantUML, and a list of operation specifications. Your task is to correct the specifications that are inconsistent with the requirement.

An operation specification must describe the following sections about the operation:
1. Summary: the summary of functionality;
2. Algorithm: algorithm or pseudo code;
3. Related Features: a list of structural or behavior features within this class that shall be accessed;
4. Related Classes: a list of classes and data types defined in **Class Diagram** that shall be accessed, in the format of `Related Classes: ClsA, CLsB, ...` or `Related Classes: None`;
5. Input: the input parameters, including the meaning, the format, and the value ranges if necessary;
6. Output: output value, including the meaning, the format, and the value ranges if necessary;
7. Pre-condition: the condition that the system and the input must satisfy before the operation is executed;
8. Post-condition: the condition that the system and the output must satisfy after the operation is executed.

Finish this task by following the guidelines below.
1. Read the requirement and the class diagram.
2. For each operation specification, determine whether it is complete and consistent with the requirement.
3. If there is any error, correct the erroneous specification.
4. Follow the specification format. Output changed specifications only; OMIT unchanged specifications.

# Requirement
```text
Overall / Domain Description
This is a console pipe-connection game. The game board is a grid surrounded by outer walls. Inside the board there is one source, and on the border there is one sink. The player places pipes from a pipe queue. After an initial delay, water begins to flow through connected pipes.
The board uses zero-based internal array indices. However, index 0 and the last row/column are occupied by the outer wall border. Therefore, the playable area starts from internal index 1 and ends at rows - 2 / cols - 2.
Player-facing coordinates intentionally align with these playable internal indices:
row 1 refers to internal row 1, and column 'A' refers to internal column 1. No row-minus-one or column-minus-one conversion is applied, except that column letters are mapped so that 'A' becomes 1.
Directions include up, down, left, and right. Each direction has a corresponding opposite direction and a unit movement offset(class PA19Helper will help class Direction to provide these functions). Pipe shapes define which directions they connect to. Termination type distinguishes source and sink.

Functional Requirements

Coordinate and Direction
A coordinate stores the internal row and column used directly to access the cell grid. A cell stored at a given grid position should carry the same coordinate value.
Because the outer border occupies index 0, playable cells naturally begin at index 1. This allows user input to align directly with the playable internal grid.
Directions support movement calculations through their unit offsets and can be compared against their opposite direction when checking pipe connectivity.

Game
The game supports placing the current pipe, skipping the current pipe, undoing the latest placement, advancing the water state, checking whether the player has won, checking whether the player has lost, and tracking the number of player steps.
When the player places a pipe, the row value is used directly. The column letter is converted so that 'A' maps to column 1, 'B' maps to column 2, and so on. For example, row 1 and column 'A' target the internal cell at [1][1].
Skipping removes the current pipe from the front of the queue and counts as one step.
Undo restores the latest placed pipe to the front of the queue, clears that pipe from the board, and counts as one step. If there is no previous placement to undo, the operation fails without changing the board.

Map
The map stores cells in a two-dimensional grid with indices from [0..rows-1] and [0..cols-1]. The outermost row and column positions are walls. The playable area is [1..rows-2] by [1..cols-2].
A pipe may be placed only when all of the following are true:
1. The target coordinate is inside the playable area.
2. The target cell is a fillable cell.
3. The target cell does not already contain a pipe.

Cell Family
Cells are parsed from map characters into concrete cell types.
A fillable cell may contain a pipe or be empty. Empty fillable cells render as a dot.
A termination cell represents either the source or the sink. It stores the direction it points toward and whether it has been filled by water.
A wall cell represents the board boundary and renders using the wall character.

Termination Cell Rendering
A termination cell renders as an arrow based on its direction and filled state. Filled and unfilled arrows come from the shared rendering constants.
Both source and sink use their stored pointing direction directly. The direction is not reversed for either type.
Throws IllegalStateException("Invalid pointingTo value!") for unknown direction.

Pipe
A pipe has a shape and a filled state. Its shape determines the directions it connects to.
Supported pipe shapes include horizontal, vertical, the four corner shapes, and cross.
Pipe rendering depends on both shape and filled state. The rendered character should come from the shared rendering constants rather than hardcoded glyphs.
Short pipe codes include HZ, VT, TL, TR, BL, BR, and CR.

Water Flow
At the beginning of water flow, the source is marked as filled.
Water expands outward from the source by distance. Each update increases the reachable fill distance by one.
Water may move from one pipe to an adjacent pipe only when both sides connect to each other: the outgoing direction of one pipe must match the opposite direction of the neighboring pipe.
The filling process follows breadth-first expansion from the source.

Win and Loss Conditions
The player wins if there is a connected path from the source to the sink.
Path checking starts from the source by moving once in the source’s pointing direction. From each pipe, traversal continues through that pipe’s connection directions. The path does not require pipes to already be filled. Reaching the sink means the game is won.
The player loses when a water-flow update fills no new pipes. Loss is checked only after the initial delay has ended and water has actually started advancing.

Pipe Queue
The pipe queue stores upcoming pipes. The player always interacts with the pipe at the front.
When a pipe is consumed, the queue is automatically refilled up to a fixed maximum length using randomly generated pipe shapes.
Undo places the restored pipe back at the front of the queue.

Delay Bar
The delay bar starts with an initial value and decreases once per round.
While the value is still positive, water has not begun flowing. Once the countdown passes zero, the corresponding positive distance indicates how far water should expand from the source.

Cell Stack
The placement history records successfully placed cells in order.
Undo uses the most recent placement. The undo counter represents the number of successful undo actions, not the current size of the placement history.

External / Tool Classes
Pa19Helper is a handwritten helper and assembly class in the pa19 package. It is responsible for constructing core game objects from provided inputs, wiring together the map, pipe queue, delay bar, and placement history. It also centralizes basic parsing and direction utility behavior.
Deserializer is responsible for reading game input from a file and producing runtime game objects. It validates that the input file exists, reads the board size, delay value, map lines, and optional default pipes. If the input ends unexpectedly or an I/O error occurs, it returns no game object and logs the error.
When parsing map text, border cells are treated as sink-side termination candidates, while inner termination symbols are treated as source-side candidates.
Deserializer ignores blank lines and comment lines beginning with # when reading meaningful input.
PipePatterns is a final utility-style constant holder for all rendering characters. It contains the wall character and grouped constants for filled and unfilled arrows and pipe shapes. Rendering logic should rely on these constants instead of hardcoded characters.
StringUtils is a lightweight utility-style class for string helpers and should not be instantiated.
```

# Operation Specifications
Game::hasWon
Summary: Checks whether the player has won the game by connecting source to sink.
Algorithm: Return map.checkPath()
Related Features: map (Map)
Related Classes: Map
Input: None
Output: boolean - true if a connected path exists from source to sink, false otherwise
Pre-condition: None
Post-condition: Returns the result of path checking on the current map state.

Game::undoStep
Summary: Undoes the most recent pipe placement, restoring the pipe to the front of the queue.
Algorithm: If cellStack is empty, return false. Otherwise, pop the most recent cell from cellStack, get its coordinate, call map.undo(coord) to clear the pipe, call pipeQueue.undo(pipe) to restore pipe to front, increment numOfSteps, and return true.
Related Features: cellStack (CellStack), map (Map), pipeQueue (PipeQueue), numOfSteps (int)
Related Classes: CellStack, Map, PipeQueue, FillableCell, Pipe, Coordinate
Input: None
Output: boolean - true if undo was successful, false if no placement to undo
Pre-condition: None
Post-condition: If successful, the latest placed pipe is removed from board and restored to queue front, step count increases.

Game::skipPipe
Summary: Removes the current pipe from the front of the queue without placing it.
Algorithm: Call pipeQueue.consume(). Increment numOfSteps by 1.
Related Features: pipeQueue (PipeQueue), numOfSteps (int)
Related Classes: PipeQueue
Input: None
Output: void
Pre-condition: pipeQueue is not empty
Post-condition: The front pipe is removed from the queue, and step count increases by 1.

Game::updateState
Summary: Advances the game state by one round: updates delay bar and water flow.
Algorithm: Call delayBar.countdown(). If delayBar.currentValue <= 0, call map.fillTiles(delayBar.distance()).
Related Features: delayBar (DelayBar), map (Map)
Related Classes: DelayBar, Map
Input: None
Output: void
Pre-condition: None
Post-condition: Delay bar is decremented. If delay expired, water expands to the current distance.

Game::hasLost
Summary: Checks whether the player has lost the game.
Algorithm: Return map.hasLost() && delayBar.currentValue <= 0 (loss only counts after water has started flowing).
Related Features: map (Map), delayBar (DelayBar)
Related Classes: Map, DelayBar
Input: None
Output: boolean - true if the player has lost, false otherwise
Pre-condition: None
Post-condition: Returns true if water has started flowing and a water update filled no new pipes.

Game::placePipe
Summary: Attempts to place the current pipe from the queue onto the board at the specified position.
Algorithm: Convert column letter to internal index (A=1, B=2, ...). Get current pipe from pipeQueue.peek(). Call map.tryPlacePipe(row, col, pipe). If successful, consume the pipe from queue, increment numOfSteps, push the cell onto cellStack, and return true. Otherwise return false.
Related Features: pipeQueue (PipeQueue), map (Map), numOfSteps (int), cellStack (CellStack)
Related Classes: PipeQueue, Map, CellStack, Pipe
Input: row: int (1-based playable row), col: char (letter A-Z mapping to 1-26)
Output: boolean - true if placement was successful, false otherwise
Pre-condition: row and col map to a valid playable cell coordinate
Post-condition: If successful, pipe is placed on the map, queue is consumed, step count increases, cell is recorded in stack.

# Operation Specifications
Game::hasWon
Summary: Checks whether the player has won the game by connecting source to sink.
Algorithm: Return map.checkPath()
Related Features: map (Map)
Related Classes: Map
Input: None
Output: boolean - true if a connected path exists from source to sink, false otherwise
Pre-condition: None
Post-condition: Returns the result of path checking on the current map state.

Game::undoStep
Summary: Undoes the most recent pipe placement, restoring the pipe to the front of the queue.
Algorithm: If cellStack is empty, return false. Otherwise, pop the most recent cell from cellStack, get its coordinate, call map.undo(coord) to clear the pipe, call pipeQueue.undo(pipe) to restore pipe to front, increment numOfSteps, and return true.
Related Features: cellStack (CellStack), map (Map), pipeQueue (PipeQueue), numOfSteps (int)
Related Classes: CellStack, Map, PipeQueue, FillableCell, Pipe, Coordinate
Input: None

# Requirement
```text
Overall / Domain Description
This is a console pipe-connection game. The game board is a grid surrounded by outer walls. Inside the board there is one source, and on the border there is one sink. The player places pipes from a pipe queue. After an initial delay, water begins to flow through connected pipes.
The board uses zero-based internal array indices. However, index 0 and the last row/column are occupied by the outer wall border. Therefore, the playable area starts from internal index 1 and ends at rows - 2 / cols - 2.
Player-facing coordinates intentionally align with these playable internal indices:
row 1 refers to internal row 1, and column 'A' refers to internal column 1. No row-minus-one or column-minus-one conversion is applied, except that column letters are mapped so that 'A' becomes 1.
Directions include up, down, left, and right. Each direction has a corresponding opposite direction and a unit movement offset(class PA19Helper will help class Direction to provide these functions). Pipe shapes define which directions they connect to. Termination type distinguishes source and sink.

Functional Requirements

Coordinate and Direction
A coordinate stores the internal row and column used directly to access the cell grid. A cell stored at a given grid position should carry the same coordinate value.
Because the outer border occupies index 0, playable cells naturally begin at index 1. This allows user input to align directly with the playable internal grid.
Directions support movement calculations through their unit offsets and can be compared against their opposite direction when checking pipe connectivity.

Game
The game supports placing the current pipe, skipping the current pipe, undoing the latest placement, advancing the water state, checking whether the player has won, checking whether the player has lost, and tracking the number of player steps.
When the player places a pipe, the row value is used directly. The column letter is converted so that 'A' maps to column 1, 'B' maps to column 2, and so on. For example, row 1 and column 'A' target the internal cell at [1][1].
Skipping removes the current pipe from the front of the queue and counts as one step.
Undo restores the latest placed pipe to the front of the queue, clears that pipe from the board, and counts as one step. If there is no previous placement to undo, the operation fails without changing the board.

Map
The map stores cells in a two-dimensional grid with indices from [0..rows-1] and [0..cols-1]. The outermost row and column positions are walls. The playable area is [1..rows-2] by [1..cols-2].
A pipe may be placed only when all of the following are true:
1. The target coordinate is inside the playable area.
2. The target cell is a fillable cell.
3. The target cell does not already contain a pipe.

Cell Family
Cells are parsed from map characters into concrete cell types.
A fillable cell may contain a pipe or be empty. Empty fillable cells render as a dot.
A termination cell represents either the source or the sink. It stores the direction it points toward and whether it has been filled by water.
A wall cell represents the board boundary and renders using the wall character.

Termination Cell Rendering
A termination cell renders as an arrow based on its direction and filled state. Filled and unfilled arrows come from the shared rendering constants.
Both source and sink use their stored pointing direction directly. The direction is not reversed for either type.
Throws IllegalStateException("Invalid pointingTo value!") for unknown direction.

Pipe
A pipe has a shape and a filled state. Its shape determines the directions it connects to.
Supported pipe shapes include horizontal, vertical, the four corner shapes, and cross.
Pipe rendering depends on both shape and filled state. The rendered character should come from the shared rendering constants rather than hardcoded glyphs.
Short pipe codes include HZ, VT, TL, TR, BL, BR, and CR.

Water Flow
At the beginning of water flow, the source is marked as filled.
Water expands outward from the source by distance. Each update increases the reachable fill distance by one.
Water may move from one pipe to an adjacent pipe only when both sides connect to each other: the outgoing direction of one pipe must match the opposite direction of the neighboring pipe.
The filling process follows breadth-first expansion from the source.

Win and Loss Conditions
The player wins if there is a connected path from the source to the sink.
Path checking starts from the source by moving once in the source’s pointing direction. From each pipe, traversal continues through that pipe’s connection directions. The path does not require pipes to already be filled. Reaching the sink means the game is won.
The player loses when a water-flow update fills no new pipes. Loss is checked only after the initial delay has ended and water has actually started advancing.

Pipe Queue
The pipe queue stores upcoming pipes. The player always interacts with the pipe at the front.
When a pipe is consumed, the queue is automatically refilled up to a fixed maximum length using randomly generated pipe shapes.
Undo places the restored pipe back at the front of the queue.

Delay Bar
The delay bar starts with an initial value and decreases once per round.
While the value is still positive, water has not begun flowing. Once the countdown passes zero, the corresponding positive distance indicates how far water should expand from the source.

Cell Stack
The placement history records successfully placed cells in order.
Undo uses the most recent placement. The undo counter represents the number of successful undo actions, not the current size of the placement history.

External / Tool Classes
Pa19Helper is a handwritten helper and assembly class in the pa19 package. It is responsible for constructing core game objects from provided inputs, wiring together the map, pipe queue, delay bar, and placement history. It also centralizes basic parsing and direction utility behavior.
Deserializer is responsible for reading game input from a file and producing runtime game objects. It validates that the input file exists, reads the board size, delay value, map lines, and optional default pipes. If the input ends unexpectedly or an I/O error occurs, it returns no game object and logs the error.
When parsing map text, border cells are treated as sink-side termination candidates, while inner termination symbols are treated as source-side candidates.
Deserializer ignores blank lines and comment lines beginning with # when reading meaningful input.
PipePatterns is a final utility-style constant holder for all rendering characters. It contains the wall character and grouped constants for filled and unfilled arrows and pipe shapes. Rendering logic should rely on these constants instead of hardcoded characters.
StringUtils is a lightweight utility-style class for string helpers and should not be instantiated.
```

```text
PipePatterns is a final utility-style constant holder for all rendering characters. It contains the wall character and grouped constants for filled and unfilled arrows and pipe shapes. Rendering logic should rely on these constants instead of hardcoded characters.
StringUtils is a lightweight utility-style class for string helpers and should not be instantiated.
```

# Operation Specifications
Map::tryPlacePipe
Summary: Attempts to place a pipe at the specified row and column coordinate.
Algorithm: Validate that row is between 1 and rows-2, col is between 1 and cols-2. Check that the cell at that coordinate is a FillableCell and has no pipe. If valid, set the cell's pipe to the given pipe and return true. Otherwise return false.
Related Features: cell (cellarray), rows (int), cols (int)
Related Classes: FillableCell, Pipe, Coordinate
Input: row: int (internal row index), col: int (internal column index), pipe: Pipe - the pipe to place
Output: boolean - true if placement was successful, false otherwise
Pre-condition: row and col are valid internal indices
Post-condition: If successful, the specified cell now contains the given pipe.

Map::fillTiles
Summary: Fills pipes with water up to the specified distance from the source using BFS.
Algorithm: If distance == 0, call fillBeginTile() to mark source as filled. Otherwise, for each coordinate in filledTiles from previous step, examine neighbors in the directions the pipe at that coordinate connects. If neighbor pipe exists and connects back (opposite direction match) and is not already filled, mark it as filled and add to new filledTiles list. Update filledTiles with the new list. Update prevFilledDistance to current distance. Track number of newly filled tiles.
Related Features: filledTiles (List<Coordinate>), sourceCell (TerminationCell), prevFilledDistance (int), prevFilledTiles (int), cell (cellarray)
Related Classes: Coordinate, TerminationCell, Pipe, Direction, Pa19Helper
Input: distance: int - the current water flow distance (non-negative)
Output: void
Pre-condition: distance >= 0, sourceCell is defined
Post-condition: Water fills pipes reachable within the given distance from source according to pipe connectivity.

Map::hasLost
Summary: Checks if the player has lost due to no new pipes being filled during a water update.
Algorithm: If prevFilledDistance >= 0 and the number of newly filled tiles in the last fillTiles call was 0, return true. Otherwise return false.
Related Features: prevFilledDistance (int), prevFilledTiles (int), filledTiles (List<Coordinate>)
Related Classes: None
Input: None
Output: boolean - true if a water update filled no new pipes, false otherwise
Pre-condition: None
Post-condition: Returns whether the last water expansion added no new tiles.

Map::undo
Summary: Removes the pipe from the specified cell coordinate.
Algorithm: Get the cell at the given coordinate. If it is a FillableCell and has a pipe, remove the pipe (set to null). Otherwise do nothing.
Related Features: cell (cellarray)
Related Classes: FillableCell, Coordinate, Pipe
Input: coord: Coordinate - the position to clear
Output: void
Pre-condition: coord is a valid internal coordinate
Post-condition: The cell at the given coordinate no longer contains a pipe.

# Requirement
```text
Overall / Domain Description
This is a console pipe-connection game. The game board is a grid surrounded by outer walls. Inside the board there is one source, and on the border there is one sink. The player places pipes from a pipe queue. After an initial delay, water begins to flow through connected pipes.
The board uses zero-based internal array indices. However, index 0 and the last row/column are occupied by the outer wall border. Therefore, the playable area starts from internal index 1 and ends at rows - 2 / cols - 2.
Player-facing coordinates intentionally align with these playable internal indices:
row 1 refers to internal row 1, and column 'A' refers to internal column 1. No row-minus-one or column-minus-one conversion is applied, except that column letters are mapped so that 'A' becomes 1.
Directions include up, down, left, and right. Each direction has a corresponding opposite direction and a unit movement offset(class PA19Helper will help class Direction to provide these functions). Pipe shapes define which directions they connect to. Termination type distinguishes source and sink.

Functional Requirements

Coordinate and Direction
A coordinate stores the internal row and column used directly to access the cell grid. A cell stored at a given grid position should carry the same coordinate value.
Because the outer border occupies index 0, playable cells naturally begin at index 1. This allows user input to align directly with the playable internal grid.
Directions support movement calculations through their unit offsets and can be compared against their opposite direction when checking pipe connectivity.

Game
The game supports placing the current pipe, skipping the current pipe, undoing the latest placement, advancing the water state, checking whether the player has won, checking whether the player has lost, and tracking the number of player steps.
When the player places a pipe, the row value is used directly. The column letter is converted so that 'A' maps to column 1, 'B' maps to column 2, and so on. For example, row 1 and column 'A' target the internal cell at [1][1].
Skipping removes the current pipe from the front of the queue and counts as one step.
Undo restores the latest placed pipe to the front of the queue, clears that pipe from the board, and counts as one step. If there is no previous placement to undo, the operation fails without changing the board.

Map
The map stores cells in a two-dimensional grid with indices from [0..rows-1] and [0..cols-1]. The outermost row and column positions are walls. The playable area is [1..rows-2] by [1..cols-2].
A pipe may be placed only when all of the following are true:
1. The target coordinate is inside the playable area.
2. The target cell is a fillable cell.
3. The target cell does not already contain a pipe.

Cell Family
Cells are parsed from map characters into concrete cell types.
A fillable cell may contain a pipe or be empty. Empty fillable cells render as a dot.
A termination cell represents either the source or the sink. It stores the direction it points toward and whether it has been filled by water.
A wall cell represents the board boundary and renders using the wall character.

Termination Cell Rendering
A termination cell renders as an arrow based on its direction and filled state. Filled and unfilled arrows come from the shared rendering constants.
Both source and sink use their stored pointing direction directly. The direction is not reversed for either type.
Throws IllegalStateException("Invalid pointingTo value!") for unknown direction.

Pipe
A pipe has a shape and a filled state. Its shape determines the directions it connects to.
Supported pipe shapes include horizontal, vertical, the four corner shapes, and cross.
Pipe rendering depends on both shape and filled state. The rendered character should come from the shared rendering constants rather than hardcoded glyphs.
Short pipe codes include HZ, VT, TL, TR, BL, BR, and CR.

Water Flow
At the beginning of water flow, the source is marked as filled.
Water expands outward from the source by distance. Each update increases the reachable fill distance by one.
Water may move from one pipe to an adjacent pipe only when both sides connect to each other: the outgoing direction of one pipe must match the opposite direction of the neighboring pipe.
The filling process follows breadth-first expansion from the source.

Win and Loss Conditions
The player wins if there is a connected path from the source to the sink.
Path checking starts from the source by moving once in the source’s pointing direction. From each pipe, traversal continues through that pipe’s connection directions. The path does not require pipes to already be filled. Reaching the sink means the game is won.
The player loses when a water-flow update fills no new pipes. Loss is checked only after the initial delay has ended and water has actually started advancing.

Pipe Queue
The pipe queue stores upcoming pipes. The player always interacts with the pipe at the front.
When a pipe is consumed, the queue is automatically refilled up to a fixed maximum length using randomly generated pipe shapes.
Undo places the restored pipe back at the front of the queue.

Delay Bar
The delay bar starts with an initial value and decreases once per round.
While the value is still positive, water has not begun flowing. Once the countdown passes zero, the corresponding positive distance indicates how far water should expand from the source.

Cell Stack
The placement history records successfully placed cells in order.
Undo uses the most recent placement. The undo counter represents the number of successful undo actions, not the current size of the placement history.

External / Tool Classes
Pa19Helper is a handwritten helper and assembly class in the pa19 package. It is responsible for constructing core game objects from provided inputs, wiring together the map, pipe queue, delay bar, and placement history. It also centralizes basic parsing and direction utility behavior.
Deserializer is responsible for reading game input from a file and producing runtime game objects. It validates that the input file exists, reads the board size, delay value, map lines, and optional default pipes. If the input ends unexpectedly or an I/O error occurs, it returns no game object and logs the error.
When parsing map text, border cells are treated as sink-side termination candidates, while inner termination symbols are treated as source-side candidates.
Deserializer ignores blank lines and comment lines beginning with # when reading meaningful input.
PipePatterns is a final utility-style constant holder for all rendering characters. It contains the wall character and grouped constants for filled and unfilled arrows and pipe shapes. Rendering logic should rely on these constants instead of hardcoded characters.
StringUtils is a lightweight utility-style class for string helpers and should not be instantiated.
```

    if (getCellStack().getStack().isEmpty())
    {
      return false;
    }
    FillableCell cell = getCellStack().pop();
    Coordinate coord = cell.getCoord();
    Pipe pipe = cell.getPipe();
    getMap().undo(coord);
    getPipeQueue().undo(pipe);
    setNumOfSteps(getNumOfSteps() + 1);
    return true;
  }

## EMF Coding Style
- When possible, call getter/setter methods to access field values. Do not read/write raw fields derived from the class diagram.
- The getter of a boolean attribute `bv` looks like `isBv()`, e.g., `isIsTrue()` for `isTrue`.
- When possibe, use the creation factory for object creation.
- To create an EList instance, import and use `org.eclipse.emf.common.util.BasicEList`.

  public Pipe generateNewPipe()
  {
    Pipe newPipe = Pa19Factory.eINSTANCE.createPipe();
    // Randomly pick a shape from the seven possible shapes
    int randomIndex = (int)(Math.random() * PipeShape.VALUES.size());
    newPipe.setShape(PipeShape.VALUES.get(randomIndex));
    newPipe.setFilled(false);
    getPipeQueue().add(newPipe);
    return newPipe;
  }

If neighbor pipe exists and connects back (the outgoing direction of one pipe matches the opposite direction of the neighboring pipe) and is not already filled, mark it as filled and add to new filledTiles list. Update filledTiles with the new list. Update prevFilledDistance to current distance. Track number of newly filled tiles.
```java
   * Related Features: filledTiles (List<Coordinate>), sourceCell (TerminationCell), prevFilledDistance (int), prevFilledTiles (int), cell (cellarray)

   * Input: distance: int - the current water flow distance (non-negative)
   * Output: void
   * Pre-condition: distance >= 0, sourceCell is defined and already marked as filled via fillBeginTile()
   * Post-condition: Water fills pipes reachable within the given distance from source according to pipe connectivity. The filledTiles list contains coordinates of all newly filled pipes at this distance.

  {
```

    if (row < 1 || row > getRows() - 2) return false;
    int colIndex = col - 1; // Convert 1-based to 0-based
    if (colIndex < 1 || colIndex > getCols() - 2) return false;

    if (targetCell instanceof FillableCell) {

      if (fillableCell.getPipe() == null) {

        return true;
      }
    }

  public void fillTiles(final int distance)
  {
    if (distance == 0) {
      fillBeginTile();
      // For distance 0, the filledTiles should contain the source cell's coordinate
      // But looking at the algorithm more carefully...
    } else {
      // For each coordinate in filledTiles from previous step
      EList<Coordinate> newFilledTiles = new BasicEList<Coordinate>();
      for (Coordinate coord : getFilledTiles()) {
        Cell cell = getCell()[coord.getRow()][coord.getCol()];
        if (cell instanceof FillableCell) {
          FillableCell fillableCell = (FillableCell) cell;
          Pipe pipe = fillableCell.getPipe();
          if (pipe != null) {
            for (Direction dir : pipe.getConnections()) {
              // Get neighbor coordinate
              Coordinate offset = Pa19Factory.eINSTANCE.createPa19Helper().getOffset(dir);
              int neighborRow = coord.getRow() + offset.getRow();
              int neighborCol = coord.getCol() + offset.getCol();
              // Check bounds
              if (neighborRow >= 0 && neighborRow < getRows() && neighborCol >= 0 && neighborCol < getCols()) {
                Cell neighborCell = getCell()[neighborRow][neighborCol];
                if (neighborCell instanceof FillableCell) {
                  FillableCell neighborFillable = (FillableCell) neighborCell;
                  Pipe neighborPipe = neighborFillable.getPipe();
                  if (neighborPipe != null && !neighborPipe.isFilled()) {
                    // Check if neighbor connects back
                    Direction opposite = Pa19Factory.eINSTANCE.createPa19Helper().getOpposite(dir);
                    if (neighborPipe.getConnections().contains(opposite)) {
                      neighborPipe.setFilled(true);
                      Coordinate neighborCoord = Pa19Factory.eINSTANCE.createCoordinate();
                      neighborCoord.setRow(neighborRow);
                      neighborCoord.setCol(neighborCol);
                      newFilledTiles.add(neighborCoord);
                    }
                  }
                } else if (neighborCell instanceof TerminationCell) {
                  TerminationCell termCell = (TerminationCell) neighborCell;
                  // Check if the termination cell's pointingTo direction connects back
                  Direction opposite = Pa19Factory.eINSTANCE.createPa19Helper().getOpposite(dir);
                  if (termCell.getPointingTo() == opposite && !termCell.isFilled()) {
                    termCell.setFilled(true);
                  }
                }
              }
            }
          }
        }
      }
      // Update filledTiles with the new list
      getFilledTiles().clear();
      getFilledTiles().addAll(newFilledTiles);
      // Update prevFilledDistance
      prevFilledDistance = distance;
      // Track number of newly filled tiles
      prevFilledTiles = newFilledTiles.size();
    }

```java
   * Algorithm: If distance == 0, call fillBeginTile() to mark source as filled.  * Summary: Attempts to place a pipe at the specified row and column coordinate.
```
 * Algorithm: Validate that row is between 1 and rows-2, col is between 1 and cols-2. Check that the cell at that coordinate is a FillableCell and has no pipe. If valid, set the cell's pipe to the given pipe and return true. Otherwise return false.
 * Related Features: cell (cellarray), rows (int), cols (int)
 * Related Classes: FillableCell, Pipe, Coordinate
 * Input: row: int (1-based internal row index), col: char (column letter 'A'-'Z' mapping to 1-26), pipe: Pipe - the pipe to place
 * Output: boolean - true if placement was successful, false otherwise
 * Pre-condition: The coordinate derived from row and col is within the playable area (row between 1 and rows-2, column letter maps to column index between 1 and cols-2)
 * Post-condition: If successful, the specified FillableCell now contains the given pipe.
 * <!-- end-model-doc -->
 * @model annotation="http://www.ustb.edu.cn/sei/mde/EnhancedCodeGen generated='true'"
 * @generated NOT
 */
public boolean tryPlacePipe(final int row, final int col, final Pipe pipe)
{
    // Validate bounds: row between 1 and rows-2, col between 1 and cols-2
    if (row < 1 || row > getRows() - 2 || col < 1 || col > getCols() - 2) {
        return false;
    }
    // Get the cell at the given coordinate
    Cell[][] cells = getCell();
    Cell cell = cells[row][col];
    // Check if it is a FillableCell and has no pipe
    if (cell instanceof FillableCell) {
        FillableCell fillableCell = (FillableCell) cell;
        if (fillableCell.getPipe() == null) {
            fillableCell.setPipe(pipe);
            return true;
        }
    }
    return false;
}
