**checkPath():**

```java
public boolean checkPath()
{
    if (getSourceCell() == null || getSinkCell() == null) {
        return false;
    }
    
    // BFS from sourceCell to sinkCell
    Queue<Coordinate> queue = new LinkedList<Coordinate>();
    Set<String> visited = new HashSet<String>();
    
    Coordinate startCoord = getSourceCell().getCoord();
    queue.add(startCoord);
    visited.add(startCoord.getRow() + "," + startCoord.getCol());
    
    while (!queue.isEmpty()) {
        Coordinate current = queue.poll();
        int row = current.getRow();
        int col = current.getCol();
        
        // Check if we reached the sink cell
        if (row == getSinkCell().getCoord().getRow() && col == getSinkCell().getCoord().getCol()) {
            return true;
        }
        
        Cell currentCell = getCell()[row][col];
        
        // Determine outgoing directions
        EList<Direction> outgoingDirs = new BasicEList<Direction>();
        
        if (currentCell instanceof FillableCell) {
            Pipe currentPipe = ((FillableCell) currentCell).getPipe();
            if (currentPipe != null) {
                outgoingDirs.addAll(currentPipe.getConnections());
            } else {
                continue; // No pipe, can't go anywhere
            }
        } else if (currentCell instanceof TerminationCell) {
            outgoingDirs.add(((TerminationCell) currentCell).getPointingTo());
        } else {
            continue; // Wall or other, can't go through
        }
        
        for (Direction dir : outgoingDirs) {
            int newRow = row;
            int newCol = col;
            switch (dir.getValue()) {
                case Direction.UP_VALUE:
                    newRow--;
                    break;
                case Direction.DOWN_VALUE:
                    newRow++;
                    break;
                case Direction.LEFT_VALUE:
                    newCol--;
                    break;
                case Direction.RIGHT_VALUE:
                    newCol++;
                    break;
            }
            
            // Check bounds
            if (newRow < 0 || newRow >= getRows() || newCol < 0 || newCol >= getCols()) {
                continue;
            }
            
            String key = newRow + "," + newCol;
            if (visited.contains(key)) {
                continue;
            }
            
            Cell neighborCell = getCell()[newRow][newCol];
            
            // Check if neighbor has a pipe (or is a termination cell)
            boolean canEnter = false;
            
            if (neighborCell instanceof FillableCell) {
                Pipe neighborPipe = ((FillableCell) neighborCell).getPipe();
                if (neighborPipe != null) {
                    // Check if neighbor pipe connects back
                    Direction opposite;
                    switch (dir.getValue()) {
                        case Direction.UP_VALUE:
                            opposite = Direction.DOWN;
                            break;
                        case Direction.DOWN_VALUE:
                            opposite = Direction.UP;
                            break;
                        case Direction.LEFT_VALUE:
                            opposite = Direction.RIGHT;
                            break;
                        case Direction.RIGHT_VALUE:
                            opposite = Direction.LEFT;
                            break;
                        default:
                            opposite = null;
                            break;
                    }
                    for (Direction nd : neighborPipe.getConnections()) {
                        if (nd == opposite) {
                            canEnter = true;
                            break;
                        }
                    }
                }
            } else if (neighborCell instanceof TerminationCell) {
                // Can enter termination cell if its pointingTo is opposite of dir
                Direction neighborPointing = ((TerminationCell) neighborCell).getPointingTo();
                Direction opposite;
```

```java
public boolean tryPlacePipe(final int row, final int col, final Pipe pipe) {
    // Validate bounds
    if (row < 0 || row >= getRows() || col < 0 || col >= getCols()) {
        return false;
    }
    // Get cell
    Cell c = getCell()[row][col];
    // Check if fillable
    if (!(c instanceof FillableCell)) {
        return false;
    }
    FillableCell fillableCell = (FillableCell) c;
```

**tryPlacePipe(int row, int col, Pipe pipe):**

```java
public boolean tryPlacePipe(final int row, final int col, final Pipe pipe)
{
    // Validate bounds
    if (row < 0 || row >= getRows() || col < 0 || col >= getCols()) {
        return false;
    }
    // Get the cell at the given position
    Cell c = getCell()[row][col];
    // Check if cell is fillable
    if (!(c instanceof FillableCell)) {
        return false;
    }
    FillableCell fillableCell = (FillableCell) c;
    // Check if cell already contains a pipe
    if (fillableCell.getPipe() != null) {
        return false;
    }
    // Place the pipe
    fillableCell.setPipe(pipe);
    return true;
}
```

```java
public void undo(final Coordinate coord)
{
    // Get cell at coord
    int row = coord.getRow();
    int col = coord.getCol();
    if (row >= 0 && row < getRows() && col >= 0 && col < getCols()) {
        Cell c = getCell()[row][col];
        // If cell is FillableCell, set its pipe to null
        if (c instanceof FillableCell) {
            ((FillableCell) c).setPipe(null);
        }
    }
    // Remove coord from filledTiles if present
    EList<Coordinate> ft = getFilledTiles();
    Coordinate toRemove = null;
    for (Coordinate ftCoord : ft) {
        if (ftCoord.getRow() == coord.getRow() && ftCoord.getCol() == coord.getCol()) {
            toRemove = ftCoord;
            break;
        }
    }
    if (toRemove != null) {
        ft.remove(toRemove);
    }
}
```

**fillTiles(int distance):**

```java
public void fillTiles(final int distance)
{
    // 1. If sourceCell not filled: fillBeginTile()
    if (getSourceCell() != null && !getSourceCell().isFilled()) {
        fillBeginTile();
    }
    
    // 2 & 3. For each filled tile, check all four adjacent cells
    EList<Coordinate> newFilled = new BasicEList<Coordinate>();
    
    for (Coordinate filledCoord : getFilledTiles()) {
        int row = filledCoord.getRow();
        int col = filledCoord.getCol();
        Cell currentCell = getCell()[row][col];
        
        // Determine the outgoing directions from the current cell
        EList<Direction> outgoingDirs = new BasicEList<Direction>();
        
        if (currentCell instanceof FillableCell) {
            Pipe currentPipe = ((FillableCell) currentCell).getPipe();
            if (currentPipe != null) {
                outgoingDirs.addAll(currentPipe.getConnections());
            }
        } else if (currentCell instanceof TerminationCell) {
            outgoingDirs.add(((TerminationCell) currentCell).getPointingTo());
        }
        
        // For each outgoing direction, check the adjacent cell
        for (Direction dir : outgoingDirs) {
            int newRow = row;
            int newCol = col;
            switch (dir.getValue()) {
                case Direction.UP_VALUE:
                    newRow--;
                    break;
                case Direction.DOWN_VALUE:
                    newRow++;
                    break;
                case Direction.LEFT_VALUE:
                    newCol--;
                    break;
                case Direction.RIGHT_VALUE:
                    newCol++;
                    break;
            }
            
            // Check bounds
            if (newRow < 0 || newRow >= getRows() || newCol < 0 || newCol >= getCols()) {
                continue;
            }
            
            // Check if already filled
            boolean alreadyFilled = false;
            for (Coordinate fc : getFilledTiles()) {
                if (fc.getRow() == newRow && fc.getCol() == newCol) {
                    alreadyFilled = true;
                    break;
                }
            }
            if (alreadyFilled) {
                continue;
            }
            
            // Check if also in newFilled
            for (Coordinate nc : newFilled) {
                if (nc.getRow() == newRow && nc.getCol() == newCol) {
                    alreadyFilled = true;
                    break;
                }
            }
            if (alreadyFilled) {
                continue;
            }
            
            Cell neighborCell = getCell()[newRow][newCol];
            
            // Check if neighbor contains a pipe
            Pipe neighborPipe = null;
            if (neighborCell instanceof FillableCell) {
                neighborPipe = ((FillableCell) neighborCell).getPipe();
            }
            
            if (neighborPipe == null) {
                continue;
            }
            
            // Check if the two pipes connect
            // Outgoing direction of current = dir
            // Opposite direction
            Direction opposite;
            switch (dir.getValue()) {
                case Direction.UP_VALUE:
                    opposite = Direction.DOWN;
                    break;
                case Direction.DOWN_VALUE:
                    opposite = Direction.UP;
                    break;
                case Direction.LEFT_VALUE:
                    opposite = Direction.RIGHT;
                    break;
                case Direction.RIGHT_VALUE:
                    opposite = Direction.LEFT;
                    break;
                default:
                    opposite = null;
                    break;
            }
            
            boolean connected = false;
            for (Direction neighborDir : neighborPipe.getConnections()) {
                if (neighborDir == opposite) {
                    connected = true;
                    break;
                }
            }
            
            if (connected) {
                Coordinate newCoord = Pa19Factory.eINSTANCE.createCoordinate();
                newCoord.setRow(newRow);
                newCoord.setCol(newCol);
                newFilled.add(newCoord);
            }
        }
    }
    
    // 4. Add newFilled tiles to filledTiles list
    if (!newFilled.isEmpty()) {
        getFilledTiles().addAll(newFilled);
    }
    
    // 5. Update prevFilledTiles count
    prevFilledTiles = getFilledTiles().size();
```
```java
}
```

**checkPath():**

```java
public boolean checkPath()
{
    if (getSourceCell() == null || getSinkCell() == null) {
        return false;
    }
    
    // BFS from sourceCell to sinkCell
    Queue<Coordinate> queue = new LinkedList<Coordinate>();
    Set<String> visited = new HashSet<String>();
    
    Coordinate startCoord = getSourceCell().getCoord();
    queue.add(startCoord);
    visited.add(startCoord.getRow() + "," + startCoord.getCol());
    
    while (!queue.isEmpty()) {
        Coordinate current = queue.poll();
        int row = current.getRow();
        int col = current.getCol();
        
        // Check if we reached the sink cell
        if (row == getSinkCell().getCoord().getRow() && col == getSinkCell().getCoord().getCol()) {
            return true;
        }
        
        Cell currentCell = getCell()[row][col];
        
        // Determine outgoing directions
        EList<Direction> outgoingDirs = new BasicEList<Direction>();
        
        if (currentCell instanceof FillableCell) {
            Pipe currentPipe = ((FillableCell) currentCell).getPipe();
            if (currentPipe != null) {
                outgoingDirs.addAll(currentPipe.getConnections());
            } else {
                continue; // No pipe, can't go anywhere
            }
        } else if (currentCell instanceof TerminationCell) {
            outgoingDirs.add(((TerminationCell) currentCell).getPointingTo());
        } else {
            continue; // Wall or other, can't go through
        }
        
        for (Direction dir : outgoingDirs) {
            int newRow = row;
            int newCol = col;
            switch (dir.getValue()) {
                case Direction.UP_VALUE:
                    newRow--;
                    break;
                case Direction.DOWN_VALUE:
                    newRow++;
                    break;
                case Direction.LEFT_VALUE:
                    newCol--;
                    break;
                case Direction.RIGHT_VALUE:
                    newCol++;
                    break;
            }
            
            // Check bounds
            if (newRow < 0 || newRow >= getRows() || newCol < 0 || newCol >= getCols()) {
                continue;
            }
            
            String key = newRow + "," + newCol;
            if (visited.contains(key)) {
                continue;
            }
            
            Cell neighborCell = getCell()[newRow][newCol];
            
            // Check if neighbor has a pipe (or is a termination cell)
            boolean canEnter = false;
            
            if (neighborCell instanceof FillableCell) {
                Pipe neighborPipe = ((FillableCell) neighborCell).getPipe();
                if (neighborPipe != null) {
                    // Check if neighbor pipe connects back
                    Direction opposite;
                    switch (dir.getValue()) {
                        case Direction.UP_VALUE:
                            opposite = Direction.DOWN;
                            break;
                        case Direction.DOWN_VALUE:
                            opposite = Direction.UP;
                            break;
                        case Direction.LEFT_VALUE:
                            opposite = Direction.RIGHT;
                            break;
                        case Direction.RIGHT_VALUE:
                            opposite = Direction.LEFT;
                            break;
                        default:
                            opposite = null;
                            break;
                    }
                    for (Direction nd : neighborPipe.getConnections()) {
                        if (nd == opposite) {
                            canEnter = true;
                            break;
                        }
                    }
                }
            } else if (neighborCell instanceof TerminationCell) {
                // Can enter termination cell if its pointingTo is opposite of dir
                Direction neighborPointing = ((TerminationCell) neighborCell).getPointingTo();
                Direction opposite;
                switch (dir.getValue()) {
                    case Direction.UP_VALUE:
                        opposite = Direction.DOWN;
                        break;
                    case Direction.DOWN_VALUE:
                        opposite = Direction.UP;
                        break;
                    case Direction.LEFT_VALUE:
                        opposite = Direction.RIGHT;
                        break;
                    case Direction.RIGHT_VALUE:
                        opposite = Direction.LEFT;
                        break;
                    default:
                        opposite = null;
                        break;
                }
                if (neighborPointing == opposite) {
                    canEnter = true;
                }
            }
            
            if (canEnter) {
                visited.add(key);
                Coordinate nextCoord = Pa19Factory.eINSTANCE.createCoordinate();
                nextCoord.setRow(newRow);
                nextCoord.setCol(newCol);
                queue.add(nextCoord);
            }
```
```java
        }
    }
    
    return false;
```
```java
}
```

```java
public boolean tryPlacePipe(final int row, final int col, final Pipe pipe) {
    // Validate bounds
    if (row < 0 || row >= getRows() || col < 0 || col >= getCols()) {
        return false;
    }
    // Get cell
    Cell c = getCell()[row][col];
    // Check if fillable
    if (!(c instanceof FillableCell)) {
        return false;
    }
    FillableCell fillableCell = (FillableCell) c;
```

**tryPlacePipe(int row, int col, Pipe pipe):**

```java
public boolean tryPlacePipe(final int row, final int col, final Pipe pipe)
{
    // Validate bounds
    if (row < 0 || row >= getRows() || col < 0 || col >= getCols()) {
        return false;
    }
    // Get the cell at the given position
    Cell c = getCell()[row][col];
    // Check if cell is fillable
    if (!(c instanceof FillableCell)) {
        return false;
    }
    FillableCell fillableCell = (FillableCell) c;
    // Check if cell already contains a pipe
    if (fillableCell.getPipe() != null) {
        return false;
    }
    // Place the pipe
    fillableCell.setPipe(pipe);
    return true;
}
```

```java
public void undo(final Coordinate coord)
{
    // Get cell at coord
    int row = coord.getRow();
    int col = coord.getCol();
    if (row >= 0 && row < getRows() && col >= 0 && col < getCols()) {
        Cell c = getCell()[row][col];
        // If cell is FillableCell, set its pipe to null
        if (c instanceof FillableCell) {
            ((FillableCell) c).setPipe(null);
        }
    }
    // Remove coord from filledTiles if present
    EList<Coordinate> ft = getFilledTiles();
    Coordinate toRemove = null;
    for (Coordinate ftCoord : ft) {
        if (ftCoord.getRow() == coord.getRow() && ftCoord.getCol() == coord.getCol()) {
            toRemove = ftCoord;
            break;
        }
    }
    if (toRemove != null) {
        ft.remove(toRemove);
    }
}
```

**fillTiles(int distance):**

```java
public void fillTiles(final int distance)
{
    // 1. If sourceCell not filled: fillBeginTile()
    if (getSourceCell() != null && !getSourceCell().isFilled()) {
        fillBeginTile();
    }
    
    // 2 & 3. For each filled tile, check all four adjacent cells
    EList<Coordinate> newFilled = new BasicEList<Coordinate>();
    
    for (Coordinate filledCoord : getFilledTiles()) {
        int row = filledCoord.getRow();
        int col = filledCoord.getCol();
        Cell currentCell = getCell()[row][col];
        
        // Determine the outgoing directions from the current cell
        EList<Direction> outgoingDirs = new BasicEList<Direction>();
        
        if (currentCell instanceof FillableCell) {
            Pipe currentPipe = ((FillableCell) currentCell).getPipe();
            if (currentPipe != null) {
                outgoingDirs.addAll(currentPipe.getConnections());
            }
        } else if (currentCell instanceof TerminationCell) {
            outgoingDirs.add(((TerminationCell) currentCell).getPointingTo());
        }
        
        // For each outgoing direction, check the adjacent cell
        for (Direction dir : outgoingDirs) {
            int newRow = row;
            int newCol = col;
            switch (dir.getValue()) {
                case Direction.UP_VALUE:
                    newRow--;
                    break;
                case Direction.DOWN_VALUE:
                    newRow++;
                    break;
                case Direction.LEFT_VALUE:
                    newCol--;
                    break;
                case Direction.RIGHT_VALUE:
                    newCol++;
                    break;
            }
            
            // Check bounds
            if (newRow < 0 || newRow >= getRows() || newCol < 0 || newCol >= getCols()) {
                continue;
            }
            
            // Check if already filled
            boolean alreadyFilled = false;
            for (Coordinate fc : getFilledTiles()) {
                if (fc.getRow() == newRow && fc.getCol() == newCol) {
                    alreadyFilled = true;
                    break;
                }
            }
            if (alreadyFilled) {
                continue;
            }
            
            // Check if also in newFilled
            for (Coordinate nc : newFilled) {
                if (nc.getRow() == newRow && nc.getCol() == newCol) {
                    alreadyFilled = true;
                    break;
                }
            }
            if (alreadyFilled) {
                continue;
            }
            
            Cell neighborCell = getCell()[newRow][newCol];
            
            // Check if neighbor contains a pipe
            Pipe neighborPipe = null;
            if (neighborCell instanceof FillableCell) {
                neighborPipe = ((FillableCell) neighborCell).getPipe();
            }
            
            if (neighborPipe == null) {
                continue;
            }
            
            // Check if the two pipes connect
            // Outgoing direction of current = dir
            // Opposite direction
            Direction opposite;
            switch (dir.getValue()) {
                case Direction.UP_VALUE:
                    opposite = Direction.DOWN;
                    break;
                case Direction.DOWN_VALUE:
                    opposite = Direction.UP;
                    break;
                case Direction.LEFT_VALUE:
                    opposite = Direction.RIGHT;
                    break;
                case Direction.RIGHT_VALUE:
                    opposite = Direction.LEFT;
                    break;
                default:
                    opposite = null;
                    break;
            }
            
            boolean connected = false;
            for (Direction neighborDir : neighborPipe.getConnections()) {
                if (neighborDir == opposite) {
                    connected = true;
                    break;
                }
            }
            
            if (connected) {
                Coordinate newCoord = Pa19Factory.eINSTANCE.createCoordinate();
                newCoord.setRow(newRow);
                newCoord.setCol(newCol);
                newFilled.add(newCoord);
            }
        }
    }
    
    // 4. Add newFilled tiles to filledTiles list
    if (!newFilled.isEmpty()) {
        getFilledTiles().addAll(newFilled);
    }
    
    // 5. Update prevFilledTiles count
    prevFilledTiles = getFilledTiles().size();
```
```java
}
```

**checkPath():**

```java
public boolean checkPath()
{
    if (getSourceCell() == null || getSinkCell() == null) {
        return false;
    }
    
    // BFS from sourceCell to sinkCell
    Queue<Coordinate> queue = new LinkedList<Coordinate>();
    Set<String> visited = new HashSet<String>();
    
    Coordinate startCoord = getSourceCell().getCoord();
    queue.add(startCoord);
    visited.add(startCoord.getRow() + "," + startCoord.getCol());
    
    while (!queue.isEmpty()) {
        Coordinate current = queue.poll();
        int row = current.getRow();
        int col = current.getCol();
        
        // Check if we reached the sink cell
        if (row == getSinkCell().getCoord().getRow() && col == getSinkCell().getCoord().getCol()) {
            return true;
        }
        
        Cell currentCell = getCell()[row][col];
        
        // Determine outgoing directions
        EList<Direction> outgoingDirs = new BasicEList<Direction>();
        
        if (currentCell instanceof FillableCell) {
            Pipe currentPipe = ((FillableCell) currentCell).getPipe();
            if (currentPipe != null) {
                outgoingDirs.addAll(currentPipe.getConnections());
            } else {
                continue; // No pipe, can't go anywhere
            }
        } else if (currentCell instanceof TerminationCell) {
            outgoingDirs.add(((TerminationCell) currentCell).getPointingTo());
        } else {
            continue; // Wall or other, can't go through
        }
        
        for (Direction dir : outgoingDirs) {
            int newRow = row;
            int newCol = col;
            switch (dir.getValue()) {
                case Direction.UP_VALUE:
                    newRow--;
                    break;
                case Direction.DOWN_VALUE:
                    newRow++;
                    break;
                case Direction.LEFT_VALUE:
                    newCol--;
                    break;
                case Direction.RIGHT_VALUE:
                    newCol++;
                    break;
            }
            
            // Check bounds
            if (newRow < 0 || newRow >= getRows() || newCol < 0 || newCol >= getCols()) {
                continue;
            }
            
            String key = newRow + "," + newCol;
            if (visited.contains(key)) {
                continue;
            }
            
            Cell neighborCell = getCell()[newRow][newCol];
            
            // Check if neighbor has a pipe (or is a termination cell)
            boolean canEnter = false;
            
            if (neighborCell instanceof FillableCell) {
                Pipe neighborPipe = ((FillableCell) neighborCell).getPipe();
                if (neighborPipe != null) {
                    // Check if neighbor pipe connects back
                    Direction opposite;
                    switch (dir.getValue()) {
                        case Direction.UP_VALUE:
                            opposite = Direction.DOWN;
                            break;
                        case Direction.DOWN_VALUE:
                            opposite = Direction.UP;
                            break;
                        case Direction.LEFT_VALUE:
                            opposite = Direction.RIGHT;
                            break;
                        case Direction.RIGHT_VALUE:
                            opposite = Direction.LEFT;
                            break;
                        default:
                            opposite = null;
                            break;
                    }
                    for (Direction nd : neighborPipe.getConnections()) {
                        if (nd == opposite) {
                            canEnter = true;
                            break;
                        }
                    }
                }
            } else if (neighborCell instanceof TerminationCell) {
                // Can enter termination cell if its pointingTo is opposite of dir
                Direction neighborPointing = ((TerminationCell) neighborCell).getPointingTo();
                Direction opposite;
                switch (dir.getValue()) {
                    case Direction.UP_VALUE:
                        opposite = Direction.DOWN;
                        break;
                    case Direction.DOWN_VALUE:
                        opposite = Direction.UP;
                        break;
                    case Direction.LEFT_VALUE:
                        opposite = Direction.RIGHT;
                        break;
                    case Direction.RIGHT_VALUE:
                        opposite = Direction.LEFT;
                        break;
                    default:
                        opposite = null;
                        break;
                }
                if (neighborPointing == opposite) {
                    canEnter = true;
                }
            }
            
            if (canEnter) {
                visited.add(key);
                Coordinate nextCoord = Pa19Factory.eINSTANCE.createCoordinate();
                nextCoord.setRow(newRow);
                nextCoord.setCol(newCol);
                queue.add(nextCoord);
            }
        }
    }
    
    return false;
}
```

```java
/**
 * <!-- begin-user-doc -->
 * <!-- end-user-doc -->
 * <!-- begin-model-doc -->
 * Summary: Attempts to place a pipe at the specified row and column. Validates that coordinates are within playable area, cell is fillable, and cell does not already contain a pipe.
 * Algorithm:
 *   1. Create Coordinate from row, col
 *   2. Call tryPlacePipe1(coord, pipe)
 * Related Features: cells array, rows, cols fields
 * Related Classes: Coordinate, FillableCell, Pipe
 * Input: row: int, col: int, pipe: Pipe
 * Output: boolean - true if pipe was placed, false otherwise
 * Pre-condition: row and col are valid internal indices
 * Post-condition: If successful, the cell at the given coordinate now contains the pipe
 * <!-- end-model-doc -->
 * @model annotation="http://www.ustb.edu.cn/sei/mde/EnhancedCodeGen generated='true'"
 * @generated NOT
 */
public boolean tryPlacePipe(final int row, final int col, final Pipe pipe)
{
    // Validate bounds
    if (row < 0 || row >= getRows() || col < 0 || col >= getCols()) {
        return false;
    }
    // Get the cell at the given position
    Cell c = getCell()[row][col];
    // Check if cell is fillable
    if (!(c instanceof FillableCell)) {
        return false;
    }
    FillableCell fillableCell = (FillableCell) c;
    // Check if cell already contains a pipe
    if (fillableCell.getPipe() != null) {
        return false;
    }
    // Place the pipe
    fillableCell.setPipe(pipe);
    return true;
```
```java
}

    result.append(cell);
    result.append(')');
    return result.toString();
```
```java
  }

   * Summary: Performs one step of water expansion. Marks source as filled if not already. Then performs breadth-first expansion from all currently filled tiles, expanding outward by one step (to the given distance limit). Tracks number of newly filled tiles for loss detection.
   * Algorithm:
   *   1. If sourceCell not filled: fillBeginTile()
```

- When possible, call getter/setter methods to access field values. Do not read/write raw fields derived from the class diagram.
- The getter of a boolean attribute `bv` looks like `isBv()`, e.g., `isIsTrue()` for `isTrue`.
- When possibe, use the creation factory for object creation.
- To create an EList instance, import and use `org.eclipse.emf.common.util.BasicEList`.

```java
  public String toString()
  {

    result.append(", cell: ");
    result.append(cell);
    result.append(')');
    return result.toString();
```

```java
public void fillTiles(final int distance) {
    // 1. If sourceCell not filled: fillBeginTile()
    if (getSourceCell() != null && !getSourceCell().isFilled()) {
        fillBeginTile();
    }
```

```java
public boolean tryPlacePipe(final int row, final int col, final Pipe pipe) {
    // Validate bounds
    if (row < 0 || row >= getRows() || col < 0 || col >= getCols()) {
        return false;
    }
    // Get cell at position
    Cell targetCell = getCell()[row][col];
    // Check if cell is fillable and doesn't already contain a pipe
    if (targetCell instanceof FillableCell) {
        FillableCell fillableCell = (FillableCell) targetCell;
        if (fillableCell.getPipe() == null) {
            fillableCell.setPipe(pipe);
            return true;
        }
    }
    return false;
}
```

For `fillTiles`:

```java
public void fillTiles(final int distance) {
    // 1. If sourceCell not filled: fillBeginTile()
    if (getSourceCell() != null && !getSourceCell().isFilled()) {
        fillBeginTile();
        // Also add source cell coordinate to filledTiles if not already there
        Coordinate sourceCoord = getSourceCell().getCoord();
        if (!getFilledTiles().contains(sourceCoord)) {
            getFilledTiles().add(sourceCoord);
        }
    }
    
    // 2-3. For each filled tile, check all four adjacent cells
    EList<Coordinate> newFilled = new BasicEList<Coordinate>();
    
    for (Coordinate coord : getFilledTiles()) {
        int r = coord.getRow();
        int c = coord.getCol();
        Cell cell = getCell()[r][c];
        
        // Determine the pipe at this cell
        Pipe currentPipe = null;
        if (cell instanceof FillableCell) {
            currentPipe = ((FillableCell) cell).getPipe();
        } else if (cell instanceof TerminationCell) {
            // Termination cells don't have pipes, they have a pointingTo direction
            // They are the source/sink
            continue; // Skip termination cells for pipe-to-pipe expansion
        }
        
        if (currentPipe == null) continue;
        
        // Check all four directions
        for (Direction dir : currentPipe.getConnections()) {
            // Compute neighbor coordinate
            int nr = r, nc = c;
            switch (dir) {
                case UP: nr = r - 1; break;
                case DOWN: nr = r + 1; break;
                case LEFT: nc = c - 1; break;
                case RIGHT: nc = c + 1; break;
            }
            
            // Check bounds
            if (nr < 0 || nr >= getRows() || nc < 0 || nc >= getCols()) continue;
            
            Cell neighborCell = getCell()[nr][nc];
            Pipe neighborPipe = null;
            if (neighborCell instanceof FillableCell) {
                neighborPipe = ((FillableCell) neighborCell).getPipe();
            }
            
            if (neighborPipe == null) continue;
            
            // Check if neighbor pipe connects back (opposite direction)
            Direction oppositeDir = getOpposite(dir);
            if (neighborPipe.getConnections().contains(oppositeDir)) {
                Coordinate neighborCoord = null;
                // Check if already filled
                boolean alreadyFilled = false;
                for (Coordinate fc : getFilledTiles()) {
                    if (fc.getRow() == nr && fc.getCol() == nc) {
                        alreadyFilled = true;
                        break;
                    }
                }
                
                if (!alreadyFilled) {
                    neighborPipe.setFilled(true);
                    neighborCoord = Pa19Factory.eINSTANCE.createCoordinate();
                    neighborCoord.setRow(nr);
                    neighborCoord.setCol(nc);
                    newFilled.add(neighborCoord);
                }
            }
        }
    }
    
    // 4. Add newFilled tiles to filledTiles list
    getFilledTiles().addAll(newFilled);
    
    // 5. Update prevFilledTiles count
    prevFilledTiles = getFilledTiles().size();
}
```

For `checkPath()`:
```java
public boolean checkPath() {
    // BFS from sourceCell to sinkCell
    if (getSourceCell() == null || getSinkCell() == null) return false;
    
    // Use a set to track visited coordinates
    Set<Coordinate> visited = new HashSet<Coordinate>();
    Queue<Coordinate> queue = new LinkedList<Coordinate>();
    
    Coordinate sourceCoord = getSourceCell().getCoord();
    queue.add(sourceCoord);
    visited.add(sourceCoord);
    
    while (!queue.isEmpty()) {
        Coordinate current = queue.poll();
        
        // Check if we reached the sink
        if (current.getRow() == getSinkCell().getCoord().getRow() && 
            current.getCol() == getSinkCell().getCoord().getCol()) {
            return true;
        }
        
        Cell cell = getCell()[current.getRow()][current.getCol()];
        Pipe pipe = null;
        if (cell instanceof FillableCell) {
            pipe = ((FillableCell) cell).getPipe();
        }
        
        if (pipe == null) continue;
        
        for (Direction dir : pipe.getConnections()) {
            int nr = current.getRow(), nc = current.getCol();
            switch (dir) {
                case UP: nr = current.getRow() - 1; break;
                case DOWN: nr = current.getRow() + 1; break;
                case LEFT: nc = current.getCol() - 1; break;
                case RIGHT: nc = current.getCol() + 1; break;
            }
            
            if (nr < 0 || nr >= getRows() || nc < 0 || nc >= getCols()) continue;
            
            Coordinate next = null;
            // Check if we've visited this
            boolean alreadyVisited = false;
            for (Coordinate v : visited) {
                if (v.getRow() == nr && v.getCol() == nc) {
                    alreadyVisited = true;
                    break;
                }
            }
            if (alreadyVisited) continue;
            
            Cell neighborCell = getCell()[nr][nc];
            Pipe neighborPipe = null;
            if (neighborCell instanceof FillableCell) {
                neighborPipe = ((FillableCell) neighborCell).getPipe();
            }
            
            if (neighborPipe == null) {
                // Check if it's the sink cell
                if (neighborCell instanceof TerminationCell) {
                    // Check if the sink's pointingTo direction matches
                    TerminationCell termCell = (TerminationCell) neighborCell;
                    if (termCell.getType() == TerminationType.SINK) {
                        Direction oppositeDir = getOpposite(dir);
                        if (termCell.getPointingTo() == oppositeDir) {
                            return true;
                        }
                    }
                }
                continue;
            }
            
            // Check if pipes connect
            Direction oppositeDir = getOpposite(dir);
            if (neighborPipe.getConnections().contains(oppositeDir)) {
                next = Pa19Factory.eINSTANCE.createCoordinate();
                next.setRow(nr);
                next.setCol(nc);
                queue.add(next);
                visited.add(next);
            }
        }
    }
    
    return false;
}
```

```java
    // 1. If sourceCell not filled: fillBeginTile()

        fillBeginTile();

            getFilledTiles().add(sourceCoord);

        Cell cell = getCell()[r][c];
        
        // Get the list of directions this cell connects to
        EList<Direction> connections = null;
        if (cell instanceof FillableCell) {

            if (pipe != null) {
                connections = pipe.getConnections();
            }
```

# Requirement
```text
Overall / Domain Description
This is a console pipe-connection game. The game board is a grid surrounded by outer walls. Inside the board there is one source, and on the border there is one sink. The player places pipes from a pipe queue. After an initial delay, water begins to flow through connected pipes.
The board uses zero-based internal array indices. However, index 0 and the last row/column are occupied by the outer wall border. Therefore, the playable area starts from internal index 1 and ends at rows - 2 / cols - 2.
Player-facing coordinates intentionally align with these playable internal indices:
row 1 refers to internal row 1, and column 'A' refers to internal column 1. No row-minus-one or column-minus-one conversion is applied, except that column letters are mapped so that 'A' becomes 1.
Directions include up, down, left, and right. Each direction has a corresponding opposite direction and a unit movement offset(class PA19Helper will help class Direction to provide these functions). Pipe shapes define which directions they connect to. Termination type distinguishes source and sink.

Functional Requirements

Coordinate and Direction
A coordinate stores the internal row and column used directly to access the cell grid. A cell stored at a given grid position should carry the same coordinate value.
Because the outer border occupies index 0, playable cells naturally begin at index 1. This allows user input to align directly with the playable internal grid.
Directions support movement calculations through their unit offsets and can be compared against their opposite direction when checking pipe connectivity.

Game
The game supports placing the current pipe, skipping the current pipe, undoing the latest placement, advancing the water state, checking whether the player has won, checking whether the player has lost, and tracking the number of player steps.
When the player places a pipe, the row value is used directly. The column letter is converted so that 'A' maps to column 1, 'B' maps to column 2, and so on. For example, row 1 and column 'A' target the internal cell at [1][1].
Skipping removes the current pipe from the front of the queue and counts as one step.
Undo restores the latest placed pipe to the front of the queue, clears that pipe from the board, and counts as one step. If there is no previous placement to undo, the operation fails without changing the board.

Map
The map stores cells in a two-dimensional grid with indices from [0..rows-1] and [0..cols-1]. The outermost row and column positions are walls. The playable area is [1..rows-2] by [1..cols-2].
A pipe may be placed only when all of the following are true:
1. The target coordinate is inside the playable area.
2. The target cell is a fillable cell.
3. The target cell does not already contain a pipe.

Cell Family
Cells are parsed from map characters into concrete cell types.
A fillable cell may contain a pipe or be empty. Empty fillable cells render as a dot.
A termination cell represents either the source or the sink. It stores the direction it points toward and whether it has been filled by water.
A wall cell represents the board boundary and renders using the wall character.

Termination Cell Rendering
A termination cell renders as an arrow based on its direction and filled state. Filled and unfilled arrows come from the shared rendering constants.
Both source and sink use their stored pointing direction directly. The direction is not reversed for either type.
Throws IllegalStateException("Invalid pointingTo value!") for unknown direction.

Pipe
A pipe has a shape and a filled state. Its shape determines the directions it connects to.
Supported pipe shapes include horizontal, vertical, the four corner shapes, and cross.
Pipe rendering depends on both shape and filled state. The rendered character should come from the shared rendering constants rather than hardcoded glyphs.
Short pipe codes include HZ, VT, TL, TR, BL, BR, and CR.

Water Flow
At the beginning of water flow, the source is marked as filled.
Water expands outward from the source by distance. Each update increases the reachable fill distance by one.
Water may move from one pipe to an adjacent pipe only when both sides connect to each other: the outgoing direction of one pipe must match the opposite direction of the neighboring pipe.
The filling process follows breadth-first expansion from the source.

Win and Loss Conditions
The player wins if there is a connected path from the source to the sink.
Path checking starts from the source by moving once in the source’s pointing direction. From each pipe, traversal continues through that pipe’s connection directions. The path does not require pipes to already be filled. Reaching the sink means the game is won.
The player loses when a water-flow update fills no new pipes. Loss is checked only after the initial delay has ended and water has actually started advancing.

Pipe Queue
The pipe queue stores upcoming pipes. The player always interacts with the pipe at the front.
When a pipe is consumed, the queue is automatically refilled up to a fixed maximum length using randomly generated pipe shapes.
Undo places the restored pipe back at the front of the queue.

Delay Bar
The delay bar starts with an initial value and decreases once per round.
While the value is still positive, water has not begun flowing. Once the countdown passes zero, the corresponding positive distance indicates how far water should expand from the source.

Cell Stack
The placement history records successfully placed cells in order.
Undo uses the most recent placement. The undo counter represents the number of successful undo actions, not the current size of the placement history.

External / Tool Classes
Pa19Helper is a handwritten helper and assembly class in the pa19 package. It is responsible for constructing core game objects from provided inputs, wiring together the map, pipe queue, delay bar, and placement history. It also centralizes basic parsing and direction utility behavior.
Deserializer is responsible for reading game input from a file and producing runtime game objects. It validates that the input file exists, reads the board size, delay value, map lines, and optional default pipes. If the input ends unexpectedly or an I/O error occurs, it returns no game object and logs the error.
When parsing map text, border cells are treated as sink-side termination candidates, while inner termination symbols are treated as source-side candidates.
Deserializer ignores blank lines and comment lines beginning with # when reading meaningful input.
PipePatterns is a final utility-style constant holder for all rendering characters. It contains the wall character and grouped constants for filled and unfilled arrows and pipe shapes. Rendering logic should rely on these constants instead of hardcoded characters.
StringUtils is a lightweight utility-style class for string helpers and should not be instantiated.
```

# Requirement
```text
Overall / Domain Description
This is a console pipe-connection game. The game board is a grid surrounded by outer walls. Inside the board there is one source, and on the border there is one sink. The player places pipes from a pipe queue. After an initial delay, water begins to flow through connected pipes.
The board uses zero-based internal array indices. However, index 0 and the last row/column are occupied by the outer wall border. Therefore, the playable area starts from internal index 1 and ends at rows - 2 / cols - 2.
Player-facing coordinates intentionally align with these playable internal indices:
row 1 refers to internal row 1, and column 'A' refers to internal column 1. No row-minus-one or column-minus-one conversion is applied, except that column letters are mapped so that 'A' becomes 1.
Directions include up, down, left, and right. Each direction has a corresponding opposite direction and a unit movement offset(class PA19Helper will help class Direction to provide these functions). Pipe shapes define which directions they connect to. Termination type distinguishes source and sink.

Functional Requirements

Coordinate and Direction
A coordinate stores the internal row and column used directly to access the cell grid. A cell stored at a given grid position should carry the same coordinate value.
Because the outer border occupies index 0, playable cells naturally begin at index 1. This allows user input to align directly with the playable internal grid.
Directions support movement calculations through their unit offsets and can be compared against their opposite direction when checking pipe connectivity.

Game
The game supports placing the current pipe, skipping the current pipe, undoing the latest placement, advancing the water state, checking whether the player has won, checking whether the player has lost, and tracking the number of player steps.
When the player places a pipe, the row value is used directly. The column letter is converted so that 'A' maps to column 1, 'B' maps to column 2, and so on. For example, row 1 and column 'A' target the internal cell at [1][1].
Skipping removes the current pipe from the front of the queue and counts as one step.
Undo restores the latest placed pipe to the front of the queue, clears that pipe from the board, and counts as one step. If there is no previous placement to undo, the operation fails without changing the board.

Map
The map stores cells in a two-dimensional grid with indices from [0..rows-1] and [0..cols-1]. The outermost row and column positions are walls. The playable area is [1..rows-2] by [1..cols-2].
A pipe may be placed only when all of the following are true:
1. The target coordinate is inside the playable area.
2. The target cell is a fillable cell.
3. The target cell does not already contain a pipe.

Cell Family
Cells are parsed from map characters into concrete cell types.
A fillable cell may contain a pipe or be empty. Empty fillable cells render as a dot.
A termination cell represents either the source or the sink. It stores the direction it points toward and whether it has been filled by water.
A wall cell represents the board boundary and renders using the wall character.

Termination Cell Rendering
A termination cell renders as an arrow based on its direction and filled state. Filled and unfilled arrows come from the shared rendering constants.
Both source and sink use their stored pointing direction directly. The direction is not reversed for either type.
Throws IllegalStateException("Invalid pointingTo value!") for unknown direction.

Pipe
A pipe has a shape and a filled state. Its shape determines the directions it connects to.
Supported pipe shapes include horizontal, vertical, the four corner shapes, and cross.
Pipe rendering depends on both shape and filled state. The rendered character should come from the shared rendering constants rather than hardcoded glyphs.
Short pipe codes include HZ, VT, TL, TR, BL, BR, and CR.

Water Flow
At the beginning of water flow, the source is marked as filled.
Water expands outward from the source by distance. Each update increases the reachable fill distance by one.
Water may move from one pipe to an adjacent pipe only when both sides connect to each other: the outgoing direction of one pipe must match the opposite direction of the neighboring pipe.
The filling process follows breadth-first expansion from the source.

Win and Loss Conditions
The player wins if there is a connected path from the source to the sink.
Path checking starts from the source by moving once in the source’s pointing direction. From each pipe, traversal continues through that pipe’s connection directions. The path does not require pipes to already be filled. Reaching the sink means the game is won.
The player loses when a water-flow update fills no new pipes. Loss is checked only after the initial delay has ended and water has actually started advancing.

Pipe Queue
The pipe queue stores upcoming pipes. The player always interacts with the pipe at the front.
When a pipe is consumed, the queue is automatically refilled up to a fixed maximum length using randomly generated pipe shapes.
Undo places the restored pipe back at the front of the queue.

Delay Bar
The delay bar starts with an initial value and decreases once per round.
While the value is still positive, water has not begun flowing. Once the countdown passes zero, the corresponding positive distance indicates how far water should expand from the source.

Cell Stack
The placement history records successfully placed cells in order.
Undo uses the most recent placement. The undo counter represents the number of successful undo actions, not the current size of the placement history.

External / Tool Classes
Pa19Helper is a handwritten helper and assembly class in the pa19 package. It is responsible for constructing core game objects from provided inputs, wiring together the map, pipe queue, delay bar, and placement history. It also centralizes basic parsing and direction utility behavior.
Deserializer is responsible for reading game input from a file and producing runtime game objects. It validates that the input file exists, reads the board size, delay value, map lines, and optional default pipes. If the input ends unexpectedly or an I/O error occurs, it returns no game object and logs the error.
When parsing map text, border cells are treated as sink-side termination candidates, while inner termination symbols are treated as source-side candidates.
Deserializer ignores blank lines and comment lines beginning with # when reading meaningful input.
PipePatterns is a final utility-style constant holder for all rendering characters. It contains the wall character and grouped constants for filled and unfilled arrows and pipe shapes. Rendering logic should rely on these constants instead of hardcoded characters.
StringUtils is a lightweight utility-style class for string helpers and should not be instantiated.
```

# Requirement
```text
Overall / Domain Description
This is a console pipe-connection game. The game board is a grid surrounded by outer walls. Inside the board there is one source, and on the border there is one sink. The player places pipes from a pipe queue. After an initial delay, water begins to flow through connected pipes.
The board uses zero-based internal array indices. However, index 0 and the last row/column are occupied by the outer wall border. Therefore, the playable area starts from internal index 1 and ends at rows - 2 / cols - 2.
Player-facing coordinates intentionally align with these playable internal indices:
row 1 refers to internal row 1, and column 'A' refers to internal column 1. No row-minus-one or column-minus-one conversion is applied, except that column letters are mapped so that 'A' becomes 1.
Directions include up, down, left, and right. Each direction has a corresponding opposite direction and a unit movement offset(class PA19Helper will help class Direction to provide these functions). Pipe shapes define which directions they connect to. Termination type distinguishes source and sink.

Functional Requirements

Coordinate and Direction
A coordinate stores the internal row and column used directly to access the cell grid. A cell stored at a given grid position should carry the same coordinate value.
Because the outer border occupies index 0, playable cells naturally begin at index 1. This allows user input to align directly with the playable internal grid.
Directions support movement calculations through their unit offsets and can be compared against their opposite direction when checking pipe connectivity.

Game
The game supports placing the current pipe, skipping the current pipe, undoing the latest placement, advancing the water state, checking whether the player has won, checking whether the player has lost, and tracking the number of player steps.
When the player places a pipe, the row value is used directly. The column letter is converted so that 'A' maps to column 1, 'B' maps to column 2, and so on. For example, row 1 and column 'A' target the internal cell at [1][1].
Skipping removes the current pipe from the front of the queue and counts as one step.
Undo restores the latest placed pipe to the front of the queue, clears that pipe from the board, and counts as one step. If there is no previous placement to undo, the operation fails without changing the board.

Map
The map stores cells in a two-dimensional grid with indices from [0..rows-1] and [0..cols-1]. The outermost row and column positions are walls. The playable area is [1..rows-2] by [1..cols-2].
A pipe may be placed only when all of the following are true:
1. The target coordinate is inside the playable area.
2. The target cell is a fillable cell.
3. The target cell does not already contain a pipe.

Cell Family
Cells are parsed from map characters into concrete cell types.
A fillable cell may contain a pipe or be empty. Empty fillable cells render as a dot.
A termination cell represents either the source or the sink. It stores the direction it points toward and whether it has been filled by water.
A wall cell represents the board boundary and renders using the wall character.

Termination Cell Rendering
A termination cell renders as an arrow based on its direction and filled state. Filled and unfilled arrows come from the shared rendering constants.
Both source and sink use their stored pointing direction directly. The direction is not reversed for either type.
Throws IllegalStateException("Invalid pointingTo value!") for unknown direction.

Pipe
A pipe has a shape and a filled state. Its shape determines the directions it connects to.
Supported pipe shapes include horizontal, vertical, the four corner shapes, and cross.
Pipe rendering depends on both shape and filled state. The rendered character should come from the shared rendering constants rather than hardcoded glyphs.
Short pipe codes include HZ, VT, TL, TR, BL, BR, and CR.

Water Flow
At the beginning of water flow, the source is marked as filled.
Water expands outward from the source by distance. Each update increases the reachable fill distance by one.
Water may move from one pipe to an adjacent pipe only when both sides connect to each other: the outgoing direction of one pipe must match the opposite direction of the neighboring pipe.
The filling process follows breadth-first expansion from the source.

Win and Loss Conditions
The player wins if there is a connected path from the source to the sink.
Path checking starts from the source by moving once in the source’s pointing direction. From each pipe, traversal continues through that pipe’s connection directions. The path does not require pipes to already be filled. Reaching the sink means the game is won.
The player loses when a water-flow update fills no new pipes. Loss is checked only after the initial delay has ended and water has actually started advancing.

Pipe Queue
The pipe queue stores upcoming pipes. The player always interacts with the pipe at the front.
When a pipe is consumed, the queue is automatically refilled up to a fixed maximum length using randomly generated pipe shapes.
Undo places the restored pipe back at the front of the queue.

Delay Bar
The delay bar starts with an initial value and decreases once per round.
While the value is still positive, water has not begun flowing. Once the countdown passes zero, the corresponding positive distance indicates how far water should expand from the source.

Cell Stack
The placement history records successfully placed cells in order.
Undo uses the most recent placement. The undo counter represents the number of successful undo actions, not the current size of the placement history.

External / Tool Classes
Pa19Helper is a handwritten helper and assembly class in the pa19 package. It is responsible for constructing core game objects from provided inputs, wiring together the map, pipe queue, delay bar, and placement history. It also centralizes basic parsing and direction utility behavior.
Deserializer is responsible for reading game input from a file and producing runtime game objects. It validates that the input file exists, reads the board size, delay value, map lines, and optional default pipes. If the input ends unexpectedly or an I/O error occurs, it returns no game object and logs the error.
When parsing map text, border cells are treated as sink-side termination candidates, while inner termination symbols are treated as source-side candidates.
Deserializer ignores blank lines and comment lines beginning with # when reading meaningful input.
PipePatterns is a final utility-style constant holder for all rendering characters. It contains the wall character and grouped constants for filled and unfilled arrows and pipe shapes. Rendering logic should rely on these constants instead of hardcoded characters.
StringUtils is a lightweight utility-style class for string helpers and should not be instantiated.
```

# Requirement
```text
Overall / Domain Description
This is a console pipe-connection game. The game board is a grid surrounded by outer walls. Inside the board there is one source, and on the border there is one sink. The player places pipes from a pipe queue. After an initial delay, water begins to flow through connected pipes.
The board uses zero-based internal array indices. However, index 0 and the last row/column are occupied by the outer wall border. Therefore, the playable area starts from internal index 1 and ends at rows - 2 / cols - 2.
Player-facing coordinates intentionally align with these playable internal indices:
row 1 refers to internal row 1, and column 'A' refers to internal column 1. No row-minus-one or column-minus-one conversion is applied, except that column letters are mapped so that 'A' becomes 1.
Directions include up, down, left, and right. Each direction has a corresponding opposite direction and a unit movement offset(class PA19Helper will help class Direction to provide these functions). Pipe shapes define which directions they connect to. Termination type distinguishes source and sink.

Functional Requirements

Coordinate and Direction
A coordinate stores the internal row and column used directly to access the cell grid. A cell stored at a given grid position should carry the same coordinate value.
Because the outer border occupies index 0, playable cells naturally begin at index 1. This allows user input to align directly with the playable internal grid.
Directions support movement calculations through their unit offsets and can be compared against their opposite direction when checking pipe connectivity.

Game
The game supports placing the current pipe, skipping the current pipe, undoing the latest placement, advancing the water state, checking whether the player has won, checking whether the player has lost, and tracking the number of player steps.
When the player places a pipe, the row value is used directly. The column letter is converted so that 'A' maps to column 1, 'B' maps to column 2, and so on. For example, row 1 and column 'A' target the internal cell at [1][1].
Skipping removes the current pipe from the front of the queue and counts as one step.
Undo restores the latest placed pipe to the front of the queue, clears that pipe from the board, and counts as one step. If there is no previous placement to undo, the operation fails without changing the board.

Map
The map stores cells in a two-dimensional grid with indices from [0..rows-1] and [0..cols-1]. The outermost row and column positions are walls. The playable area is [1..rows-2] by [1..cols-2].
A pipe may be placed only when all of the following are true:
1. The target coordinate is inside the playable area.
2. The target cell is a fillable cell.
3. The target cell does not already contain a pipe.

Cell Family
Cells are parsed from map characters into concrete cell types.
A fillable cell may contain a pipe or be empty. Empty fillable cells render as a dot.
A termination cell represents either the source or the sink. It stores the direction it points toward and whether it has been filled by water.
A wall cell represents the board boundary and renders using the wall character.

Termination Cell Rendering
A termination cell renders as an arrow based on its direction and filled state. Filled and unfilled arrows come from the shared rendering constants.
Both source and sink use their stored pointing direction directly. The direction is not reversed for either type.
Throws IllegalStateException("Invalid pointingTo value!") for unknown direction.

Pipe
A pipe has a shape and a filled state. Its shape determines the directions it connects to.
Supported pipe shapes include horizontal, vertical, the four corner shapes, and cross.
Pipe rendering depends on both shape and filled state. The rendered character should come from the shared rendering constants rather than hardcoded glyphs.
Short pipe codes include HZ, VT, TL, TR, BL, BR, and CR.

Water Flow
At the beginning of water flow, the source is marked as filled.
Water expands outward from the source by distance. Each update increases the reachable fill distance by one.
Water may move from one pipe to an adjacent pipe only when both sides connect to each other: the outgoing direction of one pipe must match the opposite direction of the neighboring pipe.
The filling process follows breadth-first expansion from the source.

Win and Loss Conditions
The player wins if there is a connected path from the source to the sink.
Path checking starts from the source by moving once in the source’s pointing direction. From each pipe, traversal continues through that pipe’s connection directions. The path does not require pipes to already be filled. Reaching the sink means the game is won.
The player loses when a water-flow update fills no new pipes. Loss is checked only after the initial delay has ended and water has actually started advancing.

Pipe Queue
The pipe queue stores upcoming pipes. The player always interacts with the pipe at the front.
When a pipe is consumed, the queue is automatically refilled up to a fixed maximum length using randomly generated pipe shapes.
Undo places the restored pipe back at the front of the queue.

Delay Bar
The delay bar starts with an initial value and decreases once per round.
While the value is still positive, water has not begun flowing. Once the countdown passes zero, the corresponding positive distance indicates how far water should expand from the source.

Cell Stack
The placement history records successfully placed cells in order.
Undo uses the most recent placement. The undo counter represents the number of successful undo actions, not the current size of the placement history.

External / Tool Classes
Pa19Helper is a handwritten helper and assembly class in the pa19 package. It is responsible for constructing core game objects from provided inputs, wiring together the map, pipe queue, delay bar, and placement history. It also centralizes basic parsing and direction utility behavior.
Deserializer is responsible for reading game input from a file and producing runtime game objects. It validates that the input file exists, reads the board size, delay value, map lines, and optional default pipes. If the input ends unexpectedly or an I/O error occurs, it returns no game object and logs the error.
When parsing map text, border cells are treated as sink-side termination candidates, while inner termination symbols are treated as source-side candidates.
Deserializer ignores blank lines and comment lines beginning with # when reading meaningful input.
PipePatterns is a final utility-style constant holder for all rendering characters. It contains the wall character and grouped constants for filled and unfilled arrows and pipe shapes. Rendering logic should rely on these constants instead of hardcoded characters.
StringUtils is a lightweight utility-style class for string helpers and should not be instantiated.
```

```text
The game supports placing the current pipe, skipping the current pipe, undoing the latest placement, advancing the water state, checking whether the player has won, checking whether the player has lost, and tracking the number of player steps.
When the player places a pipe, the row value is used directly. The column letter is converted so that 'A' maps to column 1, 'B' maps to column 2, and so on. For example, row 1 and column 'A' target the internal cell at [1][1].
Skipping removes the current pipe from the front of the queue and counts as one step.
Undo restores the latest placed pipe to the front of the queue, clears that pipe from the board, and counts as one step. If there is no previous placement to undo, the operation fails without changing the board.

Map
The map stores cells in a two-dimensional grid with indices from [0..rows-1] and [0..cols-1]. The outermost row and column positions are walls. The playable area is [1..rows-2] by [1..cols-2].
A pipe may be placed only when all of the following are true:
1. The target coordinate is inside the playable area.
2. The target cell is a fillable cell.
3. The target cell does not already contain a pipe.

Cell Family
Cells are parsed from map characters into concrete cell types.
A fillable cell may contain a pipe or be empty. Empty fillable cells render as a dot.
A termination cell represents either the source or the sink. It stores the direction it points toward and whether it has been filled by water.
A wall cell represents the board boundary and renders using the wall character.

Termination Cell Rendering
A termination cell renders as an arrow based on its direction and filled state. Filled and unfilled arrows come from the shared rendering constants.
Both source and sink use their stored pointing direction directly. The direction is not reversed for either type.
Throws IllegalStateException("Invalid pointingTo value!") for unknown direction.

Pipe
A pipe has a shape and a filled state. Its shape determines the directions it connects to.
Supported pipe shapes include horizontal, vertical, the four corner shapes, and cross.
Pipe rendering depends on both shape and filled state. The rendered character should come from the shared rendering constants rather than hardcoded glyphs.
Short pipe codes include HZ, VT, TL, TR, BL, BR, and CR.

Water Flow
At the beginning of water flow, the source is marked as filled.
Water expands outward from the source by distance. Each update increases the reachable fill distance by one.
Water may move from one pipe to an adjacent pipe only when both sides connect to each other: the outgoing direction of one pipe must match the opposite direction of the neighboring pipe.
The filling process follows breadth-first expansion from the source.

Win and Loss Conditions
The player wins if there is a connected path from the source to the sink.
Path checking starts from the source by moving once in the source’s pointing direction. From each pipe, traversal continues through that pipe’s connection directions. The path does not require pipes to already be filled. Reaching the sink means the game is won.
The player loses when a water-flow update fills no new pipes. Loss is checked only after the initial delay has ended and water has actually started advancing.

Pipe Queue
The pipe queue stores upcoming pipes. The player always interacts with the pipe at the front.
When a pipe is consumed, the queue is automatically refilled up to a fixed maximum length using randomly generated pipe shapes.
Undo places the restored pipe back at the front of the queue.

Delay Bar
The delay bar starts with an initial value and decreases once per round.
While the value is still positive, water has not begun flowing. Once the countdown passes zero, the corresponding positive distance indicates how far water should expand from the source.

Cell Stack
The placement history records successfully placed cells in order.
Undo uses the most recent placement. The undo counter represents the number of successful undo actions, not the current size of the placement history.

External / Tool Classes
Pa19Helper is a handwritten helper and assembly class in the pa19 package. It is responsible for constructing core game objects from provided inputs, wiring together the map, pipe queue, delay bar, and placement history. It also centralizes basic parsing and direction utility behavior.
Deserializer is responsible for reading game input from a file and producing runtime game objects. It validates that the input file exists, reads the board size, delay value, map lines, and optional default pipes. If the input ends unexpectedly or an I/O error occurs, it returns no game object and logs the error.
When parsing map text, border cells are treated as sink-side termination candidates, while inner termination symbols are treated as source-side candidates.
Deserializer ignores blank lines and comment lines beginning with # when reading meaningful input.
PipePatterns is a final utility-style constant holder for all rendering characters. It contains the wall character and grouped constants for filled and unfilled arrows and pipe shapes. Rendering logic should rely on these constants instead of hardcoded characters.
StringUtils is a lightweight utility-style class for string helpers and should not be instantiated.
```

# Operation Specifications
DelayBar::distance
Summary: Returns the current water expansion distance based on the delay countdown.
Algorithm: If currentValue > 0, return -currentValue (negative meaning water hasn't started); otherwise return -currentValue (positive distance).
Related Features: currentValue, initialValue
Related Classes: None
Input: None
Output: int - positive distance value when currentValue <= 0, negative when currentValue > 0
Pre-condition: None
Post-condition: Returns the appropriate distance value.

DelayBar::countdown
Summary: Decrements the current delay value by 1 each round until it reaches zero.
Algorithm: If currentValue > 0, decrement currentValue by 1.
Related Features: currentValue, initialValue
Related Classes: None
Input: None
Output: void
Pre-condition: None
Post-condition: currentValue is decreased by 1 if it was positive; otherwise unchanged.

```text
Pa19Helper is a handwritten helper and assembly class in the pa19 package. It is responsible for constructing core game objects from provided inputs, wiring together the map, pipe queue, delay bar, and placement history. It also centralizes basic parsing and direction utility behavior.
Deserializer is responsible for reading game input from a file and producing runtime game objects. It validates that the input file exists, reads the board size, delay value, map lines, and optional default pipes. If the input ends unexpectedly or an I/O error occurs, it returns no game object and logs the error.
When parsing map text, border cells are treated as sink-side termination candidates, while inner termination symbols are treated as source-side candidates.
Deserializer ignores blank lines and comment lines beginning with # when reading meaningful input.
PipePatterns is a final utility-style constant holder for all rendering characters. It contains the wall character and grouped constants for filled and unfilled arrows and pipe shapes. Rendering logic should rely on these constants instead of hardcoded characters.
StringUtils is a lightweight utility-style class for string helpers and should not be instantiated.
```
