# Requirement
```text
Overall / Domain Description
This is a console pipe-connection game. The game board is a grid surrounded by outer walls. Inside the board there is one source, and on the border there is one sink. The player places pipes from a pipe queue. After an initial delay, water begins to flow through connected pipes.
The board uses zero-based internal array indices. However, index 0 and the last row/column are occupied by the outer wall border. Therefore, the playable area starts from internal index 1 and ends at rows - 2 / cols - 2.
Player-facing coordinates intentionally align with these playable internal indices:
row 1 refers to internal row 1, and column 'A' refers to internal column 1. No row-minus-one or column-minus-one conversion is applied, except that column letters are mapped so that 'A' becomes 1.
Directions include up, down, left, and right. Each direction has a corresponding opposite direction and a unit movement offset(class PA19Helper will help class Direction to provide these functions). Pipe shapes define which directions they connect to. Termination type distinguishes source and sink.

Functional Requirements

Coordinate and Direction
A coordinate stores the internal row and column used directly to access the cell grid. A cell stored at a given grid position should carry the same coordinate value.
Because the outer border occupies index 0, playable cells naturally begin at index 1. This allows user input to align directly with the playable internal grid.
Directions support movement calculations through their unit offsets and can be compared against their opposite direction when checking pipe connectivity.

Game
The game supports placing the current pipe, skipping the current pipe, undoing the latest placement, advancing the water state, checking whether the player has won, checking whether the player has lost, and tracking the number of player steps.
When the player places a pipe, the row value is used directly. The column letter is converted so that 'A' maps to column 1, 'B' maps to column 2, and so on. For example, row 1 and column 'A' target the internal cell at [1][1].
Skipping removes the current pipe from the front of the queue and counts as one step.
Undo restores the latest placed pipe to the front of the queue, clears that pipe from the board, and counts as one step. If there is no previous placement to undo, the operation fails without changing the board.

Map
The map stores cells in a two-dimensional grid with indices from [0..rows-1] and [0..cols-1]. The outermost row and column positions are walls. The playable area is [1..rows-2] by [1..cols-2].
A pipe may be placed only when all of the following are true:
1. The target coordinate is inside the playable area.
2. The target cell is a fillable cell.
3. The target cell does not already contain a pipe.

Cell Family
Cells are parsed from map characters into concrete cell types.
A fillable cell may contain a pipe or be empty. Empty fillable cells render as a dot.
A termination cell represents either the source or the sink. It stores the direction it points toward and whether it has been filled by water.
A wall cell represents the board boundary and renders using the wall character.

Termination Cell Rendering
A termination cell renders as an arrow based on its direction and filled state. Filled and unfilled arrows come from the shared rendering constants.
Both source and sink use their stored pointing direction directly. The direction is not reversed for either type.
Throws IllegalStateException("Invalid pointingTo value!") for unknown direction.

Pipe
A pipe has a shape and a filled state. Its shape determines the directions it connects to.
Supported pipe shapes include horizontal, vertical, the four corner shapes, and cross.
Pipe rendering depends on both shape and filled state. The rendered character should come from the shared rendering constants rather than hardcoded glyphs.
Short pipe codes include HZ, VT, TL, TR, BL, BR, and CR.

Water Flow
At the beginning of water flow, the source is marked as filled.
Water expands outward from the source by distance. Each update increases the reachable fill distance by one.
Water may move from one pipe to an adjacent pipe only when both sides connect to each other: the outgoing direction of one pipe must match the opposite direction of the neighboring pipe.
The filling process follows breadth-first expansion from the source.

Win and Loss Conditions
The player wins if there is a connected path from the source to the sink.
Path checking starts from the source by moving once in the source’s pointing direction. From each pipe, traversal continues through that pipe’s connection directions. The path does not require pipes to already be filled. Reaching the sink means the game is won.
The player loses when a water-flow update fills no new pipes. Loss is checked only after the initial delay has ended and water has actually started advancing.

Pipe Queue
The pipe queue stores upcoming pipes. The player always interacts with the pipe at the front.
When a pipe is consumed, the queue is automatically refilled up to a fixed maximum length using randomly generated pipe shapes.
Undo places the restored pipe back at the front of the queue.

Delay Bar
The delay bar starts with an initial value and decreases once per round.
While the value is still positive, water has not begun flowing. Once the countdown passes zero, the corresponding positive distance indicates how far water should expand from the source.

Cell Stack
The placement history records successfully placed cells in order.
Undo uses the most recent placement. The undo counter represents the number of successful undo actions, not the current size of the placement history.

External / Tool Classes
Pa19Helper is a handwritten helper and assembly class in the pa19 package. It is responsible for constructing core game objects from provided inputs, wiring together the map, pipe queue, delay bar, and placement history. It also centralizes basic parsing and direction utility behavior.
Deserializer is responsible for reading game input from a file and producing runtime game objects. It validates that the input file exists, reads the board size, delay value, map lines, and optional default pipes. If the input ends unexpectedly or an I/O error occurs, it returns no game object and logs the error.
When parsing map text, border cells are treated as sink-side termination candidates, while inner termination symbols are treated as source-side candidates.
Deserializer ignores blank lines and comment lines beginning with # when reading meaningful input.
PipePatterns is a final utility-style constant holder for all rendering characters. It contains the wall character and grouped constants for filled and unfilled arrows and pipe shapes. Rendering logic should rely on these constants instead of hardcoded characters.
StringUtils is a lightweight utility-style class for string helpers and should not be instantiated.
```

# Operation Specifications
Map::undo
Summary: Removes a pipe from the specified coordinate on the map.
Algorithm:
  1. Get the cell at the given coordinate
  2. If the cell is a FillableCell with a pipe, set its pipe to null
Related Features: cell array
Related Classes: Coordinate, FillableCell
Input: coord : Coordinate - the coordinate to clear
Output: void
Pre-condition: coord is not null
Post-condition: The pipe at the specified coordinate is removed (set to null).

Map::fillTiles
Summary: Fills pipes with water up to the specified distance from the source using BFS.
Algorithm:
  1. If this is the first fill (distance == 1), call fillBeginTile() to mark source as filled
  2. Perform BFS from the source, expanding outward by distance steps
  3. For each adjacent pipe, check if both sides connect (outgoing direction matches opposite of neighbor)
  4. Mark reachable pipes as filled
  5. Update filledTiles list with newly filled coordinates
  6. Update prevFilledDistance to current distance
Related Features: sourceCell, filledTiles, prevFilledDistance, prevFilledTiles
Related Classes: TerminationCell, Pipe, Coordinate, Direction
Input: distance : int - the current water expansion distance (positive integer)
Output: void
Pre-condition: distance > 0
Post-condition: All pipes within the given distance from source that are properly connected are marked as filled.

Map::hasLost
Summary: Checks if the player has lost based on water flow stagnation.
Algorithm:
  1. If prevFilledDistance is null or prevFilledTiles is 0, return false (not yet started or first fill)
  2. Compare current filledTiles size with prevFilledTiles
  3. If no new tiles were filled (size unchanged), return true
  4. Otherwise return false
Related Features: filledTiles, prevFilledTiles, prevFilledDistance
Related Classes: None
Input: None
Output: boolean - true if no new tiles were filled in the last update, false otherwise
Pre-condition: None
Post-condition: Returns loss state based on water flow progress.

Map::tryPlacePipe
Summary: Attempts to place a pipe at the specified coordinate on the map.
Algorithm:
  1. Check if coordinate is within playable area (1..rows-2, 1..cols-2)
  2. Check if the cell at that coordinate is a FillableCell
  3. Check if the cell does not already contain a pipe
  4. If all conditions met, set the cell's pipe to the given pipe and return true
  5. Otherwise return false
Related Features: cell array, rows, cols
Related Classes: Coordinate, FillableCell, Pipe
Input: row : int - the row coordinate, col : int - the column coordinate, pipe : Pipe - the pipe to place
Output: boolean - true if placement was successful, false otherwise
Pre-condition: row and col are valid integers
Post-condition: If successful, the specified cell now contains the given pipe.

# Requirement
```text
Overall / Domain Description
This is a console pipe-connection game. The game board is a grid surrounded by outer walls. Inside the board there is one source, and on the border there is one sink. The player places pipes from a pipe queue. After an initial delay, water begins to flow through connected pipes.
The board uses zero-based internal array indices. However, index 0 and the last row/column are occupied by the outer wall border. Therefore, the playable area starts from internal index 1 and ends at rows - 2 / cols - 2.
Player-facing coordinates intentionally align with these playable internal indices:
row 1 refers to internal row 1, and column 'A' refers to internal column 1. No row-minus-one or column-minus-one conversion is applied, except that column letters are mapped so that 'A' becomes 1.
Directions include up, down, left, and right. Each direction has a corresponding opposite direction and a unit movement offset(class PA19Helper will help class Direction to provide these functions). Pipe shapes define which directions they connect to. Termination type distinguishes source and sink.

Functional Requirements

Coordinate and Direction
A coordinate stores the internal row and column used directly to access the cell grid. A cell stored at a given grid position should carry the same coordinate value.
Because the outer border occupies index 0, playable cells naturally begin at index 1. This allows user input to align directly with the playable internal grid.
Directions support movement calculations through their unit offsets and can be compared against their opposite direction when checking pipe connectivity.

Game
The game supports placing the current pipe, skipping the current pipe, undoing the latest placement, advancing the water state, checking whether the player has won, checking whether the player has lost, and tracking the number of player steps.
When the player places a pipe, the row value is used directly. The column letter is converted so that 'A' maps to column 1, 'B' maps to column 2, and so on. For example, row 1 and column 'A' target the internal cell at [1][1].
Skipping removes the current pipe from the front of the queue and counts as one step.
Undo restores the latest placed pipe to the front of the queue, clears that pipe from the board, and counts as one step. If there is no previous placement to undo, the operation fails without changing the board.

Map
The map stores cells in a two-dimensional grid with indices from [0..rows-1] and [0..cols-1]. The outermost row and column positions are walls. The playable area is [1..rows-2] by [1..cols-2].
A pipe may be placed only when all of the following are true:
1. The target coordinate is inside the playable area.
2. The target cell is a fillable cell.
3. The target cell does not already contain a pipe.

Cell Family
Cells are parsed from map characters into concrete cell types.
A fillable cell may contain a pipe or be empty. Empty fillable cells render as a dot.
A termination cell represents either the source or the sink. It stores the direction it points toward and whether it has been filled by water.
A wall cell represents the board boundary and renders using the wall character.

Termination Cell Rendering
A termination cell renders as an arrow based on its direction and filled state. Filled and unfilled arrows come from the shared rendering constants.
Both source and sink use their stored pointing direction directly. The direction is not reversed for either type.
Throws IllegalStateException("Invalid pointingTo value!") for unknown direction.

Pipe
A pipe has a shape and a filled state. Its shape determines the directions it connects to.
Supported pipe shapes include horizontal, vertical, the four corner shapes, and cross.
Pipe rendering depends on both shape and filled state. The rendered character should come from the shared rendering constants rather than hardcoded glyphs.
Short pipe codes include HZ, VT, TL, TR, BL, BR, and CR.

Water Flow
At the beginning of water flow, the source is marked as filled.
Water expands outward from the source by distance. Each update increases the reachable fill distance by one.
Water may move from one pipe to an adjacent pipe only when both sides connect to each other: the outgoing direction of one pipe must match the opposite direction of the neighboring pipe.
The filling process follows breadth-first expansion from the source.

Win and Loss Conditions
The player wins if there is a connected path from the source to the sink.
Path checking starts from the source by moving once in the source’s pointing direction. From each pipe, traversal continues through that pipe’s connection directions. The path does not require pipes to already be filled. Reaching the sink means the game is won.
The player loses when a water-flow update fills no new pipes. Loss is checked only after the initial delay has ended and water has actually started advancing.

Pipe Queue
The pipe queue stores upcoming pipes. The player always interacts with the pipe at the front.
When a pipe is consumed, the queue is automatically refilled up to a fixed maximum length using randomly generated pipe shapes.
Undo places the restored pipe back at the front of the queue.

Delay Bar
The delay bar starts with an initial value and decreases once per round.
While the value is still positive, water has not begun flowing. Once the countdown passes zero, the corresponding positive distance indicates how far water should expand from the source.

Cell Stack
The placement history records successfully placed cells in order.
Undo uses the most recent placement. The undo counter represents the number of successful undo actions, not the current size of the placement history.

External / Tool Classes
Pa19Helper is a handwritten helper and assembly class in the pa19 package. It is responsible for constructing core game objects from provided inputs, wiring together the map, pipe queue, delay bar, and placement history. It also centralizes basic parsing and direction utility behavior.
Deserializer is responsible for reading game input from a file and producing runtime game objects. It validates that the input file exists, reads the board size, delay value, map lines, and optional default pipes. If the input ends unexpectedly or an I/O error occurs, it returns no game object and logs the error.
When parsing map text, border cells are treated as sink-side termination candidates, while inner termination symbols are treated as source-side candidates.
Deserializer ignores blank lines and comment lines beginning with # when reading meaningful input.
PipePatterns is a final utility-style constant holder for all rendering characters. It contains the wall character and grouped constants for filled and unfilled arrows and pipe shapes. Rendering logic should rely on these constants instead of hardcoded characters.
StringUtils is a lightweight utility-style class for string helpers and should not be instantiated.
```

While the value is still positive, water has not begun flowing. Once the countdown passes zero, the corresponding positive distance indicates how far water should expand from the source.

Cell Stack
The placement history records successfully placed cells in order.
Undo uses the most recent placement. The undo counter represents the number of successful undo actions, not the current size of the placement history.

External / Tool Classes
Pa19Helper is a handwritten helper and assembly class in the pa19 package. It is responsible for constructing core game objects from provided inputs, wiring together the map, pipe queue, delay bar, and placement history. It also centralizes basic parsing and direction utility behavior.
Deserializer is responsible for reading game input from a file and producing runtime game objects. It validates that the input file exists, reads the board size, delay value, map lines, and optional default pipes. If the input ends unexpectedly or an I/O error occurs, it returns no game object and logs the error.
When parsing map text, border cells are treated as sink-side termination candidates, while inner termination symbols are treated as source-side candidates.
Deserializer ignores blank lines and comment lines beginning with # when reading meaningful input.
PipePatterns is a final utility-style constant holder for all rendering characters. It contains the wall character and grouped constants for filled and unfilled arrows and pipe shapes. Rendering logic should rely on these constants instead of hardcoded characters.
StringUtils is a lightweight utility-style class for string helpers and should not be instantiated.

# Operation Specifications
Game::hasWon
Summary: Checks whether the player has won the game by connecting source to sink.
Algorithm: Return the result of calling map.checkPath().
Related Features: map
Related Classes: Map
Input: None
Output: boolean - true if a path from source to sink exists, false otherwise
Pre-condition: None
Post-condition: Returns the win state from the map.

Game::hasLost
Summary: Checks whether the player has lost the game.
Algorithm: Return the result of calling map.hasLost().
Related Features: map
Related Classes: Map
Input: None
Output: boolean - true if the player has lost, false otherwise
Pre-condition: None
Post-condition: Returns the loss state from the map.

Game::skipPipe
Summary: Removes the current pipe from the front of the queue and counts it as one step.
Algorithm:
  1. Call pipeQueue.consume() to remove the front pipe
  2. Increment numOfSteps by 1
Related Features: pipeQueue, numOfSteps
Related Classes: PipeQueue
Input: None
Output: void
Pre-condition: Pipe queue is not empty
Post-condition: The front pipe is removed from the queue, and step count increases by 1.

Game::undoStep
Summary: Undoes the most recent pipe placement, restoring the pipe to the front of the queue.
Algorithm:
  1. Call cellStack.pop() to get the last placed cell
  2. If null, return false (nothing to undo)
  3. Get the coordinate from the cell
  4. Call map.undo(coordinate) to clear the pipe from the board
  5. Call pipeQueue.undo(cell.pipe) to restore the pipe to the front
  6. Increment numOfSteps by 1
  7. Return true
Related Features: cellStack, map, pipeQueue, numOfSteps
Related Classes: CellStack, Map, PipeQueue, FillableCell, Pipe, Coordinate
Input: None
Output: boolean - true if undo was successful, false if no placement to undo
Pre-condition: None
Post-condition: If successful, the last pipe is removed from the board, restored to the queue, and step count increases.

Game::placePipe
Summary: Attempts to place the current pipe from the queue onto the board at the specified coordinates.
Algorithm:
  1. Convert col character to column index ('A' -> 1, 'B' -> 2, etc.)
  2. Get the current pipe from pipeQueue.peek()
  3. Call map.tryPlacePipe(row, colIndex, pipe)
  4. If successful, call pipeQueue.consume() and push the cell onto cellStack
  5. Increment numOfSteps by 1
  6. Return true if placement succeeded, false otherwise
Related Features: map, pipeQueue, cellStack, numOfSteps
Related Classes: Map, PipeQueue, CellStack, Pipe
Input: row : int - the row coordinate (1-based playable index), col : char - the column letter ('A'-'Z')
Output: boolean - true if placement was successful, false otherwise
Pre-condition: row and col represent valid playable coordinates
Post-condition: If successful, the pipe is placed on the map, the queue advances, the placement is recorded, and step count increases.

Game::updateState
Summary: Advances the water flow state by one step, including delay countdown and tile filling.
Algorithm:
  1. Call delayBar.countdown()
  2. If delayBar.distance() > 0, call map.fillTiles(delayBar.distance())
Related Features: delayBar, map
Related Classes: DelayBar, Map
Input: None
Output: void
Pre-condition: None
Post-condition: Delay bar is decremented; if water should flow, tiles are filled up to the current distance.

# Requirement
```text
Overall / Domain Description
This is a console pipe-connection game. The game board is a grid surrounded by outer walls. Inside the board there is one source, and on the border there is one sink. The player places pipes from a pipe queue. After an initial delay, water begins to flow through connected pipes.
The board uses zero-based internal array indices. However, index 0 and the last row/column are occupied by the outer wall border. Therefore, the playable area starts from internal index 1 and ends at rows - 2 / cols - 2.
Player-facing coordinates intentionally align with these playable internal indices:
row 1 refers to internal row 1, and column 'A' refers to internal column 1. No row-minus-one or column-minus-one conversion is applied, except that column letters are mapped so that 'A' becomes 1.
Directions include up, down, left, and right. Each direction has a corresponding opposite direction and a unit movement offset(class PA19Helper will help class Direction to provide these functions). Pipe shapes define which directions they connect to. Termination type distinguishes source and sink.

Functional Requirements

Coordinate and Direction
A coordinate stores the internal row and column used directly to access the cell grid. A cell stored at a given grid position should carry the same coordinate value.
Because the outer border occupies index 0, playable cells naturally begin at index 1. This allows user input to align directly with the playable internal grid.
Directions support movement calculations through their unit offsets and can be compared against their opposite direction when checking pipe connectivity.

Game
The game supports placing the current pipe, skipping the current pipe, undoing the latest placement, advancing the water state, checking whether the player has won, checking whether the player has lost, and tracking the number of player steps.
When the player places a pipe, the row value is used directly. The column letter is converted so that 'A' maps to column 1, 'B' maps to column 2, and so on. For example, row 1 and column 'A' target the internal cell at [1][1].
Skipping removes the current pipe from the front of the queue and counts as one step.
Undo restores the latest placed pipe to the front of the queue, clears that pipe from the board, and counts as one step. If there is no previous placement to undo, the operation fails without changing the board.

Map
The map stores cells in a two-dimensional grid with indices from [0..rows-1] and [0..cols-1]. The outermost row and column positions are walls. The playable area is [1..rows-2] by [1..cols-2].
A pipe may be placed only when all of the following are true:
1. The target coordinate is inside the playable area.
2. The target cell is a fillable cell.
3. The target cell does not already contain a pipe.

Cell Family
Cells are parsed from map characters into concrete cell types.
A fillable cell may contain a pipe or be empty. Empty fillable cells render as a dot.
A termination cell represents either the source or the sink. It stores the direction it points toward and whether it has been filled by water.
A wall cell represents the board boundary and renders using the wall character.

Termination Cell Rendering
A termination cell renders as an arrow based on its direction and filled state. Filled and unfilled arrows come from the shared rendering constants.
Both source and sink use their stored pointing direction directly. The direction is not reversed for either type.
Throws IllegalStateException("Invalid pointingTo value!") for unknown direction.

Pipe
A pipe has a shape and a filled state. Its shape determines the directions it connects to.
Supported pipe shapes include horizontal, vertical, the four corner shapes, and cross.
Pipe rendering depends on both shape and filled state. The rendered character should come from the shared rendering constants rather than hardcoded glyphs.
Short pipe codes include HZ, VT, TL, TR, BL, BR, and CR.

Water Flow
At the beginning of water flow, the source is marked as filled.
Water expands outward from the source by distance. Each update increases the reachable fill distance by one.
Water may move from one pipe to an adjacent pipe only when both sides connect to each other: the outgoing direction of one pipe must match the opposite direction of the neighboring pipe.
The filling process follows breadth-first expansion from the source.

Win and Loss Conditions
The player wins if there is a connected path from the source to the sink.
Path checking starts from the source by moving once in the source’s pointing direction. From each pipe, traversal continues through that pipe’s connection directions. The path does not require pipes to already be filled. Reaching the sink means the game is won.
The player loses when a water-flow update fills no new pipes. Loss is checked only after the initial delay has ended and water has actually started advancing.

Pipe Queue
The pipe queue stores upcoming pipes. The player always interacts with the pipe at the front.
When a pipe is consumed, the queue is automatically refilled up to a fixed maximum length using randomly generated pipe shapes.
Undo places the restored pipe back at the front of the queue.

Delay Bar
The delay bar starts with an initial value and decreases once per round.
While the value is still positive, water has not begun flowing. Once the countdown passes zero, the corresponding positive distance indicates how far water should expand from the source.

Cell Stack
The placement history records successfully placed cells in order.
Undo uses the most recent placement. The undo counter represents the number of successful undo actions, not the current size of the placement history.

External / Tool Classes
Pa19Helper is a handwritten helper and assembly class in the pa19 package. It is responsible for constructing core game objects from provided inputs, wiring together the map, pipe queue, delay bar, and placement history. It also centralizes basic parsing and direction utility behavior.
Deserializer is responsible for reading game input from a file and producing runtime game objects. It validates that the input file exists, reads the board size, delay value, map lines, and optional default pipes. If the input ends unexpectedly or an I/O error occurs, it returns no game object and logs the error.
When parsing map text, border cells are treated as sink-side termination candidates, while inner termination symbols are treated as source-side candidates.
Deserializer ignores blank lines and comment lines beginning with # when reading meaningful input.
PipePatterns is a final utility-style constant holder for all rendering characters. It contains the wall character and grouped constants for filled and unfilled arrows and pipe shapes. Rendering logic should rely on these constants instead of hardcoded characters.
StringUtils is a lightweight utility-style class for string helpers and should not be instantiated.
```

You will be given a **Requirement**, a **Class Diagram** in PlantUML, and a list of operation specifications. Your task is to correct the specifications that are inconsistent with the requirement.

An operation specification must describe the following sections about the operation:
1. Summary: the summary of functionality;
2. Algorithm: algorithm or pseudo code;
3. Related Features: a list of structural or behavior features within this class that shall be accessed;
4. Related Classes: a list of classes and data types defined in **Class Diagram** that shall be accessed, in the format of `Related Classes: ClsA, CLsB, ...` or `Related Classes: None`;
5. Input: the input parameters, including the meaning, the format, and the value ranges if necessary;
6. Output: output value, including the meaning, the format, and the value ranges if necessary;
7. Pre-condition: the condition that the system and the input must satisfy before the operation is executed;
8. Post-condition: the condition that the system and the output must satisfy after the operation is executed.

Finish this task by following the guidelines below.
1. Read the requirement and the class diagram.
2. For each operation specification, determine whether it is complete and consistent with the requirement.
3. If there is any error, correct the erroneous specification.
4. Follow the specification format. Output changed specifications only; OMIT unchanged specifications.

# Requirement
```text
Overall / Domain Description
This is a console pipe-connection game. The game board is a grid surrounded by outer walls. Inside the board there is one source, and on the border there is one sink. The player places pipes from a pipe queue. After an initial delay, water begins to flow through connected pipes.
The board uses zero-based internal array indices. However, index 0 and the last row/column are occupied by the outer wall border. Therefore, the playable area starts from internal index 1 and ends at rows - 2 / cols - 2.
Player-facing coordinates intentionally align with these playable internal indices:
row 1 refers to internal row 1, and column 'A' refers to internal column 1. No row-minus-one or column-minus-one conversion is applied, except that column letters are mapped so that 'A' becomes 1.
Directions include up, down, left, and right. Each direction has a corresponding opposite direction and a unit movement offset(class PA19Helper will help class Direction to provide these functions). Pipe shapes define which directions they connect to. Termination type distinguishes source and sink.

Functional Requirements

Coordinate and Direction
A coordinate stores the internal row and column used directly to access the cell grid. A cell stored at a given grid position should carry the same coordinate value.
Because the outer border occupies index 0, playable cells naturally begin at index 1. This allows user input to align directly with the playable internal grid.
Directions support movement calculations through their unit offsets and can be compared against their opposite direction when checking pipe connectivity.

Game
The game supports placing the current pipe, skipping the current pipe, undoing the latest placement, advancing the water state, checking whether the player has won, checking whether the player has lost, and tracking the number of player steps.
When the player places a pipe, the row value is used directly. The column letter is converted so that 'A' maps to column 1, 'B' maps to column 2, and so on. For example, row 1 and column 'A' target the internal cell at [1][1].
Skipping removes the current pipe from the front of the queue and counts as one step.
Undo restores the latest placed pipe to the front of the queue, clears that pipe from the board, and counts as one step. If there is no previous placement to undo, the operation fails without changing the board.

Map
The map stores cells in a two-dimensional grid with indices from [0..rows-1] and [0..cols-1]. The outermost row and column positions are walls. The playable area is [1..rows-2] by [1..cols-2].
A pipe may be placed only when all of the following are true:
1. The target coordinate is inside the playable area.
2. The target cell is a fillable cell.
3. The target cell does not already contain a pipe.

Cell Family
Cells are parsed from map characters into concrete cell types.
A fillable cell may contain a pipe or be empty. Empty fillable cells render as a dot.
A termination cell represents either the source or the sink. It stores the direction it points toward and whether it has been filled by water.
A wall cell represents the board boundary and renders using the wall character.

Termination Cell Rendering
A termination cell renders as an arrow based on its direction and filled state. Filled and unfilled arrows come from the shared rendering constants.
Both source and sink use their stored pointing direction directly. The direction is not reversed for either type.
Throws IllegalStateException("Invalid pointingTo value!") for unknown direction.

Pipe
A pipe has a shape and a filled state. Its shape determines the directions it connects to.
Supported pipe shapes include horizontal, vertical, the four corner shapes, and cross.
Pipe rendering depends on both shape and filled state. The rendered character should come from the shared rendering constants rather than hardcoded glyphs.
Short pipe codes include HZ, VT, TL, TR, BL, BR, and CR.

Water Flow
At the beginning of water flow, the source is marked as filled.
Water expands outward from the source by distance. Each update increases the reachable fill distance by one.
Water may move from one pipe to an adjacent pipe only when both sides connect to each other: the outgoing direction of one pipe must match the opposite direction of the neighboring pipe.
The filling process follows breadth-first expansion from the source.

Win and Loss Conditions
The player wins if there is a connected path from the source to the sink.
Path checking starts from the source by moving once in the source’s pointing direction. From each pipe, traversal continues through that pipe’s connection directions. The path does not require pipes to already be filled. Reaching the sink means the game is won.
The player loses when a water-flow update fills no new pipes. Loss is checked only after the initial delay has ended and water has actually started advancing.

Pipe Queue
The pipe queue stores upcoming pipes. The player always interacts with the pipe at the front.
When a pipe is consumed, the queue is automatically refilled up to a fixed maximum length using randomly generated pipe shapes.
Undo places the restored pipe back at the front of the queue.

Delay Bar
The delay bar starts with an initial value and decreases once per round.
While the value is still positive, water has not begun flowing. Once the countdown passes zero, the corresponding positive distance indicates how far water should expand from the source.

Cell Stack
The placement history records successfully placed cells in order.
Undo uses the most recent placement. The undo counter represents the number of successful undo actions, not the current size of the placement history.

External / Tool Classes
Pa19Helper is a handwritten helper and assembly class in the pa19 package. It is responsible for constructing core game objects from provided inputs, wiring together the map, pipe queue, delay bar, and placement history. It also centralizes basic parsing and direction utility behavior.
Deserializer is responsible for reading game input from a file and producing runtime game objects. It validates that the input file exists, reads the board size, delay value, map lines, and optional default pipes. If the input ends unexpectedly or an I/O error occurs, it returns no game object and logs the error.
When parsing map text, border cells are treated as sink-side termination candidates, while inner termination symbols are treated as source-side candidates.
Deserializer ignores blank lines and comment lines beginning with # when reading meaningful input.
PipePatterns is a final utility-style constant holder for all rendering characters. It contains the wall character and grouped constants for filled and unfilled arrows and pipe shapes. Rendering logic should rely on these constants instead of hardcoded characters.
StringUtils is a lightweight utility-style class for string helpers and should not be instantiated.
```

# Operation Specifications
Game::hasWon
Summary: Checks whether the player has won the game by verifying a connected path from source to sink.
Algorithm: Return the result of calling map.checkPath().
Related Features: map
Related Classes: Map
Input: None
Output: boolean - true if a connected path from source to sink exists, false otherwise
Pre-condition: None
Post-condition: Returns the win state from the map.

Game::hasLost
Summary: Checks whether the player has lost the game.
Algorithm: Return the result of calling map.hasLost().
Related Features: map
Related Classes: Map
Input: None
Output: boolean - true if the player has lost, false otherwise
Pre-condition: None
Post-condition: Returns the loss state from the map.

Game::skipPipe
Summary: Removes the current pipe from the front of the queue and counts it as one step.
Algorithm:
  1. Call pipeQueue.consume() to remove the front pipe
  2. Increment numOfSteps by 1
Related Features: pipeQueue, numOfSteps
Related Classes: PipeQueue
Input: None
Output: void
Pre-condition: Pipe queue is not empty
Post-condition: The front pipe is removed from the queue, and step count increases by 1.

Game::undoStep
Summary: Undoes the most recent pipe placement, restoring the pipe to the front of the queue.
Algorithm:
  1. Call cellStack.pop() to get the last placed cell
  2. If null, return false (nothing to undo)
  3. Get the coordinate from the cell
  4. Call map.undo(coordinate) to clear the pipe from the board
  5. Call pipeQueue.undo(cell.pipe) to restore the pipe to the front
  6. Increment numOfSteps by 1
  7. Return true
Related Features: cellStack, map, pipeQueue, numOfSteps
Related Classes: CellStack, Map, PipeQueue, FillableCell, Pipe, Coordinate
Input: None
Output: boolean - true if undo was successful, false if no placement to undo
Pre-condition: None
Post-condition: If successful, the last pipe is removed from the board, restored to the queue, and step count increases.

Game::placePipe
Summary: Attempts to place the current pipe from the queue onto the board at the specified coordinates.
Algorithm:
  1. Convert col character to column index ('A' -> 1, 'B' -> 2, etc.)
  2. Get the current pipe from pipeQueue.peek()
  3. Call map.tryPlacePipe(row, colIndex, pipe)
  4. If successful, call pipeQueue.consume() and push the cell onto cellStack
  5. Increment numOfSteps by 1
  6. Return true if placement succeeded, false otherwise
Related Features: map, pipeQueue, cellStack, numOfSteps
Related Classes: Map, PipeQueue, CellStack, Pipe
Input: row : int - the row coordinate (1-based playable index), col : char - the column letter ('A'-'Z')
Output: boolean - true if placement was successful, false otherwise
Pre-condition: row and col represent valid playable coordinates
Post-condition: If successful, the pipe is placed on the map, the queue advances, the placement is recorded, and step count increases.

Game::updateState
Summary: Advances the water flow state by one step, including delay countdown and tile filling.
Algorithm:
  1. Call delayBar.countdown()
  2. If delayBar.distance() > 0, call map.fillTiles(delayBar.distance())
Related Features: delayBar, map
Related Classes: DelayBar, Map
Input: None
Output: void
Pre-condition: None
Post-condition: Delay bar is decremented; if water should flow, tiles are filled up to the current distance.

Related Features: delayBar, map
Related Classes: DelayBar, Map
Input: None
Output: void
Pre-condition: None
Post-condition: Delay bar is decremented; if water should flow, tiles are filled up to the current distance.

# Requirement
```text
Overall / Domain Description
This is a console pipe-connection game. The game board is a grid surrounded by outer walls. Inside the board there is one source, and on the border there is one sink. The player places pipes from a pipe queue. After an initial delay, water begins to flow through connected pipes.
The board uses zero-based internal array indices. However, index 0 and the last row/column are occupied by the outer wall border. Therefore, the playable area starts from internal index 1 and ends at rows - 2 / cols - 2.
Player-facing coordinates intentionally align with these playable internal indices:
row 1 refers to internal row 1, and column 'A' refers to internal column 1. No row-minus-one or column-minus-one conversion is applied, except that column letters are mapped so that 'A' becomes 1.
Directions include up, down, left, and right. Each direction has a corresponding opposite direction and a unit movement offset(class PA19Helper will help class Direction to provide these functions). Pipe shapes define which directions they connect to. Termination type distinguishes source and sink.

Functional Requirements

Coordinate and Direction
A coordinate stores the internal row and column used directly to access the cell grid. A cell stored at a given grid position should carry the same coordinate value.
Because the outer border occupies index 0, playable cells naturally begin at index 1. This allows user input to align directly with the playable internal grid.
Directions support movement calculations through their unit offsets and can be compared against their opposite direction when checking pipe connectivity.

Game
The game supports placing the current pipe, skipping the current pipe, undoing the latest placement, advancing the water state, checking whether the player has won, checking whether the player has lost, and tracking the number of player steps.
When the player places a pipe, the row value is used directly. The column letter is converted so that 'A' maps to column 1, 'B' maps to column 2, and so on. For example, row 1 and column 'A' target the internal cell at [1][1].
Skipping removes the current pipe from the front of the queue and counts as one step.
Undo restores the latest placed pipe to the front of the queue, clears that pipe from the board, and counts as one step. If there is no previous placement to undo, the operation fails without changing the board.

Map
The map stores cells in a two-dimensional grid with indices from [0..rows-1] and [0..cols-1]. The outermost row and column positions are walls. The playable area is [1..rows-2] by [1..cols-2].
A pipe may be placed only when all of the following are true:
1. The target coordinate is inside the playable area.
2. The target cell is a fillable cell.
3. The target cell does not already contain a pipe.

Cell Family
Cells are parsed from map characters into concrete cell types.
A fillable cell may contain a pipe or be empty. Empty fillable cells render as a dot.
A termination cell represents either the source or the sink. It stores the direction it points toward and whether it has been filled by water.
A wall cell represents the board boundary and renders using the wall character.

Termination Cell Rendering
A termination cell renders as an arrow based on its direction and filled state. Filled and unfilled arrows come from the shared rendering constants.
Both source and sink use their stored pointing direction directly. The direction is not reversed for either type.
Throws IllegalStateException("Invalid pointingTo value!") for unknown direction.

Pipe
A pipe has a shape and a filled state. Its shape determines the directions it connects to.
Supported pipe shapes include horizontal, vertical, the four corner shapes, and cross.
Pipe rendering depends on both shape and filled state. The rendered character should come from the shared rendering constants rather than hardcoded glyphs.
Short pipe codes include HZ, VT, TL, TR, BL, BR, and CR.

Water Flow
At the beginning of water flow, the source is marked as filled.
Water expands outward from the source by distance. Each update increases the reachable fill distance by one.
Water may move from one pipe to an adjacent pipe only when both sides connect to each other: the outgoing direction of one pipe must match the opposite direction of the neighboring pipe.
The filling process follows breadth-first expansion from the source.

Win and Loss Conditions
The player wins if there is a connected path from the source to the sink.
Path checking starts from the source by moving once in the source’s pointing direction. From each pipe, traversal continues through that pipe’s connection directions. The path does not require pipes to already be filled. Reaching the sink means the game is won.
The player loses when a water-flow update fills no new pipes. Loss is checked only after the initial delay has ended and water has actually started advancing.

Pipe Queue
The pipe queue stores upcoming pipes. The player always interacts with the pipe at the front.
When a pipe is consumed, the queue is automatically refilled up to a fixed maximum length using randomly generated pipe shapes.
Undo places the restored pipe back at the front of the queue.

Delay Bar
The delay bar starts with an initial value and decreases once per round.
While the value is still positive, water has not begun flowing. Once the countdown passes zero, the corresponding positive distance indicates how far water should expand from the source.

Cell Stack
The placement history records successfully placed cells in order.
Undo uses the most recent placement. The undo counter represents the number of successful undo actions, not the current size of the placement history.

External / Tool Classes
Pa19Helper is a handwritten helper and assembly class in the pa19 package. It is responsible for constructing core game objects from provided inputs, wiring together the map, pipe queue, delay bar, and placement history. It also centralizes basic parsing and direction utility behavior.
Deserializer is responsible for reading game input from a file and producing runtime game objects. It validates that the input file exists, reads the board size, delay value, map lines, and optional default pipes. If the input ends unexpectedly or an I/O error occurs, it returns no game object and logs the error.
When parsing map text, border cells are treated as sink-side termination candidates, while inner termination symbols are treated as source-side candidates.
Deserializer ignores blank lines and comment lines beginning with # when reading meaningful input.
PipePatterns is a final utility-style constant holder for all rendering characters. It contains the wall character and grouped constants for filled and unfilled arrows and pipe shapes. Rendering logic should rely on these constants instead of hardcoded characters.
StringUtils is a lightweight utility-style class for string helpers and should not be instantiated.
```

# Operation Specifications
PipeQueue::peek
Summary: Returns the pipe at the front of the queue without removing it.
Algorithm: Return the first element of the pipeQueue list.
Related Features: pipeQueue
Related Classes: Pipe
Input: None
Output: Pipe - the front pipe of the queue
Pre-condition: pipeQueue is not empty
Post-condition: The queue remains unchanged.

PipeQueue::generateNewPipe
Summary: Creates a new random pipe with a random shape.
Algorithm:
  1. Randomly select a PipeShape from the enum values
  2. Create a new Pipe with that shape and filled = false
  3. Return the new pipe
Related Features: None
Related Classes: Pipe, PipeShape
Input: None
Output: Pipe - a new randomly generated pipe
Pre-condition: None
Post-condition: Returns a new unfilled pipe with a random shape.

PipeQueue::undo
Summary: Restores a pipe to the front of the queue (used during undo operations).
Algorithm: Insert the given pipe at the beginning (index 0) of the pipeQueue list.
Related Features: pipeQueue
Related Classes: Pipe
Input: pipe : Pipe - the pipe to restore to the front
Output: void
Pre-condition: pipe is not null
Post-condition: The pipe is added to the front of the queue; queue size increases by 1.

PipeQueue::consume
Summary: Removes the front pipe from the queue and refills if necessary.
Algorithm:
  1. Remove the first element from pipeQueue list
  2. If the queue size is less than maxGenLength, call generateNewPipe() repeatedly until queue is full
Related Features: pipeQueue, maxGenLength
Related Classes: Pipe
Input: None
Output: void
Pre-condition: pipeQueue is not empty
Post-condition: The front pipe is removed; queue is refilled to maxGenLength if needed.

# Operation Specifications
PipeQueue::peek
Summary: Returns the pipe at the front of the queue without removing it.
Algorithm: Return the first element of the pipeQueue list.
Related Features: pipeQueue
Related Classes: Pipe
Input: None
Output: Pipe - the front pipe of the queue
Pre-condition: pipeQueue is not empty
Post-condition: The queue remains unchanged.

PipeQueue::generateNewPipe
Summary: Creates a new random pipe with a random shape.
Algorithm:
  1. Randomly select a PipeShape from the enum values
  2. Create a new Pipe with that shape and filled = false
  3. Return the new pipe
Related Features: None
Related Classes: Pipe, PipeShape
Input: None
Output: Pipe - a new randomly generated pipe
Pre-condition: None
Post-condition: Returns a new unfilled pipe with a random shape.

PipeQueue::undo
Summary: Restores a pipe to the front of the queue (used during undo operations).
Algorithm: Insert the given pipe at the beginning (index 0) of the pipeQueue list.
Related Features: pipeQueue
Related Classes: Pipe
Input: pipe : Pipe - the pipe to restore to the front
Output: void
Pre-condition: pipe is not null
Post-condition: The pipe is added to the front of the queue; queue size increases by 1.

PipeQueue::consume
Summary: Removes the front pipe from the queue and refills if necessary.
Algorithm:
  1. Remove the first element from pipeQueue list
  2. If the queue size is less than maxGenLength, call generateNewPipe() repeatedly until queue is full
Related Features: pipeQueue, maxGenLength
Related Classes: Pipe
Input: None
Output: void
Pre-condition: pipeQueue is not empty
Post-condition: The front pipe is removed; queue is refilled to maxGenLength if needed.

public boolean placePipe(final int row, final char col) {
    int colIndex = col - 'A' + 1;
    Pipe pipe = getPipeQueue().peek();
    boolean success = getMap().tryPlacePipe(row, colIndex, pipe);
    if (success) {
        getPipeQueue().consume();
        FillableCell cell = Pa19Factory.eINSTANCE.createFillableCell();
        Coordinate coord = Pa19Factory.eINSTANCE.createCoordinate();
        coord.setRow(row);
        coord.setCol(colIndex);
        cell.setCoord(coord);

}

public void skipPipe() {
    getPipeQueue().consume();
    setNumOfSteps(getNumOfSteps() + 1);

public boolean undoStep() {
    FillableCell cell = getCellStack().pop();
    if (cell == null) return false;
    Coordinate coord = cell.getCoord();
    getMap().undo(coord);
    getPipeQueue().undo(cell.getPipe());
    setNumOfSteps(getNumOfSteps() + 1);
    return true;
}

   * Summary: Attempts to place the current pipe from the queue onto the board at the specified coordinates.

   *   2. Get the current pipe from pipeQueue.peek()

   * Summary: Fills pipes with water up to the specified distance from the source using BFS.

  public void fillTiles(final int distance)
  {
    // 1. If this is the first fill (distance == 1), call fillBeginTile() to mark source as filled
    if (distance == 1) {
      fillBeginTile();
    }
    
    // 7. Update prevFilledTiles to the number of filled tiles before this fill operation
    setPrevFilledTiles(getFilledTiles().size());
    
    // Get the source cell
    TerminationCell source = getSourceCell();
    if (source == null) {
      return;
    }
    
    // 2. Perform BFS from the source, expanding outward by distance steps
    Pa19Helper helper = Pa19Factory.eINSTANCE.createPa19Helper();
    
    // BFS queue stores coordinates to visit
    java.util.Queue<Coordinate> queue = new java.util.LinkedList<>();
    java.util.Set<Coordinate> visited = new java.util.HashSet<>();
    
    Coordinate sourceCoord = source.getCoord();
    queue.add(sourceCoord);
    visited.add(sourceCoord);
    
    int steps = 0;
    
    while (!queue.isEmpty() && steps < distance) {
      int levelSize = queue.size();
      for (int i = 0; i < levelSize; i++) {
        Coordinate current = queue.poll();
        Cell currentCell = getCell()[current.getRow()][current.getCol()];
        
        if (currentCell instanceof TerminationCell) {
          TerminationCell termCell = (TerminationCell) currentCell;
          if (termCell == source) {
            // From source, water flows in the pointingTo direction
            Direction dir = source.getPointingTo();
            Coordinate offset = helper.getOffset(dir);
            Coordinate neighborCoord = current.add(offset);
            // Check bounds
            if (neighborCoord.getRow() >= 0 && neighborCoord.getRow() < getRows() && 
                neighborCoord.getCol() >= 0 && neighborCoord.getCol() < getCols() &&
                !visited.contains(neighborCoord)) {
              Cell neighborCell = getCell()[neighborCoord.getRow()][neighborCoord.getCol()];
              if (neighborCell instanceof FillableCell) {
                FillableCell fillableNeighbor = (FillableCell) neighborCell;
                Pipe neighborPipe = fillableNeighbor.getPipe();
                if (neighborPipe != null) {
                  // Check if neighbor connects back (has opposite direction)
                  Direction opposite = helper.getOpposite(dir);
                  if (neighborPipe.getConnections().contains(opposite)) {
                    neighborPipe.setFilled(true);
                    Coordinate filledCoord = Pa19Factory.eINSTANCE.createCoordinate();
                    filledCoord.setRow(neighborCoord.getRow());
                    filledCoord.setCol(neighborCoord.getCol());
                    getFilledTiles().add(filledCoord);
                    queue.add(neighborCoord);
                    visited.add(neighborCoord);
                  }
                }
              }
            }
          }
        } else if (currentCell instanceof FillableCell) {
          FillableCell fillableCell = (FillableCell) currentCell;
          Pipe pipe = fillableCell.getPipe();
          if (pipe != null && pipe.isFilled()) {
            // Explore all connection directions
            for (Direction dir : pipe.getConnections()) {
              Coordinate offset = helper.getOffset(dir);
              Coordinate neighborCoord = current.add(offset);
              if (neighborCoord.getRow() >= 0 && neighborCoord.getRow() < getRows() && 
                  neighborCoord.getCol() >= 0 && neighborCoord.getCol() < getCols() &&
                  !visited.contains(neighborCoord)) {
                Cell neighborCell = getCell()[neighborCoord.getRow()][neighborCoord.getCol()];
                if (neighborCell instanceof FillableCell) {
                  FillableCell fillableNeighbor = (FillableCell) neighborCell;
                  Pipe neighborPipe = fillableNeighbor.getPipe();
                  if (neighborPipe != null) {
                    // Check if neighbor connects back
                    Direction opposite = helper.getOpposite(dir);
                    if (neighborPipe.getConnections().contains(opposite)) {
                      neighborPipe.setFilled(true);
                      Coordinate filledCoord = Pa19Factory.eINSTANCE.createCoordinate();
                      filledCoord.setRow(neighborCoord.getRow());
                      filledCoord.setCol(neighborCoord.getCol());
                      getFilledTiles().add(filledCoord);
                      queue.add(neighborCoord);
                      visited.add(neighborCoord);
                    }
                  }
                } else if (neighborCell instanceof TerminationCell) {
                  // Check if termination cell's pointingTo matches
                  TerminationCell termNeighbor = (TerminationCell) neighborCell;
                  Direction opposite = helper.getOpposite(dir);
                  if (termNeighbor.getPointingTo() == opposite) {
                    termNeighbor.setFilled(true);
                    queue.add(neighborCoord);
                    visited.add(neighborCoord);
                  }
                }
              }
            }
          }
        }
      }
      steps++;
    }
    
    // 6. Update prevFilledDistance to current distance
    setPrevFilledDistance(distance);

      fillBeginTile();
    }
    
    // 7. Update prevFilledTiles to the number of filled tiles before this fill operation
    setPrevFilledTiles(getFilledTiles().size());
    
    TerminationCell source = getSourceCell();
    if (source == null || source.getCoord() == null) {
      return;
    }
    
    Pa19Helper helper = Pa19Factory.eINSTANCE.createPa19Helper();
    
    // BFS
    java.util.Queue<Coordinate> queue = new java.util.LinkedList<>();
    java.util.Set<Coordinate> visited = new java.util.HashSet<>();
    
    Coordinate sourceCoord = source.getCoord();
    queue.add(sourceCoord);
    visited.add(sourceCoord);
    
    int currentDistance = 0;
    
    while (!queue.isEmpty() && currentDistance < distance) {
      int levelSize = queue.size();
      for (int i = 0; i < levelSize; i++) {
        Coordinate currentCoord = queue.poll();
        Cell currentCell = getCell()[currentCoord.getRow()][currentCoord.getCol()];
        
        // Determine which directions to explore from this cell
        java.util.List<Direction> exploreDirections = new java.util.ArrayList<>();
        
        if (currentCell instanceof TerminationCell) {
          TerminationCell termCell = (TerminationCell) currentCell;
          if (termCell == source) {
            // From source, water flows in the pointingTo direction
            exploreDirections.add(source.getPointingTo());
          }
          // For sink or other termination cells, we might also explore
          // But for now, just handle source
        } else if (currentCell instanceof FillableCell) {
          FillableCell fillableCell = (FillableCell) currentCell;
          Pipe pipe = fillableCell.getPipe();
          if (pipe != null && pipe.isFilled()) {
            exploreDirections.addAll(pipe.getConnections());
          }
        }
        
        // Explore each direction
        for (Direction dir : exploreDirections) {
          Coordinate offset = helper.getOffset(dir);
          Coordinate neighborCoord = currentCoord.add(offset);
          int nRow = neighborCoord.getRow();
          int nCol = neighborCoord.getCol();
          
          // Check bounds
          if (nRow < 0 || nRow >= getRows() || nCol < 0 || nCol >= getCols()) {
            continue;
          }
          if (visited.contains(neighborCoord)) {
            continue;
          }
          
          Cell neighborCell = getCell()[nRow][nCol];
          Direction opposite = helper.getOpposite(dir);
          
          if (neighborCell instanceof FillableCell) {
            FillableCell fillableNeighbor = (FillableCell) neighborCell;
            Pipe neighborPipe = fillableNeighbor.getPipe();
            if (neighborPipe != null && neighborPipe.getConnections().contains(opposite)) {
              // Connection is valid
              neighborPipe.setFilled(true);
              // Create a new Coordinate for filledTiles
              Coordinate filledCoord = Pa19Factory.eINSTANCE.createCoordinate();
              filledCoord.setRow(nRow);
              filledCoord.setCol(nCol);
              getFilledTiles().add(filledCoord);
              queue.add(neighborCoord);
              visited.add(neighborCoord);
            }
          } else if (neighborCell instanceof TerminationCell) {
            TerminationCell termNeighbor = (TerminationCell) neighborCell;
            if (termNeighbor.getPointingTo() == opposite) {
              termNeighbor.setFilled(true);
              queue.add(neighborCoord);
              visited.add(neighborCoord);
            }
          }
        }
      }
      currentDistance++;
    }
    
    // 6. Update prevFilledDistance to current distance
    setPrevFilledDistance(distance);
  }
  public boolean checkPath()
  {
    // BFS from sourceCell to sinkCell
    TerminationCell source = getSourceCell();
    TerminationCell sink = getSinkCell();
    if (source == null || sink == null || source.getCoord() == null || sink.getCoord() == null) {
      return false;
    }
    
    Pa19Helper helper = Pa19Factory.eINSTANCE.createPa19Helper();
    
    java.util.Queue<Coordinate> queue = new java.util.LinkedList<>();
    java.util.Set<Coordinate> visited = new java.util.HashSet<>();
    
    Coordinate sourceCoord = source.getCoord();
    queue.add(sourceCoord);
    visited.add(sourceCoord);
    
    while (!queue.isEmpty()) {
      Coordinate currentCoord = queue.poll();
      Cell currentCell = getCell()[currentCoord.getRow()][currentCoord.getCol()];
      
      // Check if we reached the sink
      if (currentCell == sink) {
        return true;
      }
      
      // Determine which directions to explore
      java.util.List<Direction> exploreDirections = new java.util.ArrayList<>();
      
      if (currentCell instanceof TerminationCell) {
        TerminationCell termCell = (TerminationCell) currentCell;
        if (termCell == source) {
          exploreDirections.add(source.getPointingTo());
        }
        // For other termination cells (like sink), don't explore further
      } else if (currentCell instanceof FillableCell) {
        FillableCell fillableCell = (FillableCell) currentCell;
        Pipe pipe = fillableCell.getPipe();
        if (pipe != null) {
          exploreDirections.addAll(pipe.getConnections());
        }
      }
      
      for (Direction dir : exploreDirections) {
        Coordinate offset = helper.getOffset(dir);
        Coordinate neighborCoord = currentCoord.add(offset);
        int nRow = neighborCoord.getRow();
        int nCol = neighborCoord.getCol();
        
        if (nRow < 0 || nRow >= getRows() || nCol < 0 || nCol >= getCols()) {
          continue;
        }
        if (visited.contains(neighborCoord)) {
          continue;
        }
        
        Cell neighborCell = getCell()[nRow][nCol];
        Direction opposite = helper.getOpposite(dir);
        
        if (neighborCell instanceof FillableCell) {
          FillableCell fillableNeighbor = (FillableCell) neighborCell;
          Pipe neighborPipe = fillableNeighbor.getPipe();
          if (neighborPipe != null && neighborPipe.getConnections().contains(opposite)) {
            queue.add(neighborCoord);
            visited.add(neighborCoord);
          }
        } else if (neighborCell instanceof TerminationCell) {
          TerminationCell termNeighbor = (TerminationCell) neighborCell;
          if (termNeighbor.getPointingTo() == opposite) {
            queue.add(neighborCoord);
            visited.add(neighborCoord);
          }
        }
      }
    }
    
    return false;
  }
  public boolean hasLost()
  {
    // 1. If prevFilledDistance is null, return false (water has not started flowing yet)
    if (getPrevFilledDistance() == null) {
      return false;
    }
    // 2. Compare current filledTiles size with prevFilledTiles
    // 3. If no new tiles were filled (size unchanged), return true
    if (getFilledTiles().size() == getPrevFilledTiles()) {
      return true;
    }
    // 4. Otherwise return false
    return false;
  }
protected int prevFilledTiles = PREV_FILLED_TILES_EDEFAULT;
protected Integer prevFilledDistance = PREV_FILLED_DISTANCE_EDEFAULT;

  /**
   * <!-- begin-user-doc -->

   * <!-- begin-model-doc -->
   * Summary: Attempts to place a pipe at the specified coordinate on the map.
   * Algorithm:
   *   1. Check if coordinate is within playable area (1..rows-2, 1..cols-2)
   *   2. Check if the cell at that coordinate is a FillableCell
   *   3. Check if the cell does not already contain a pipe
   *   4. If all conditions met, set the cell's pipe to the given pipe and return true
   *   5. Otherwise return false
   * Related Features: cell array, rows, cols
   * Related Classes: Coordinate, FillableCell, Pipe
   * Input: row : int - the row coordinate (1-based internal index), col : int - the column coordinate (1-based internal index), pipe : Pipe - the pipe to place
   * Output: boolean - true if placement was successful, false otherwise
   * Pre-condition: row is between 1 and rows-2 inclusive, col is between 1 and cols-2 inclusive
   * Post-condition: If successful, the specified cell now contains the given pipe.
   * <!-- end-model-doc -->
   * @model annotation="http://www.ustb.edu.cn/sei/mde/EnhancedCodeGen generated='true'"
   * @generated
   */

public boolean tryPlacePipe(final int row, final int col, final Pipe pipe)
{
    // Check if coordinate is within playable area (1..rows-2, 1..cols-2)
    if (row < 1 || row > getRows() - 2 || col < 1 || col > getCols() - 2) {
        return false;
    }
    // Check if the cell at that coordinate is a FillableCell
    Cell targetCell = getCell()[row][col];
    if (!(targetCell instanceof FillableCell)) {
        return false;
    }
    FillableCell fillableCell = (FillableCell) targetCell;
    // Check if the cell does not already contain a pipe
    if (fillableCell.getPipe() != null) {
        return false;
    }
    // Set the cell's pipe to the given pipe and return true
    fillableCell.setPipe(pipe);
    return true;
}
public void undo(final Coordinate coord)
{

    if (targetCell instanceof FillableCell) {
        FillableCell fillableCell = (FillableCell) targetCell;
        if (fillableCell.getPipe() != null) {
            fillableCell.setPipe(null);
        }
    }
}
public void fillTiles(final int distance)
{
    // Record the number of filled tiles before this operation
    int prevCount = getFilledTiles().size();
    setPrevFilledTiles(prevCount);
    
    // If this is the first fill, mark source as filled
    if (distance == 1) {
        fillBeginTile();
    }
    
    // BFS from source
    TerminationCell source = getSourceCell();
    if (source == null) return;
    
    Coordinate sourceCoord = source.getCoord();
    if (sourceCoord == null) return;
    
    // Track visited positions
    boolean[][] visited = new boolean[getRows()][getCols()];
    Queue<Coordinate> queue = new LinkedList<>();
    Queue<Integer> distQueue = new LinkedList<>();
    
    queue.add(sourceCoord);
    distQueue.add(0);
    visited[sourceCoord.getRow()][sourceCoord.getCol()] = true;
    
    while (!queue.isEmpty()) {
        Coordinate current = queue.poll();
        int currentDist = distQueue.poll();
        
        if (currentDist >= distance) continue;
        
        Cell cell = getCell()[current.getRow()][current.getCol()];
        
        // Determine the directions to explore
        EList<Direction> directions = new BasicEList<>();
        
        if (cell instanceof TerminationCell) {
            TerminationCell tc = (TerminationCell) cell;
            if (tc.isFilled()) {
                directions.add(tc.getPointingTo());
            }
        } else if (cell instanceof FillableCell) {
            FillableCell fc = (FillableCell) cell;
            Pipe pipe = fc.getPipe();
            if (pipe != null && pipe.isFilled()) {
                directions = pipe.getConnections();
            }
        }
        
        for (Direction dir : directions) {
            int newRow = current.getRow();
            int newCol = current.getCol();
            
            if (dir == Direction.UP) newRow--;
            else if (dir == Direction.DOWN) newRow++;
            else if (dir == Direction.LEFT) newCol--;
            else if (dir == Direction.RIGHT) newCol++;
            
            if (newRow < 0 || newRow >= getRows() || newCol < 0 || newCol >= getCols()) continue;
            if (visited[newRow][newCol]) continue;
            
            Cell neighborCell = getCell()[newRow][newCol];
            Direction oppositeDir = getOpposite(dir);
            
            boolean canFlow = false;
            if (neighborCell instanceof FillableCell) {
                FillableCell nfc = (FillableCell) neighborCell;
                Pipe neighborPipe = nfc.getPipe();
                if (neighborPipe != null) {
                    if (neighborPipe.getConnections().contains(oppositeDir)) {
                        canFlow = true;
                        neighborPipe.setFilled(true);
                    }
                }
            } else if (neighborCell instanceof TerminationCell) {
                TerminationCell ntc = (TerminationCell) neighborCell;
                if (ntc.getPointingTo() == oppositeDir) {
                    canFlow = true;
                    ntc.setFilled(true);
                }
            }
            
            if (canFlow) {
                Coordinate neighborCoord = neighborCell.getCoord();
                visited[newRow][newCol] = true;
                queue.add(neighborCoord);
                distQueue.add(currentDist + 1);
            }
        }
    }
    
    // Update filledTiles list
    getFilledTiles().clear();
    for (int r = 0; r < getRows(); r++) {
        for (int c = 0; c < getCols(); c++) {
            Cell cell = getCell()[r][c];
            if (cell instanceof FillableCell) {
                FillableCell fc = (FillableCell) cell;
                if (fc.getPipe() != null && fc.getPipe().isFilled()) {
                    getFilledTiles().add(fc.getCoord());
                }
            } else if (cell instanceof TerminationCell) {
                TerminationCell tc = (TerminationCell) cell;
                if (tc.isFilled()) {
                    getFilledTiles().add(tc.getCoord());
                }
            }
        }
    }
    
    setPrevFilledDistance(distance);
}
public boolean checkPath()
{
    TerminationCell source = getSourceCell();
    TerminationCell sink = getSinkCell();
    if (source == null || sink == null) return false;
    
    Coordinate sourceCoord = source.getCoord();
    if (sourceCoord == null) return false;
    
    boolean[][] visited = new boolean[getRows()][getCols()];
    Queue<Coordinate> queue = new LinkedList<>();
    
    queue.add(sourceCoord);
    visited[sourceCoord.getRow()][sourceCoord.getCol()] = true;
    
    while (!queue.isEmpty()) {
        Coordinate current = queue.poll();
        
        Cell cell = getCell()[current.getRow()][current.getCol()];
        
        // If we reached the sink, return true
        if (cell == sink) return true;
        
        // Get directions to explore
        EList<Direction> directions = new BasicEList<>();
        
        if (cell instanceof TerminationCell) {
            TerminationCell tc = (TerminationCell) cell;
            if (tc.isFilled()) {
                directions.add(tc.getPointingTo());
            }
        } else if (cell instanceof FillableCell) {
            FillableCell fc = (FillableCell) cell;
            Pipe pipe = fc.getPipe();
            if (pipe != null && pipe.isFilled()) {
                directions = pipe.getConnections();
            }
        }
        
        for (Direction dir : directions) {
            int newRow = current.getRow();
            int newCol = current.getCol();
            
            if (dir == Direction.UP) newRow--;
            else if (dir == Direction.DOWN) newRow++;
            else if (dir == Direction.LEFT) newCol--;
            else if (dir == Direction.RIGHT) newCol++;
            
            if (newRow < 0 || newRow >= getRows() || newCol < 0 || newCol >= getCols()) continue;
            if (visited[newRow][newCol]) continue;
            
            Cell neighborCell = getCell()[newRow][newCol];
            Direction oppositeDir = getOpposite(dir);
            
            boolean canPass = false;
            if (neighborCell instanceof FillableCell) {
                FillableCell nfc = (FillableCell) neighborCell;
                Pipe neighborPipe = nfc.getPipe();
                if (neighborPipe != null && neighborPipe.getConnections().contains(oppositeDir)) {
                    canPass = true;
                }
            } else if (neighborCell instanceof TerminationCell) {
                TerminationCell ntc = (TerminationCell) neighborCell;
                if (ntc.getPointingTo() == oppositeDir) {
                    canPass = true;
                }
            }
            
            if (canPass) {
                visited[newRow][newCol] = true;
                queue.add(neighborCell.getCoord());
            }
        }
    }
    
    return false;
}
public void fillTiles(final int distance)
{
    // Record the number of filled tiles before this operation
    setPrevFilledTiles(getFilledTiles().size());
    
    // If this is the first fill, mark source as filled
    if (distance == 1) {
        fillBeginTile();
    }
    
    TerminationCell source = getSourceCell();
    if (source == null) return;
    
    Coordinate sourceCoord = source.getCoord();
    if (sourceCoord == null) return;
    
    boolean[][] visited = new boolean[getRows()][getCols()];
    Queue<Coordinate> queue = new LinkedList<>();
    Queue<Integer> distQueue = new LinkedList<>();
    
    visited[sourceCoord.getRow()][sourceCoord.getCol()] = true;
    queue.add(sourceCoord);
    distQueue.add(0);
    
    while (!queue.isEmpty()) {
        Coordinate current = queue.poll();
        int currentDist = distQueue.poll();
        
        if (currentDist >= distance) continue;
        
        Cell cell = getCell()[current.getRow()][current.getCol()];
        EList<Direction> directions = new BasicEList<Direction>();
        
        if (cell instanceof TerminationCell) {
            TerminationCell tc = (TerminationCell) cell;
            if (tc.isFilled()) {
                directions.add(tc.getPointingTo());
            }
        } else if (cell instanceof FillableCell) {
            FillableCell fc = (FillableCell) cell;
            Pipe pipe = fc.getPipe();
            if (pipe != null && pipe.isFilled()) {
                directions.addAll(pipe.getConnections());
            }
        }
        
        for (Direction dir : directions) {
            int newRow = current.getRow();
            int newCol = current.getCol();
            
            switch (dir) {
                case UP: newRow--; break;
                case DOWN: newRow++; break;
                case LEFT: newCol--; break;
                case RIGHT: newCol++; break;
            }
            
            if (newRow < 0 || newRow >= getRows() || newCol < 0 || newCol >= getCols()) continue;
            if (visited[newRow][newCol]) continue;
            
            Cell neighborCell = getCell()[newRow][newCol];
            Direction oppositeDir;
            switch (dir) {
                case UP: oppositeDir = Direction.DOWN; break;
                case DOWN: oppositeDir = Direction.UP; break;
                case LEFT: oppositeDir = Direction.RIGHT; break;
                default: oppositeDir = Direction.LEFT; break;
            }
            
            boolean canFlow = false;
            if (neighborCell instanceof FillableCell) {
                FillableCell nfc = (FillableCell) neighborCell;
                Pipe neighborPipe = nfc.getPipe();
                if (neighborPipe != null && neighborPipe.getConnections().contains(oppositeDir)) {
                    canFlow = true;
                    neighborPipe.setFilled(true);
                }
            } else if (neighborCell instanceof TerminationCell) {
                TerminationCell ntc = (TerminationCell) neighborCell;
                if (ntc.getPointingTo() == oppositeDir) {
                    canFlow = true;
                    ntc.setFilled(true);
                }
            }
            
            if (canFlow) {
                visited[newRow][newCol] = true;
                queue.add(neighborCell.getCoord());
                distQueue.add(currentDist + 1);
            }
        }
    }
    
    // Update filledTiles list
    getFilledTiles().clear();
    for (int r = 0; r < getRows(); r++) {
        for (int c = 0; c < getCols(); c++) {
            Cell cell = getCell()[r][c];
            if (cell instanceof FillableCell) {
                FillableCell fc = (FillableCell) cell;
                if (fc.getPipe() != null && fc.getPipe().isFilled()) {
                    getFilledTiles().add(fc.getCoord());
                }
            } else if (cell instanceof TerminationCell) {
                TerminationCell tc = (TerminationCell) cell;
                if (tc.isFilled()) {
                    getFilledTiles().add(tc.getCoord());
                }
            }
        }
    }
    
    setPrevFilledDistance(distance);
}
